articleTitle: Modeling and Tuning of Electric Drive Train Capturing Horizontal Mode Resonance
abstract: In this first paper of a two-part series, an online tuneable approximate system model (ASM) is proposed for an electric drive train. This ASM approximates the horizontal mode resonance (HMR) response of an electric drive train to an applied reactive torque. Reactive torque is a net zero torque ripple added on top of the reference torque oscillating at a certain frequency. This reactive torque uses the inertia of the rotor to generate reactive torque on the inner surface of the stator bore counteracting the forces of HMR and consequently attenuating the vibrations. Furthermore, the ASM is tuned online independent of the operating point of the electric drive. This tuning method and the ASM are experimentally evaluated in the lab and are an important step towards the development of active horizontal vibration control (AHVC) of HMR.

articleTitle: Optimal Damping of Horizontal Mode Resonance of an Electric Drive Train Using Reactive Torque
abstract: In this second paper of a two-part series, an adaptive closed-loop (ACL) active horizontal vibration control (AHVC) for damping horizontal mode resonance (HMR) is proposed. The ACL control injects reactive torque in addition to the torque required by the speed controller of an electric drive train. This reactive torque uses the inertia of the rotor to generate reactive torque on the inner surface of the stator bore counteracting the forces of HMR and consequently attenuating the vibrations. Furthermore, the phase of the injected reactive torque is controlled in such a way that a minimum amplitude of reactive torque is injected for a given operating condition. This reduces additional losses incurred due to ACL control. The proposed method and optimization technique is experimentally verified in a laboratory environment and the results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis and Optimization of Iron Nitride Enabled 800-V PM-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Traction Motor with Varying Poles for Extended Operating Speed Range
abstract: This paper compares and analyzes 8-pole and 6-pole U-shaped Permanent Magnet-assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor (PMaSynRM) designs with double-layer and triple-layer topologies for 800-V traction applications with extended operating speed range (EOSR). Multi-objective optimizer selects the optimal designs satisfying the defined objectives and constraints by iteratively updating the generation of candidate designs. The proposed designs use the combination of rare-earth permanent magnets (Dy-free NdFeB) and Iron Nitride (FeN) rare-earth free permanent magnets to achieve comparable performance to the baseline at EOSR. Due to the presence of demagnetization prone magnets in the rotor, the optimal designs are evaluated for global and local demagnetization risk at extreme temperatures of −20°C and 150°C. The practical feasibility of the proposed designs for EOSR traction application is validated through mechanical stress analysis. With the 800-V system, performance metrics of the designs including magnet cost assessment are presented and compared with the baseline design. Comparable performance can be inferred from the results.

articleTitle: On the Utilization of Radial Vibration Transient Signals for Induction Machine Misalignment Diagnosis
abstract: Vibration measurement is widely employed for di-agnosing malfunctions in rotating machinery including electrical machines. While steady-state vibration signals are extensively studied for diagnosing mechanical defects such as misalignment, load unbalances, and bearing defects, transient analysis of vibration signals remains a research gap. In particular, vibration mea-surement in the housing of electrical machines offers insights into both mechanical and electromagnetic signatures. This manuscript aims to explore the potential of transient radial vibration analysis to enhance the reliability of misalignment diagnosis. To this aim, a squirrel cage induction machine is utilized as a case study, while transient vibrations under slip swinging conditions such as soft-started and directly-fed start-ups are analysed. The analysis of slowly varying transient vibrations reveals severe misalignment indications that cannot be adequately addressed using steady- state current or vibration spectra. This is particularly interesting for machines with intermittent duty and frequent starts (e.g., pumps, fans, etc.).

articleTitle: Investigation of Demagnetization in Halbach Machines
abstract: Even under open-circuit, Halbach machines suffer from an irreversible demagnetization issue. In this paper, the relationship between Halbach segment number per pole and electromagnetic performance reduction caused by demagnetization under both open-circuit and on-load is analyzed. The influence of demagnetization factors, including current, airgap length, permanent magnet (PM) thickness, and PM angular width, is investigated. It is found that Halbach machines with more segments per pole, larger airgap length, thicker PM have higher demagnetization withstand capability. However, when the number of segments per pole is greater than 3, the improvement in demagnetization withstand capability is negligible. Meanwhile, compared with the Halbach machines with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100{{\% }}$</tex> PM width ratio, a gap between adjacent PMs can mitigate the influence of demagnetization.

articleTitle: Verification of Load Angle Characteristics of a Novel Counter-Rotating Twin Harmonic PM Machine Using Locked-Rotor Measurements
abstract: Recently, three-port machines having one set of electrical connections and two mechanical shafts have received some academic interest due to the possibilities they offer. Using specific magnetic field harmonics, these two shafts can be made to counter-rotate. Counter-rotating turbines can, for example, be used in applications such as low-pressure hydropower pumps, in aviation propulsion using counter-rotating propellers, or similarly in marine propulsion, where they can improve the system efficiency compared to one turbine. Additionally, using a three-port machine can improve the economical feasibility of such applications by only requiring one stator and one power electronic converter compared to using two traditional two-port machines. In this paper, a 2 kW three-port machine with counter-rotating shafts is presented. First, its load angle characteristics are described using analytical equations only. Then, FEA models of the three-port machine are presented, and a numerical locked rotor test is performed to describe the load angle characteristics. Finally, measurements from locked rotor tests on a lab setup are presented. It can be concluded that these three methods produce similar results, verifying that the technology demonstrator can indeed be accurately modeled by two 2D numerical models.

articleTitle: An Investigation of the Impedance Spectroscopy Suitability for Traction Motor Windings Insulation Health Assessment
abstract: Stator inter-turn faults are among the most critical faults in electrical machines due to their fast evolution into a catastrophic breakdown. This type of fault is especially critical for electric vehicle applications because it may compromise human safety. This fault is directly linked to the reliability of the electric insulating system. In this paper, the authors investigate the impact of accelerated ageing on the dielectric properties of traction motor windings insulation. The aim is to understand if the impedance spectroscopy is reliable for assessing the health of the insulation and lead to appropriate diagnostic outcomes. The results indicate that the impedance spectroscopy should be used with caution and secondary analysis and criteria need to be developed.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Hybrid Excitation Flux Switching Generator for Micro Hydroelectric System
abstract: This paper presents a design study of a hybrid excitation flux switching generator (HEFSG) for micro hydroelectric power generation system installed in water supply facilities as a kind of renewable energy systems. Interior permanent magnet synchronous generators installed in current micro hydroelectric power generation systems may lack the power generation range in the low-speed and high-torque range, depending on the location and conditions where the systems are installed, resulting in the loss of power generation opportunities. In this research and development, HEFSG as a kind of variable flux machines is applied with the aim of realizing a micro hydroelectric power generation system that can be used in various occasions and conditions. Application-oriented optimum design of HEFSG under given design constraint and specifications using finite element electromagnetic analysis is conducted. The design results show that the designed HEFSG can expand the high torque operating range in low-speed region that meets for the target requirement.

articleTitle: A Novel Segmented-Rotor Hybrid-Excited Synchronous Motor for Electric Vehicle Application
abstract: Permanent magnet AC (PMAC) motors are widely utilised in electric vehicles due to their high efficiency and power density. However, the major limitations of these motors are complex field weakening operation, limited constant power speed region, and reliance on costly and environmentally unfriendly rare-earth permanent magnets (PMs). In contrast, electrically excited synchronous motors offer solutions to these limitations. But their power density and efficiency are lower compared to PMAC motors. Hence, a motor combining both PMs and DC winding presents a promising solution. This paper introduces a novel segmented-rotor synchronous motor designed for electric vehicle application. It has permanent magnets and DC excited winding for field excitation. This machine is first of its kind in which path of magnet flux and DC field flux in rotor are separate and hence they can be considered parallel. In addition each rotor pole structure is hybridised. This results in segmented rotor structure, thus enhancing the power density. Flux distortion due to high current-loading is addressed by introducing a novel asymmetric pole-offset concept. Simulation studies using finite element method (FEM) are carried out to validate the proposed design and results are presented.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis on Different Deep Neural Network Models for Magnetic Hysteresis with Distorted Excitation Waveforms
abstract: Hereby presented is a comparative analysis of different deep neural network models aimed at simulating magnetic hysteresis under distorted excitation waveforms. Specifically feed forward neural networks (FFNN), recurrent neural networks (RNN), and nonlinear autoregressive exogenous (NARX) networks have been chosen to be evaluated due to their distinct capabilities in capturing non-linear relationships and temporal dependencies, making them suitable for the complex and dynamic nature of hysteresis phenomena. Utilizing the Preisach model to generate training and validation data, the study highlights the ability of neural networks to model complex magnetic behaviors. The final results indicate that FFNNs achieve the highest accuracy with an average error of 3%, outperforming RNNs and NARX networks. The findings underscore the suitability of FFNNs for applications where training datasets are limited or computational resources are constrained.

articleTitle: Comparative Behavior Study of Various PMSM Topologies Under Demagnetization Conditions
abstract: To improve our understanding of permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSM) fault behavior caused by local demagnetization faults, we propose in this article to study the influence of the machine topology on its electromagnetic harmonic behavior. Ultimately, this comparative study aims to identify the characteristic frequencies of this fault that must be monitored in order to detect it when the demagnetization rate is still very low. For this purpose, finite element modeling was used to analyze the impact of rotor fault position, and rotor topology (surface-mounted magnet rotor, interior magnet rotor, flux-concentrated rotor) on the characteristic frequency signatures of the fault. The effect of stator winding type (integer-slot/concentrated/distributed winding, single/double-layer winding) was also investigated. The results showed that the ratio of the number of slots to the number of pole pairs is representative of the characteristic frequencies of a local demagnetization fault. Meanwhile, the rotor topology influences the amplitude variation of these signatures, which can be relatively significant depending on the machine robustness to such a fault. Finally, we also observe that frequency analysis can be used to locate the faulty pole in the rotor.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis of an IPM Machine for Charging Operations in Electric Vehicles
abstract: In electric vehicles (EVs), using integrated chargers and onboard chargers is greatly economical because it re-utilizes vehicular devices and saves space when allocating the battery pack. While designing a DC-DC converter for an integrated charger, determining the inductance and performance offered by the electric propulsion machine is essential. The behaviour of the machine under normal motoring operation and as an inductor in a DC-DC converter is different. The inductance offered by an electric machine for a DC-DC converter is different from the inductance at normal operation. In this work, a comprehensive approach to accurately calculate the inductance offered by an Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPM) to a charging operation is calculated using Finite Element Method (FEM). The core and copper losses under this operation are also computed and compared with the normal motoring operation. The sensitivity of inductance offered by the machine with respect to the design parameters is also analyzed.

articleTitle: PM and PM-Less Motors for Electric Vehicles: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: The automotive industry is focusing on developing more efficient and sustainable powertrains in response to the increasing demand for electric vehicles. The benefits and draw-backs of using alternative motor designs, along with the growing trend among motor manufacturers to reduce their reliance on Permanent Magnets are explored by the authors. The analysis includes electromagnetic studies aimed at identifying the operational limits of each type of motor. Specifically, the comparison involves an Interior Permanent Magnet motor, which utilizes NdFeB magnets, and various permanent magnet less motor designs, such as the Electrically Excited Synchronous Motor, the Hybrid Excited Permanent Magnet motor, the Reluctance motor, and the Permanent Magnet assisted Reluctance motor.

articleTitle: On the Effect of Permanent Magnet Eddy Currents During Dynamic Short-Circuits in Traction Motors
abstract: This paper studies the impact of permanent magnet eddy currents on three-phase short-circuit behavior in traction motors. A semi-analytical method is presented, allowing for an evaluation of the sub-transient short circuit behavior resulting from eddy currents. Furthermore, based on typical parameters of traction motors, a fast assessment of the relevance of eddy currents in dynamic short-circuit scenarios is presented. Overall, the effect of eddy current field reaction is found to be small, if not negligible, but it tends to become relevant for larger machines without magnet segmentation. The presented findings are intended to act as a guideline for fast assessment of PM eddy current impact during fault of traction motors.

articleTitle: Multi-Monopole Surface Permanent Magnet Bearingless Motor with DC Suspension Current
abstract: This paper proposes a novel multi-monopole permanent magnet bearingless motor which topology is similar to homopolar bearingless motors. Multiple permanent magnets that are parallelly magnetized in each radial direction are mounted on a ring rotor core. The air-gap flux density distribution includes the rotor pole number and dc component so that radial suspension forces can be generated by dc current in a two-pole suspension winding. Therefore, it does not require rotor rotational angular positions to control the radial suspension force. In addition, a combined winding topology can be applied to the proposed multi-monopole bearingless motor. In this paper, basic principles of force and torque generations are presented. In calculations using 3D-FEM analysis, two pole/slot combinations are compared regarding torques, radial suspension forces, and force error angles. It is verified that the proposed multi-monopole bearingless motor is superior to conventional consequent-pole bearingless motors.

articleTitle: Spline-Based Rotor and Stator Optimization of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
abstract: This work features the magnetostatic optimization of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor using 2D nonlinear simulations in an Isogeometric Analysis framework. The rotor and stator designs are optimized for both geometric parameters and surface shapes via modifications of control points. The scaling laws for magnetism are employed to allow for axial and radial scaling, enabling a thorough optimization of all critical machine parameters for multiple operating points. The process is carried out in a gradient-based fashion with the objectives of lowering motor material cost, torque ripple and losses. It is shown that the optimization can be efficiently conducted for many optimization variables and all objective values can be reduced.

articleTitle: Current Distribution in the Damper Bars of the Synchronous Turbo-Generator
abstract: The damper winding of a synchronous turbo-generator is traditionally modelled by one, two or more fictitious windings along the mutually orthogonal d and q axes. In this paper, the real spatial distribution of the damper winding of a synchronous turbo-generator has been taken into account by the winding function approach and consequently the currents in all damper bars versus time are obtained. This makes it possible to conclude which of the damper bars are most loaded in different operating conditions – steady state condition, steady state condition when a small amount of inverse magnetic field exists in the air gap as well as in some of the transients.

articleTitle: Robust Torque Control of Internal Permanent Magnet Motor Using Experimental Flux Maps
abstract: As the industrial and transportation fields are moving towards electrification, electrical motors are facing increasingly stringent requirements, resulting in accelerated degradation due to parameter variation and component aging. This paper proposes an advanced electric motor torque control strategy robust against the motor parameter variations due to environment and aging. Therefore, to mitigate the adverse effects of these variations, the proposed control strategy leverages multidimensional lookup tables to generate the current references for a standard current vector control. In particular, this paper investigates the impact of motor parameter variations on traditional torque control methods and compares them with a new robust control strategy. The results demonstrate the importance of robust control techniques in electric motor control systems, particularly in demanding applications such as automotive and motorsport.

articleTitle: Analysis of Cogging Torque of a PMSM Drive and its Mitigation via Hybrid Static-Active Filtering and Proportional-Integral Control
abstract: In this paper, a hybrid static-active filter is presented as a new approach to cogging torque mitigation in PMSM drive systems. The cogging torque data acquisition process of the selected PMSM drive is explained, and the performance and theory of the static filter stage is examined as well. The design, benefits and challenges of the active filter, and the hybrid filter as a whole, is also examined, and the importance of noise reference generation, bandwidth and delays are explained through examples from the Active Noise Control (ANC) sphere.

articleTitle: Stress-dependent Iron Loss in Segmented Laminations Considering Surface Roughness
abstract: The paper studies the effects caused by the interface of two separate, or segmented laminated components, with particular emphasis upon reluctance and iron loss. The quality, or smoothness, of the lamination cut edge at the interface of two components is shown to be important, and so the influence of surface roughness at the interface between two adjacent segmented laminations is considered. In general, the smoother the interface surfaces, the smaller the effective gap. Consequently, the surface roughness at the interface of components has a direct influence upon the reluctance of the magnetic circuit. The impact of roughness is experimentally tested and analyzed in detail to determine how it also affects iron loss. The mechanical compressive stress between segments is also considered, given that there must be pressure between adjacent laminated segments. The paper seeks to understand how changing the surface roughness and compressive stress can influence iron losses in segmented electrical machines.

articleTitle: Design Comparison of Wrapped and non-Wrapped Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
abstract: Wrapped Interior Permanent Magnet (IPM) synchronous motors represent a recent breakthrough in the domain of high-speed IPM machines. This innovative rotor design introduces buried Permanent Magnets (PMs) and a Carbon-Fiber (CF) sleeve to secure the magnets against centrifugal forces, obviating the need for traditional iron bridges or ribs, typical in conventional IPM rotor configurations. Nevertheless, the design and analysis of retaining sleeves are essential for enabling safe and efficient high-speed operation. This paper proposes an analytical model for the retaining sleeve design, introducing a graphical pre-design tool to forecast the dimensions and characteristics requisite for the carbon sleeve, given the target maximum speed. A comparative analysis is then conducted between standard IPM motors with ribs and wrapped IPM motors at different maximum speed speeds, highlighting the benefits of the wrapped IPM design and the possible drawbacks.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of High-Speed Switched Reluctance Machines for Aerospace Applications
abstract: A multi-objective optimization method of high-speed switched reluctance machines (SRMs) is presented based on the field-circuit co-simulations integrating the finite element method (FEM) and the genetic algorithm. The adverse impact of the manufacturing process on the material properties is considered through the experimental test on a toroidal laminated core, with which the prediction accuracy of the electromagnetic performances of high-speed SRMs is enhanced. In addition, the empirical allocation of weight coefficients on multi-optimization objectives is avoided by introducing the loss density as a boundary condition in the optimization, simplifying the optimization task. A case study targeting at the 15 kW, 20000 r/min SRM is presented, based on which the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed optimization method are validated. The efficiency of the optimal SRM increases by 1.7% compared with the initial design, whilst the mass is reduced by 0.51 kg.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling of Airgap Fields in Double Magnetic Salient Reluctance Machines with Tangential Field Consideration
abstract: The airgap magnetic field is the most crucial performance for the design and optimization of double magnetic salient reluctance machines (DMSRMs), including mutually switched reluctance machines and switched reluctance motors. However, the existing literatures are limited to the prediction of radial component of the airgap magnetic field, the tangential component is neglected. To address the issue, this paper proposes a universal analytical model of the airgap field for DMSRMs. A simple analytical expression for the airgap field of DMSRMs is derived and verified by finite-element (FE) and experiment, which gives more insight into the radial and tangential airgap field for guiding further design.

articleTitle: A System-Level Design for Reliability of Integrated Motor Drives
abstract: Because of increasing the importance of using an integrated motor drive (IMD) in industry, considering reliability in the design of IMD plays a crucial role. An IMD consists of an electrical motor (EM) and an electrical drive (ED) in a single unit. This configuration helps to eliminate cables and reduce volume which yields increased power density. The most important factors in the failure of EM and ED as a single unit are thermal effects and vibration. In the case of an IMD, a high-reliability design is of paramount importance because there are mutual thermal impacts between the EM and ED. Both EM and ED have components that are susceptible to failure, leading to system failure. Components such as shaft, bearing, stator, and rotor may fail in the EM, and components such as power modules, DC link capacitors, and microcontroller unit (MCU) may degrade due to the stress and thermal in the ED. This paper proposes a method to assess the reliability of an IMD systematically. The proposed algorithm includes three main stages, which are IMD specifications, design for reliability, and system-level functionality testing. The mutual impact between the EM and ED is considered in the design for the reliability stage which is subdivided into three: analysis, initial design, and verification. Applying this algorithm to design an IMD results in reliable operation under various conditions.

articleTitle: Analytical Model for Predicting Output Voltage Distortion of Salient Pole Synchronous Generators under Linear Load
abstract: In this paper, the voltage distortion of rotor wound, salient pole, synchronous generators is studied. Using finite element modelling, the harmonic EMF is analyzed in no-load and load condition. Simulations show that the EMF harmonics are dependent on the load of the machine. Based on FEM results a simplified analytical model for the prediction of voltage distortion is proposed. This model uses an approximated air gap flux density. The goal is to achieve an accurate prediction based on readily available machine parameters. Finally, the results are compared against FEM simulations to evaluate the accuracy of the proposed model.

articleTitle: A Novel PMSM Rotor Speed and Angle Estimation Based on a Multifunctional Sensor
abstract: Accurate rotor position and speed are essential for reliable and efficient electric motor control. This paper proposes a real-time algorithm at higher speeds based on a new concept of multifunctional sensors. However, accuracy, the ranges of machine rotational speed and torque, measurement noises, computation effort, and hardware size and cost are among the parameters that should be considered during the algorithm design. The proposed method consists of a sliding mode angle-tracking observer (ATO) and a neural network estimator, which enable the algorithm to operate robustly at all operating ranges of the motor. The contribution of this paper is to present a robust algorithm for estimating the rotor angle using a multifunctional sensor. Despite its low computation efforts, simulation and implementation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the suggested algorithm.

articleTitle: Investigation Performance Characteristics of the Flat Fan Nozzle on the Oil Spray Cooling System
abstract: This article presented experimentally a study on the flat fan nozzle and the impact of the nozzle's input parameters on its performance with oil as a high viscosity coolant, as well as estimating their performance, spray characteristic, and heat transfer coefficient (HTC) during the design period. For this purpose, the test bench was developed, and NF0390, as a commercial flat fan nozzle with a medium spray angle, was selected. A series of experiments are carried out, and the impact of various nozzle input parameters is investigated. The nozzle's performance is investigated by heat transfer capability, temperature rise and providing temperature uniformity. Several suggestions and tips for more efficient and even temperature and cooling performances are proposed.

articleTitle: Rotor Faults Condition Monitoring in Direct on Line Start Permanent Magnet Motors
abstract: Direct on-line permanent magnet motors have been gaining attention in pumping and other applications due to their improved efficiency and smaller size-to-power ratio, while facilitating the acceleration of the motor. Being an induction motor and a permanent magnet synchronous motor at the same time, this machine's stress analysis and condition monitoring poses tremendous interest and little work has been accomplished so far. This paper sheds some light on this area by primarily studying the frequency spectra of the stator current under healthy conditions. Then two different rotor faults are studied: the demagnetization and a broken bar. The analysis concerns both the starting transient and the steady state. The results are based on extensive simulations with Finite Element Analysis of a model verified by experimental testing.

articleTitle: Broken Bar Detection of Axial-Flux Induction Machines Through Advanced Transient Current Signature Analysis
abstract: Taking into account the criticalness of the early detection of broken rotor bars in medium- and high-power induction machines (IM), several diagnosis techniques have been developed, validated, and refined for commercial radial flux IM. Among them, the advanced technique of current signature analysis (ATCSA) is stated to achieve a reliable diagnosis of the motor condition. Nonetheless, the feasibility and sensitiveness of these diagnosis tools when applied to axial flux IM has not been covered in the literature, although it is a logical step in the advent of modern machining techniques. In this paper, the ATCSA is evaluated on an axial flux induction machine designed to match the performance of a comparative radial flux IM. The assessment was conducted through three-dimensional finite element simulations, resulting in a successful outcome: it was found that ATCSA can successfully indicate the presence of rotor bar breakage in AFIM. As a result, a numerical factor is devised in this paper to indicate the rotor fault severity in AFIM, which automatically tracks the energy path of relevant faulty current harmonics.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design and Structural Analysis of Magnetic-Geared Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Unmanned Underwater Vehicle
abstract: This paper presents a magnetic-geared permanent magnet synchronous motor (MG-PMSM), which is an integrated structure composed of a PMSM and a MG, designed for application to an unmanned underwater vehicle (UUV). The MG-PMSM features a dual rotor structure: a high-speed permanent magnetic rotor (PMR) and a low-speed pole piece rotor (PPR). To meet the required load conditions of the UUV, the PPR, directly connected to the output shaft, operates under load conditions, while the PMR operates under no-load conditions by controlling current. The aim of this study is to investigate the electromagnetic performance of the proposed MG-PMSM under different gear ratios and slot-pole combinations. To support the PPR, pin bolts and an iron core bridge were considered for the proposed MG-PMSM. A structural analysis of the PPR and its support structure was conducted considering load conditions. Finally, the power density per unit volume of the finally selected MG-PMSM for the direct drive system was compared with that of a PMSM with a M G for an indirect drive system.

articleTitle: Equivalent Resistance Model of the Permanent-Magnet Motor for Predicting Electromagnetic Losses
abstract: This paper proposes an equivalent resistance model of the permanent-magnet (PM) motor which is useful for predicting the losses. The PM loss and iron loss are replaced by the eddy-current loss and hysteresis loss in the equivalent resistance model, where the characteristics of these losses are extracted from the analytical model. The harmonic current and the current control angle are investigated in the paper to guarantee the accuracy of the loss prediction. The parameters in the equivalent resistance model can be easily obtained from the finite-element model and experiment. The proposed model demonstrates significant potential to improve motor efficiency.

articleTitle: Multi-Physics Design and Analysis of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Motors for In-Wheel Direct-Drive
abstract: In this paper, a novel dual-rotor inner-stator axial flux permanent magnet vernier motor(AFPMVM) that utilizes stator teeth as magnetic field modulation components is investigated and analyzed for the in-wheel direct-drive applications. Two variations of this topology are implemented, featuring both a toroidal winding and a drum winding. First of all, this paper conducts a comparative analysis of the performance of two aforementioned AFPM topologies and traditional radial-flux motor. Then, a quasi three-dimensional analysis method is utilized to verify the electromagnetic performance, ensuring that the design meets the required specifications. Next, stator and rotor structures were designed and simulated to analyze the stress and deformation of different components during installation and motor operation. Finally, based on the results of finite element analysis, the AFPM motor with a toroidal winding was selected for comparison and a prototype with a maximum torque of 135Nm was manufactured. The results show that the AFPM proposed in this article has significant advantages in both torque and efficiency.

articleTitle: Design and Prototype Tests of Magnetic-Geared Switched Reluctance Motor for In-Wheel Direct-Drive EVs
abstract: In-wheel motors for electric vehicles (EVs) have attracted significant attention due to their compact size, ease of maintenance, and quiet operation. Direct-drive permanent magnet (PM) motors and magnetic-geared PM motors have been proposed as in-wheel motors because of their high torque density. However, in addition to torque density, in-wheel motors for EVs require high-speed operation, which is difficult to achieve with these motors because flux weakening control is relatively ineffective. This paper presents a novel magnetic-geared motor consisting of a flux-modulated magnetic gear and a switched reluctance (SR) motor. The proposed motor exhibits a wide speed-torque characteristic that surpasses conventional in-wheel direct-drive motors. Furthermore, a targeted maximum torque of 100 N.m and a maximum speed of 376 rpm were achieved with a prototype machine.

articleTitle: Surface vs. Embedded Magnets in Permanent Magnet Outer Rotor Synchronous Motors
abstract: A comprehensive comparison of two topologies of outer rotor Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs) is given. Specifically, it examines outer rotor motors with rotor surface magnets (S-PMSM) and those with embedded V-positioned magnets (V-PMSM) under geometric constraints dictated by the system's requirements for high specific torque. The investigation involves initial design considerations and Finite Element Method (FEM) optimization for maximizing the specific torque while minimizing torque ripple. Both motor designs aim to achieve a high torque density and specific torque alongside a substantial field-weakening capability for efficient operation across a broad speed range. The analysis covers aspects of design methodology, optimization processes, and performance evaluation, including torque production and efficiency.

articleTitle: Ripple Correlation Control for a Low-Cost Single-Stage Photovoltaic Water Pumping System
abstract: In this paper, an integrated control algorithm is presented for a low-cost single-stage photovoltaic water pumping system. The pump is driven by a brushless DC motor, controlled in the three-phase conduction mode. The integrated control algorithm includes the maximum power point tracking and the third harmonic injection PWM techniques. While the MPPT ensures the extraction of the maximum available power from the PV panels, the third harmonic injection PWM carries out the switching action of the BLDCM drive. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed technique reduces torque ripple by approximately 60% when compared to the conventional method with an equal number of drive components.

articleTitle: Combination Method and Comparative Analysis of Parallel Hybrid Excitation Machines with Integrated Armature Winding
abstract: The parallel hybrid excitation machine is a combination of a rotor-permanent magnet machine and a stator-wound reluctance machine, inheriting the advantages of the both two parts. This paper proposes the design criteria for combining the two machines using a set of integrated armature winding, aiming to improve the existing separate armature winding structure. The analysis indicates that a single-layer structure is mandatory for the unified star of slots and the same winding configuration of the two parts. The high winding factors for both the permanent magnet machine part and the reluctance machine part cannot be achieved simultaneously. Four 18-stator-slot parallel hybrid excitation machines with different rotor pole pair numbers were then selected and compared. The comparison results indicate the machine with fewer rotor pole pairs exhibits higher flux linkage and output torque, but diminished flux regulation and short-circuit current suppression capability.

articleTitle: Flux Switching Gerotor Pump
abstract: In this paper, we explore a smart integration of a gerotor positive displacement pump inside a flux-switching permanent magnet motor. Optimization as well as 3D simulations have been carried out and exposed. A prototype has been manufactured and measured and a fair comparison with a conventional motor is exposed, validating the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Unified Flux Observer for Induction and Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
abstract: A new unified adaptive flux observer for induction machines (IMs) and permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) is proposed in this work. The proposed unified observer is created using both the well-known “Voltage Model” (VM) and the “Flux Model” (FM) in the estimated rotating synchronous frame. Under the time-scale separation assumption between the rotor flux dynamics and the stator current dynamics in the estimated rotor synchronous frame, the rotor flux can be considered a slowly varying signal for which an adaptation law has been designed. We showed that the proposed unified observer can be applied to IMs and PMSMs with minimum knowledge of motor parameters, requiring only information on the stator resistance and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dq$</tex> axis inductances. The stability of the proposed observer is proven using the Lyapunov theory based on the presented unified model. Finally, numerical simulations in MATLAB/Simulink and experimental tests on an IM and a PMSM are provided to illustrate the theoretical results.

articleTitle: Determination of Current Transducer Phase Delay and its Effect on PWM-Induced Losses Calculation in Laminated Ferromagnetic Materials
abstract: Current transducers introduce a phase delay depending on the frequency of excitation, which affects the calculation of PWM-induced power loss in ferromagnetic materials. It is therefore necessary to compensate for this delay. The measurement setup is presented, the compensation characteristics were determined and applied to the results of DC bias measurements performed on a ring core sample of ferromagnetic material. Significant effect of compensation is found for some cases with higher frequency of excitation current.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control with Indirect Field Oriented Speed Estimation for Seven-Phase Induction Machines
abstract: Multiphase machines offer more degrees of freedom than conventional three-phase machines. Thus, a multiphase drive can control multiple spatial harmonics independently of each other. With the torque generation in the 1 <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>vector space, this paper proposes to inject currents in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{rd}$</tex>vector space for the speed estimation thus realizing a sensorless control scheme. At lower mechanical speeds, the back-EMF decreases and becomes more difficult to estimate as the signal-to-noise ratio decreases. Injecting a slip increases the stator frequency, which in turn allows a better estimation of the back electromotive force. An experiment showing a start from standstill conditions demonstrates the proposed control.

articleTitle: Experimental Comparison of Three Direct Winding Cooling Methods
abstract: The urgency of mitigating climate change has fueled a shift towards electrification across industries, driving the need for efficient and high-power-density electric machines. While significant attention has historically been paid to electromagnetic design, the rising importance of power density and efficiency has underscored the criticality of thermal management. In this context, various cooling topologies have been explored to enhance heat transfer effectiveness and minimize thermal resistance. This paper presents experimental evaluations of three direct winding cooling methods: submerged stator cooling, mid- conductor winding cooling, and submerged jet cooling. Through controlled experiments, the thermal and hydraulic performances of these methods were analyzed, revealing insights into their efficacy under different operating conditions. The results show that submerged stator cooling has the lowest thermohydraulic performance, having a higher thermal resistance at equal pumping power. Mid-conductor winding cooling and submerged jet cooling achieve comparable results, albeit a different operating conditions. The submerged jet measurements indicate relatively low pressure drops at flow rates in the common range expected for this size of machine. Mid-conductor winding cooling achieved similar thermal resistances and pumping powers but at exceptionally low flow rates and high pressure drops. It is concluded that for this case, submerged jet is the preferred technique of the three, but mid-conductor winding cooling shows promise for less compactly wound coils where pressure drop can be reduced and flow rate increased.

articleTitle: Moving from a 3D Axial Flux Machine Model to 2D Considering the Impact of End Leakage Flux
abstract: Axial Flux Machines (AFMs) may have a potential of smaller axial length and higher power and torque density compared to the Radial Flux Machines (RFMs). However, the AFM needs to be modeled in Three-Dimensions (3D) yielding a large computation time when solving the Finite Element Method (FEM) model. A larger extent of computation time can be reduced by transforming the 3D problem to a Two-Dimensional (2D) problem. A single computation plane located at the center of the magnet in the 3D model is employed. This transformation leads to a loss of information due to the leakage flux in the axial direction, mainly around the rotor magnets and around the stator end windings. The purpose of this paper is to transform the 3D AFM model to a 2D model and quantify the consequences. An off-the-shelf outer stator inner rotor reference AFM is compared with an equivalent 3D FEM model. Several 3D and 2D models with varying core and magnet lengths were compared. A model with narrow core and magnet lengths was further investigated for five different model sizes ranging from full 3D to 2D. The results for the investigated machine type reveal that the rotor magnet leakage contributes to a dominant effect that necessitates a 3D model if a magnetically leading rotor core surrounds the magnet in the radial direction, and when the radial thickness of the magnets is small. Similarly, winding end leakage effects must be modeled in 3D when the radial thickness of the stator core is small relative to the coil end extent.

articleTitle: Magnetic Hysteresis Impact on HF Signal Injection
abstract: This article presents a model of a Synchronous Reluctance Motor (SynRM) at standstill, including magnetic hysteresis, to study its impact on High-Frequency (HF) signal injection. So that it can easily be simulated, the model is rewritten under state-form. The parameters of the model are identified, based on experimental data, using a customized fitting procedure adapted to hysteresis curves. The proposed model explains the impact of magnetic hysteresis on HF signal injection and reproduces accurately the experiments.

articleTitle: An Efficient Open-Loop Approach to Reliable Starting of Synchronous Reluctance Motor Drives
abstract: This article introduces a reliable open-loop starting method for sensorless synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM) drives, based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I-f$</tex> control. A torque controller has been proposed to vary the rate of reference frequency during <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I- f$</tex> operation. The torque controller ensures stable starting by manipulating the reference frequency rate according to the prevailing loading condition of the drive. A two-stage optimal current injection approach for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I-f$</tex> control has been discussed to enhance the efficiency of the proposed starting method. The first stage evaluates the optimum current based on the estimated torque and in succession, the second stage utilises a speed-band based algorithm to fine-tune the previously obtained operating current. The proposed control scheme has been validated through a combination of simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Finite Difference Model for the Calculation of Eddy Current Losses in Foil Windings of Distribution Transformers
abstract: This paper presents a 2D model for calculating the magnetic vector potential, current density distribution and losses in foil windings of distribution transformers based on the finite difference method. The model solves a Helmholtz equation in the complex domain to obtain the magnetic field and to account for the eddy currents induced in the foil winding. The factor of increased losses due to eddy currents was calculated and all results were validated by comparison with the model based on the finite element method.

articleTitle: A Novel Torque-Coupled Axial-Flux Permanent Magnet Motor with Magnetic Coupler for Flux Weakening
abstract: This paper proposes a torque-coupled axial-flux permanent magnet (AFPM) motor with a wide speed operating range. The motor system incorporates an innovative and adaptive mechanical flux weakening method comprising a single-stator dual-rotor type AFPM and a magnetic coupler with a rigid stopper. The two components are concentrically integrated to maximize radial space utilization, enabling the torque generated by both rotors to collaboratively act on the load side through the magnetic coupler. As the load torque varies, the torque of both rotors is also regulated. This enables the automatic adjustment of the angular displacement between the two rotors through the magnetic coupler, thereby changing the combined electromotive force (EMF) to achieve a wide speed range flux weakening operation. In addition, the implementation for calculating the flux weakening degree during constant power operation is presented. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the design are validated through three-dimensional finite element simulations.

articleTitle: SPMMs and Enclosures Steady Heat Transfer Modeling Utilizing a 3-D Finite Element Partitioning Technique
abstract: Instead of using a single, complete, finite-element (FE) model of a synchronous permanent magnet machine (SPMM) and it's enclosure for the purpose of carrying out a detailed thermal analysis, it is shown in this paper that analogous results can be obtained by partitioning the FE model into two domains i.e., the electric machine active part and its enclosure. The aforementioned procedure is not quite straightforward, as it requires the application of a surface heat source on the area in contact with the electrical machine, in order to excite thermally the enclosure. Then, the thermal analysis of the electrical machine follows by constraining the nodal temperature distribution of the area in thermal contact with the enclosure. There are important advantages over the conventional modeling approach. The computational cost of the FE analysis is significantly reduced due to the reduction of the mesh sizes and the inherent nonlinear computational cost of the FE method in conjunction with the number of nodes of the FE mesh. In addition, the design procedure of the FE model is simplified and expedited, whereas the graphics post-processing is easier and yields useful visual results.

articleTitle: Line-Start Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Stator Fault Diagnostics Immune to Unbalanced Supply Voltages
abstract: This paper presents an inter-turn short-circuit fault diagnostic technique for three-phase line-start permanent magnet synchronous motors immune to the supply voltage conditions. More traditional fault diagnostic methodologies are unable to fully address the diagnosis of stator inter-turn short-circuit faults in three-phase motors under unbalanced supply voltage conditions, since the most traditional indicators are similarly impacted. The proposed technique relies on the spectral analysis of specific harmonics (originated by the slot harmonics), presented in the alpha-beta plane modulus of the motor current, explored in a new way. The severity factor is determined resorting to the Parseval's theorem (calculation of the total energy of the analyzed subharmonics). Experimental results, considering different load torques, unbalanced supply voltage conditions, and fault severity levels, show that inter-turn short-circuit fault detection can be fully achieved under unbalanced supply voltage conditions.

articleTitle: Impact of SMC Property on Axial Flux Machine Employing Ferrite PM in Traction Applications
abstract: This paper investigates impact of soft magnetic composite (SMC) properties on an axial flux permanent magnet machine (AFPM) employing ferrite permanent magnet (PM) in traction applications. In general, as iron loss of SMCs gets smaller, the efficiency of AFPMs can be higher. However, the torque and output power of AFPMs are reduced due to the decrease in magnetic permeability because there is a trade-off relationship between the iron loss and permeability of SMCs. In this paper, many virtual SMC materials with different iron loss and permeability are used for simulations of the proposed AFPM in order to investigate sensitivity to material properties. First, the impact of the permeability on the torque and output power is investigated because the output power is very important in traction applications. Additionally, the total energy loss of the AFPMs employing various SMCs is evaluated by WLTC driving cycle. Finally, this paper shows the newly developed SMC materials and discusses a suitable SMC property from the perspective of the efficiency and output power in traction applications.

articleTitle: Indirect Efficiency Measurement of Outer-Rotor Inverter-Fed PM Synchronous Machines
abstract: In many cases, a direct torque measurement is not suitable or not possible when it comes to efficiency determination of electric machines. Examples are the rising requirements for lower measurement uncertainty due to the increasing number of super premium efficiency motors (IE4 and higher) or the rising number of super high-speed machines, impeding a direct torque measurement. The efficiency determination from the summation of losses (indirect determination) is a well-known alternative for large-power grid-operated machines. We expand the known loss determination methods to 1- and 3-phase outer-rotor PM machines of 15 … 12 000 W rated output power. Only slight deviations between directly and indirectly determined efficiency values are concluded. However, for these rather small machines the measurement uncertainty of the indirect method is often bigger than of the direct method due to the high uncertainties in the eddy current and friction loss determination.

articleTitle: Electrification of Non-Road Mobile Machinery: A Tool for Motor Selection
abstract: In this research paper, a MATLAB-based tool is designed to assist users in selecting and dimensioning electric motors for electrification of the powertrain of Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM). The tool leverages a normalized duty cycle, which is then scaled based on the specific application requirements. By plotting the scaled duty cycle on an efficiency map of an electric motor, the evaluation of the suitability of the electric machine is performed for the proposed heavy-duty application and powertrain. The primary purpose of this tool is to streamline the design and realization process of electric powertrains for Non-Road Mobile Machinery.

articleTitle: Analytical Design Optimization of Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Machines - Part II: Results
abstract: The reduction of computational time in design optimization of anisotropic electrical machines play a fundamental role, since the identification of the supply conditions requires the accurate knowledge of the machine magnetic model. This paper proposes a fast design optimization procedure for permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance machines (PMaSyRM) based on non-linear magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC) proposed and detailed in the part I, capable of accounting for both saturation and cross-saturation effects. The optimization routine is used to identify the inevitable trade-offs between the competitive needs of maximizing the torque at base speed and maximizing the efficiency in different operating points, for a given outer envelope. The obtained results are commented in depth, thus leading to some design insights also in terms of demagnetization resistance under short circuit condition.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Modeling of Bearing and Transmission Currents in Electric Vehicles
abstract: The pulse-width modulation employed in inverters generates a common mode voltage, leading to bearing currents that can reduce the lifetime of electrical machines. The automotive industry's trends towards higher battery voltages and fast-switching wide-bandgap semiconductor devices further exacerbate this phenomenon. This study presents an extended high-frequency model of electric vehicle powertrains, parameterized analytically and numerically, which incorporates the transmission to predict parasitic current flow through all bearings and gears. The results indicate significant circulating bearing currents in electric vehicles with 800 V battery voltages and state-of-the-art inverters using wide-bandgap semiconductor devices. Furthermore, it is shown that the installation of a shaft grounding device on the drive end of electrical machines, coupled with the inclusion of a transmission, yields a significant reduction in drive end bearing currents while showing no substantial impact on the non-drive end bearing current. The observed transmission bearing currents and current densities indicate a low risk of bearing damage.

articleTitle: An Electrical Machine Design Procedure Based on Thermo-Electromagnetic Coupling
abstract: This research introduces a design procedure based on thermo-electromagnetic coupling. This coupling of these two important design procedures allows the thermal calculation to be performed during the sensitivity analysis iteration. In this way, machine designers can make direct adjustments to parameters that have an effect not only on electromagnetic performance but also on the thermal performance of the machine. The results benefit from applying the fast, analytical matrix model, an advanced variant of the classical lumped parameter thermal network (LPTN). The matrix model reduces computational costs and operating times, thus allowing it to be integrated into the electrical machine sensitivity analyses.

articleTitle: Parasitic Parameters Effect on the Operation of High Frequency Electric Drive System
abstract: The rapid switching of semiconductor power modules in electric drive systems generates high frequency (HF) common mode voltage at the motor terminals which causes bearing failure and winding degradation. Therefore, accurate characterization of the inverter and motor parameters - including parasitic effects - is vitally important to understand the high frequency performance as well as to model and mitigate the switching oscillations of the electric drive system. In this paper, the high frequency operation of the inverter in the electric drive system, as well as the direct effect of the parasitic components on the complete system are thoroughly investigated. Moreover, a detailed extraction process of the high frequency parasitic parameters is introduced. An equivalent circuit model of the complete drive system based on the impedance characteristics is introduced. Additionally, a HF model of a 750W three-phase induction motor is developed with parameter values determined from measurements on this motor.

articleTitle: Synchronization Process Analysis of Line Start Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
abstract: Ahstract-Line-start permanent magnet synchronous machines (LSPMSM) can start without converters, enabling them to replace asynchronous machines in low-cost industrial applications. The starting process of line-start interior permanent magnet synchronous machine(LS-IPMSM) still lacks accurate analysis. In this paper, we use the quasi-static method to simplify the five-rank dq0 model to a two-rank model. A new method is proposed to compute the synchronous capability of LSPMSMs based on the simplified model. Simulation results show the high accuracy of the simplified model during the starting process and the effectiveness of the proposed method to compute the starting capability for LS-IPMSMs compared to the conventional method.

articleTitle: Claw Pole -Single Magnet Rotor Small Synchronous Actuator Motor: Optimal Design via 3D-MEC with 3D FEM Validation
abstract: Small synchronous PM motor variable speed drives (actuators) are widely applied for automotive auxiliaries and home appliances. Reducing cost but keeping performance (efficiency) high with less costly and more available PMs is imperative. The present paper considers the claw pole single magnet small synchronous motor with bonded Nd, ferrite and sintered NdFeB rotor magnet, with Somaloy versus forged iron rotor core and tooth-wound three phase stator winding for which a 3D-MEC(magnetic equivalent circuit) based optimal design methodology and code, with 3D-FEM key validations is proposed, developed and documented through extensive digital simulation results on a 12 slot, 10 pole machine.

articleTitle: The Evaluation of Optimal Ratio of Outer Diameter to Axial Length on Torque Density for the External Rotor PMSM
abstract: The high torque density external rotor permanent magnet synchronous motors (ER-PMSMs) are desired in numerous applications today. The ratio of rotor diameter to axial length and rotor diameter to stator diameter are key parameters which has great impact on the torque density. This paper investigated the optimum ratio of outer diameter to axial length for maximising the torque density of the ER-PMSMS. It was found that when the ratios of outer diameter to axial length and rotor diameter to stator diameter are 3.1 and 1.11, respectively, the torque of model motor reaches the maximum. It is also found that the volume of the motor has little effect on the selection of the optimum ratio within the proposed torque range.

articleTitle: Considerations on Matrix-Based, Analytical Temperature Prediction Tools for Electrical Machines
abstract: Thermal analysis is an important part of electrical machine design. Improving the accuracy and speed of the thermal analysis model is an important step in optimizing the design procedure, considering the need for temperature prediction of high-performance electrical machines at both steady-state and transient operation conditions. In this paper, a fast thermal modeling technique with lower computational cost and runtime is implemented. This model applies matrix arithmetic as an advanced variant of the classical lumped parameter thermal network (LPTN). This allows flexible adjustment of the model parameters in cases such as sensitivity analyses. A 24-slot 8-pole high-speed PMSM is used as a test case. An equivalent five-node thermal model is built for one of its stator slot sections, thus finding the temperature at the copper winding and stator iron. The steady-state temperature at the five nodes derived using the classical LPTN and the proposed approach are compared, along with the calculation time taken. The error values of the temperature results obtained by the two methods are also presented.

articleTitle: Demagnetisation and Performance Study of Neodymium and Ferrite Assisted SynRM
abstract: This paper focuses on the demagnetisation and performance study of ferrite magnets used in a Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Machine (PMaSynRM). The effect of magnetomotive force (MMF) from the stator on the rotor barrier is studied at different current magnitudes and phase advance. The self-demagnetisation of the magnets is also investigated under no-load conditions, and an attempt is made to determine the remanent flux density of different magnets when placed in different rotor barriers together. Lastly, the performance of an optimized ferrite rotor design is compared with an Nd motor of similar volume. To address the performance shortcomings observed when comparing the ferrite motor with the Nd motor of similar volume, a suggested solution involves the development of a hybrid motor incorporating both types of magnets. To match the performance with the Nd motor, the hybrid motor has to be elongated with the same active diameter. This hybrid design yields a weight reduction of 0.9 kg for the Nd magnet while maintaining performance equivalent to that of a Nd motor. Additionally, a substantial cost reduction of approximately 18 % is achieved.

Author Keywords: Permanent magnet assisted Synchronous reluctance machines

articleTitle: Seven-Leg VSI SVPWM Technique for Novel Dual-Armature Winding Dual-PM Flux Modulated Machines With Array-Torque Components
abstract: The SVPWM control strategy of a seven-leg voltage source inverter (SL-VSI) for a novel dual-armature winding dual-PM flux modulated machine (DWDM) is proposed in this paper. The DWDM has 5-phase stator windings and 3-phase rotor windings, and the permanent magnets arranged in Halbach forms are embedded in both stator and rotor slots. The DWDM is able to generate array-torque components based on unique slot/pole combinations. Similar to a five-leg VSI (FL-VSI) dual three-phase machine driving, the eight-phase DWDM can be controlled using a SL-VSI as the supply, with one inverter leg being common to both the stator and the rotor. The proposed topology can increase the power density of the integrated system. It can also serve as a fault-tolerant solution when an open-circuit fault occurs in the power device of a bridge arm in the commonly used eight-phase VSI. Two SVPWM methods for the FL-VSI, i.e., the half-period method and the centralization modulation method, are generalized to the proposed SL-VSI. The simulation results verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design and Thermal Analysis of a Novel Transverse Flux Permanent Magnet Machine
abstract: Transverse flux permanent magnet motors (TFPMMs) have received much attention due to simple windings and high reliability. However, existing TFPMs still have problems, such as high cogging torque. Therefore, this paper provides a new TFPMM with step skew crossed teeth structure (SSCT-TFM), which can optimize the reluctance distribution on the stator surface and thus reduce the cogging torque. In addition, the 3D flux of the TFPMM leads to complex thermal design. This paper provides a thermal network model of SSCT-TFM to evaluate the temperature of each part of the motor. A 3D finite element analysis (FEA) model is developed further to analyze the electromagnetic and thermal performance of the SSCT-TFM. Finally, a prototype is manufactured and tested for no-load and load performance.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Multiple-Torque Components Dual Rotor Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine for Aviation Propulsion Applications
abstract: In this paper, a novel multiple-torque components dual rotor axial flux permanent magnet vernier machine for aviation propulsion applications is proposed. The machine adopts Halbach PMs in the stator slot opening to reduce leakage flux. Based on the dual rotor structure and flux modulation effect, the proposed machine features four torque components, which can further improve the torque density. The paper investigates the effect of some key parameters on torque and utilizes multi-objective genetic algorithm (MOGA) for global optimization. The machine parameters are determined according to the Pareto solution set. Through the 3-D finite element (FE) method, the paper explores the electromagnetic performances of the machine. The results indicate that the proposed machine has high torque and torque density, which can meet the design requirements of the aviation propulsion machine.

articleTitle: Development of a Neural Network Approach to Evaluate Magnetic Losses in Nanocrystalline Transformers
abstract: Nanocrystalline transformers play a crucial role in modern power distribution systems due to their high efficiency and superior magnetic properties. However, an accurate evaluation of losses in these transformers is essential for optimizing their performance. The application of neural networks in assessing losses in nanocrystalline transformers was performed in this work. Neural networks, a subset of artificial intelligence, have shown remarkable capabilities in modeling complex systems and predicting outcomes based on input data. By training neural networks with relevant parameters, accurate predictions of losses in nanocrystalline transformers can be achieved. Overall, leveraging neural networks for evaluating losses in nanocrys-talline transformers presents a promising avenue for enhancing transformer design and performance in modern power systems.

articleTitle: A Sustainable Booster Induction Motor for Dual Axle Automotive Applications
abstract: This work evaluates replacing copper hairpins with aluminium hairpin and focuses on high torque density sustainable induction motor designs used as torque booster for dual-axle automotive applications. A performance comparison of the motor using aluminium and copper hairpins is conducted. The performance study focuses on maximizing torque, power and reducing active weight, as well as the environmental impact of the booster motor of the electric vehicle's electric drive unit. A thermal evaluation of the motor is conducted for 10-time repeated acceleration from 0 to 100 km/h. Due to the lower AC copper loss of the aluminium hairpin winding, the total stator resistive losses for both motors remain comparable to each other. The torque capability for both motors is almost identical. Due to the lower material density, the motor with aluminium hairpin winding becomes lighter and consequently with a higher torque density. aluminium has a significantly lower environmental load unit compared to copper, and it can be considered a sustainable material to be used in the winding of booster motors for the electric vehicle drive unit.

articleTitle: Performance and Efficiency Mapping of Externally Excited Synchronous Machines
abstract: This paper presents the process of analyzing the performance of an externally excited synchronous machine (EESM). The paper aims to provide engineers and researchers with a simple process to extract motor maps using finite element analysis (FEA) followed by an analytical post-processing of the simulation results. An example motor is considered where the flux maps are extracted through FEA calculations and then used to define the operational limits of the motor at a specific dc-link voltage level using an optimization algorithm. Within the operational limits of the motor, the losses are then minimized and finally, the results from the optimization are shown.

articleTitle: Advanced Analysis of Armature Currents Signals for Sparking Detection in DC Motors and Generators
abstract: DC machines are not so spread in industry as other electric machines. However, they still subsist in many applications being, in some of them, critical assets. Since most of the research papers dealing with diagnostics have been focused on AC machines, there is a scarcity of predictive maintenance methods that are suited to DC machines and that can be applied in industry. In this context, one of the most common anomalies in DC machines (both motors and generators) is the presence of sparks between the brushes and commutator system. This sparking phenomenon is a symptom of the presence of several faults in the machine, such as inadequate contact between brushes and commutator, commutator deformation, eccentricities, deposit of contamination, etc. All these can lead to catastrophic effects in the machine if they are not detected in due time. Therefore, the detection of the sparking phenomenon when it is still in its early stage and the correct quantification of the sparking severity is a valuable tool for the determination of the health of these machines. This paper presents a method to detect and assess the sparking activity in DC machines. The method is based on the time-frequency analysis of armature currents by using the Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT). The experimental results confirm that an increase in the sparking activity generates a large amount of low-frequency harmonics. This fact allows the introduction of fault severity Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) that relate the current condition of the commutation quality with respect to a baseline (reference pattern) that is obtained when the machine is in healthy condition.

articleTitle: Analysing the Performance of a High-Speed Solid Rotor Induction Machine with Copper Coating
abstract: Performance requirements for electrical machines have increased as a result of sustainability and reliability demands, leading to more power dense machines. One way to address this need for improved performance is by utilizing emerging materials. By taking advantage of new technologies, it is possible to utilize different materials to enhance the capabilities of electrical machines. In this study, the performance of a 12 kW high-speed solid rotor induction machine (SRIM) is improved by a copper coating on the rotor surface. The results demonstrate that incorporating a thin copper coating leads to improvements in electromagnetic torque, ranging from 54% to 82%, across various operating conditions. Torque generation capability and rotor losses are investigated through finite element analysis and verified by experimental test of a prototype.

articleTitle: Detection of Stator Asymmetries in Synchronous Reluctance Motors through the Analysis of the Stator Current
abstract: In recent years, there is a growing interest in synchronous reluctance motors due to their advantages like high efficiency or the absence of rare-earth permanent magnets. However, fault diagnosis techniques applied to SynRMs are limited. One of the most common types of failures in electric motors are the stator faults. Hence, this paper presents a methodology for the detection of stator asymmetries that enhances the identification of fault components and their severity in SynRM. The method is based on the capture of current signals and on the application of frequency and time-frequency transforms (in this case, the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) and the Short Time Fourier Transform (STFT)). The results show clear signatures linked the fault that appear both in the current spectrum and in the time-frequency map. Moreover, the intensities of these signatures increase as the fault gets worse, so a fault indicator based on the amplitude of the third harmonic is introduced for determining the fault severity level. The results of this work, obtained for different levels of load, allow to detect the presence of stator asymmetries and their severity both under the startup transiend and during the steady-state regime.

articleTitle: Impacts of Stator Current Angle and Rotor Current on Solid Losses of Hairpin Windings in Traction Electrically Excited Synchronous Machines
abstract: Hairpins in motor windings have attracted growing interest in the industrial community. However, the AC losses in the hairpins are much greater than those in the round wire when a high frequency current passes through, resulting in a reduction in the efficiency of the motor. Generally, AC losses are categorized into skin effect and proximity effect, which are caused by flux leakage. In this case, the magnetic leakage is due to the interaction of stator and rotor magnetic field variation, resulting in flux leakage at the slots opening. The synthesized magnetic field built by the stator current, including amplitude and angle, and the rotor current decides the level and position of stator iron-core saturation. Such saturation affects the flux leakage and furthermore hairpin AC losses. In this article, a model built in ANSYS to study the effect of current angles and rotor current on AC losses and AC resistance at different operation situations. The results of this paper can help improve the existing model of AC losses and therefore contribute to a more accurate motor control method.

articleTitle: Research on Harmonic Optimization to Reduce UMP Induced by Rotor Eccentricity in PMSMs
abstract: This paper aims to illustrate the beneficial effect of weakening flux density harmonics in reducing the unbalanced magnetic pull (UMP) induced by rotor eccentricity in permanent magnet (PM) synchronous motors (PMSMs). Firstly, the initial phase angles of flux density harmonics under rotor eccentricity are analyzed. Then, the effect of eccentric magnets on radial electromagnetic force is investigated. The interaction between the original flux density harmonics and the sideband harmonics introduced by rotor eccentricity generates the 1storder radial force. The eccentric magnet greatly weakens these flux density harmonics, thereby reducing the source of UMP. Finally, two 48-slot/8-pole PMSMs with concentric magnets and eccentric magnets are used to verify the analytical analysis. The simulation results show that the UMP of PMSM with eccentric magnets is obviously lower than that with concentric magnets.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Approaches for Electromagnetic Analysis of Traction Electrical Motors: A Proposal for a Benchmark Problem
abstract: The rising demand for high-performance traction electrical motors in electric vehicles necessitates efficient design solutions. This paper describes a preliminary approach to data-driven modelling of the electromagnetic design problem of traction electrical motors. The initial step consists of generating the dataset for training the data-driven models, which is performed using an FEA-based procedure. Subsequently, different data-driven approaches are compared to surrogate the output of the electromagnetic analysis, identified in the computation of the torque and the torque ripple of a specific electrical motor structure.

articleTitle: Design and Scaling Effects of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines for Propeller Direct Drives
abstract: Surface permanent magnet synchronous machines (SPMSM) are generally viewed as the most promising electrical machine type for aircraft propulsion. Simultaneously, the power range per propulsion unit is becoming more flexible through distributed propulsion options. Therefore, the scalability effects of SPMSM for propeller drives become relevant and are investigated in this paper. For this purpose, in a first step the analytical design method from [1] is expanded and compared to literature values and finite element analysis. It shows sufficient agreement to both. Furthermore, it is extended to encompass propeller boundary conditions to evaluate the influence of different power levels for distributed propulsion, diameter limits and torque-speed-splits on efficiency, power density and winding choice.

articleTitle: Two-Phase Commutation Method for Improved Transient Performance of a Dual-Rotor Switched Reluctance Machine
abstract: This paper presents a two-phase commutation scheme to improve the transient behavior of a dual-rotor switched reluctance machine operating under master/slave control. Since the slave rotor is not actively controlled in the conventional master/slave control method, unwanted oscillations occur when the machine is subjected to torque unbalances. Contrary to more conventional commutation strategies, both phase windings of the machine are switched on during specific intervals such that these oscillations are dampened with limited influence on the master. A dynamic model of the machine is verified by simulations and experimental measurements. The commutation scheme is validated for constant current operation as well as in conjuction with a PI speed controller by means of simulations.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Asymmetrical Rewound Six-Phase Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Machines
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of four permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance machines (PMaSynRM) with different winding configurations named as reference machine (three-phase star-connected winding), motor 1 (asymmetrical six-phase winding), motor 2 (symmetrical six-phase winding) and motor 3 (rewound five-phase winding). Four identical stators and one rotor were used to construct the four machines using the same copper volume as much as possible. The performance comparison has been conducted using Ansys Maxwell transient simulations for the healthy and for a fault case with one-phase open. At health case and rated condition, Motor 1 offers the superior performance where it has the lowest torque ripple, which is 21% lower than the reference machine. Moreover, it has 4.48% higher average torque and 0.2% higher efficiency than the reference machine. At fault case, Motor 1 provides the highest average torque, 66.56% higher than the reference machine, and 65.85% lower torque ripple. Motor 2 has the lowest torque ripple in the failure situation, 67.37% lower than the reference machine and 61.41% more average torque. Motor 3 offers 53.3% less torque ripple and 54.77% more average torque.
