These results on motor 1, 2 and 3 show that their changes in the stator lead to a huge decrease in torque ripple in case of an open-phase fault, compared to the reference motor.

articleTitle: Analysis of Unbalanced Magnetic Force in DC-Biased Current Vernier Reluctance Machines with Odd Rotor Pole Number
abstract: In this paper, the unbalanced magnetic force (UMF) in flux-modulation machines is studied using DC-biased current vernier reluctance machine as an example. The equations for UMF and each harmonic component of the air-gap flux density are derived. The correctness of the proposed equations is validated by comparing the 12/7 and 12/11 machines of DC-biased current vernier reluctance machines. Then, the influence of motor structural parameters on UMF is investigated through response surface methodology. Finally, the optimization results for the 12/7 machine are shown.

articleTitle: Parametric Analysis of a Double-Stator Single-Rotor Coreless Axial Flux Machine
abstract: This paper presents a parametric study of the double-stator single-rotor coreless axial flux machine, based on analytical modeling. This novel approach is based on calculating the no-load peak flux density produced by a single magnet and then assuming a cosine function of the 3D field distribution, so that the flux linkage can be calculated with integration. This permits a straightforward comparison with other machine topologies using conventional analytical equations. The model is firstly investigated for no-load conditions using the finite element method and experiments over a prototype, showing good agreement. Then a parametric study is conducted in order to validate the model in different machine designs, focusing on resultant torque density and efficiency. These performance indicators are of the same order of magnitude that previous values of some transverse flux machines and axial flux machines in the literature.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Linear Double-Stack Scattered Permanent Magnet Flux Switching Motor
abstract: Wave energy can be implemented by the development of low speed linear generators. For integration into devices with corrosion and fouling protection, they are likely to need high magnetic gaps. This gives a set of unique requirements for linear electrical machine design. In this study, three flux-switching type linear machines are compared, a single magnet per pole version, a dispositioned permanent magnet version and a biased flux topology. The suggested topologies are tailor-designed to operate at a low speed of O.5m/ s, determined by the wave speed, and feature a magnetic gap of 3mm, this is necessitated by the intention to integrate the machine into the wave energy converter, addressing the need for sealing and encapsulation requirements. In conventional flux-switching PM machines, since the PMs are wrapped with the armature winding, thermal management of PMs is not possible, and consequently, the demagnetization of the PMs is more probable. In the proposed flux-switching with dispositioned permanent magnets (FSDPM) topology, thanks to the dispositioned PMs, the PMs are protected from demagnetization. In the proposed inter-modular permanent magnet (IMPM) structure, the PMs are placed between neighbouring E-modules and are not wrapped with armature windings, so the PMs are far from the heating source and are completely protected from demagnetization. The presented topologies are optimized using a multi-objective genetic algorithm to obtain structures that offer the best characteristics in terms of thrust force and force ripple. The optimized structures are simulated using 2D finite element method (FEM), and the no-load and full-load performances of the presented topologies are obtained and compared in several aspects. It is suggested that the version with the distributed magnets results in a 10% increase in the force capability of these machines.

articleTitle: Flux Density Evaluation of Dual-Core Phase Shifting Transformer in Normal Operating Conditions
abstract: Phase shifting transformer (PST) are a robust solution for governing the power flow on ac networks. Although this technology has mainly been deployed on the Italian 400 kV network, Terna (the Italian Transmission System Operator) also detect their need on the 230 kV network. Due to the requested large phase shift angles up to ±35° and rated power up to 650 MVA, a detailed analysis has been carried out to investigate the expected winding voltages as a function of load power factor, in order to anticipate possible unsafe operation in new planned 230 kV PSTs. The duality principle has been applied and, therefore, the electromagnetic equivalent circuit has been implemented in ATP-EMTP. The paper deals with the evaluation of the expected winding voltage of a dual-core PST both in buck and boost mode as a function of load power factor in normal operating condition, i.e. with the core not in saturation

articleTitle: Analytical Model of a High Frequency Rotary Transformer in Non-Resonant Topologies
abstract: This paper provides a detailed analysis of the behavior of a high frequency rotary transformer that supplies the excitation winding of a prototype electrically excited synchronous motor. This work includes the study of two different system topologies carried out through an analytical model, finite element analysis and experimental tests: the former is the standard model that should be used on an electric drive, the latter presents a capacitor connected in parallel to the load branch. The paper highlights the impact of the air gap width between the two cores of the transformer on its performance and provides recommendations for the design of high-performance rotary transformer.

articleTitle: Ground Fault Detection and Faulty Electric Machine Recognition in Parallel-Connected Variable Speed Drives
abstract: Variable Speed Drives (VSD) are widely implemented in industrial facilities in order to execute controlled processes. However, the use of pulsed voltage waves used for their feeding causes accelerated aging and higher risks of ground faults. In this matter, conventional protection relays against ground faults do not work properly due to the inverter high frequency components emissions incurring in a loss of selectivity. Additionally, in the industrial processes and machinery, multiple motors are often connected in parallel to the same inverter, which enhance the difficulty of discerning the fault. In this paper, a ground fault detection method for variable speed drives with several electric machines (EM) parallel-connected to the same inverter is proposed. The method uses a high value grounding resistor in the DC midpoint of the converter to detect the fault, discern the faulty phase of the AC side which has the fault and recognize the EM in fault. The method is supported by commutated capacitors that are used to vary the features of the leakage current measured in the grounding resistor, obtaining different features when the capacitor is connected in the faulty motor. To validate the methodology, some simulations were conducted in Matlab-Simulink achieving promising results.

articleTitle: Topology Analysis of Electric Machines for a Specific Mission Profile in Aviation Applications
abstract: In this paper, the required process for the electromagnetic design of electrical machines used in electric air-craft for a specific mission profile is exhibited. In the mission profile, 4.4 MW of power is required for the aircraft takeoff. The flight should cover 1500 km and be supplied fully with electrical energy. After analyzing the possible machine topologies through theoretical equations for covering the takeoff power, two different motor topologies were chosen for simulation in a FEM software. Multiple crucial electromagnetic and thermal boundary conditions were investigated in both topologies, and the geometry parameters of the topology that could fulfill these conditions were optimized. Since the outer stator diameter of the electrical machines is limited by the propeller diameter, the airgap diameter has been set to a constant value, and other design variables were changed within a defined range to achieve maximized power using “Quadratic response surface” optimization.

articleTitle: Suppression of Vibration in PMSM Caused by Time-Varying Load for Reciprocating Compressor
abstract: This paper deals with the vibration characteristics of permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) when there is time-varying load generated in the reciprocating compressor. As the reciprocating mechanism is necessary for compressing the refrigerant, the time-varying load torque is inevitable in compressor. However, this load torque affects to the system dynamics such as the speed fluctuation. These speed ripple cause unexpected vibration characteristics because they induce sideband components in the time harmonics of the electromagnetic force of PMSM. Therefore, we analyzed the vibration characteristics of PMSM according to time harmonics variation and conduct a study to suppress sideband vibration by adopting harmonic current injection method.

articleTitle: Handling Torque Constraint in Electric Machine Optimization for Variable Speed Noise Reduction
abstract: The problem of handling the torque conservation constraint during a multi-objective optimization of the magnetic noise radiated, at variable speed, by a 48 stator slots and 8 poles, Toyota Prius 2004 based electrical machine is addressed. Managing the torque conservation as a constraint of the optimization algorithm leads to a highly constrained problem. Handling the torque conservation by setting a torque maximization objective to the optimization results in a larger the three-dimensional space of solutions to be browsed. In both cases, poor optimization performances are reached. A compromise is found by guarantying the torque conservation through the combination of a relaxed optimization constraint and torque maximization objective.

articleTitle: Influence of Moisture on the Frequency Response Analysis of Poles of Synchronous Machines
abstract: Frequency Response Analysis (FRA) is a well-established technique for the condition monitoring of power transformers. The use of FRA for rotating electrical machines is nowadays a prominent research area. In previous works, the use of FRA for synchronous machine field winding diagnostics has been studied, but some key factors still remain uncertain in this application. The moisture content is one of the uncertainty factors that could, a priori, be envisaged as potentially influential. Therefore, the influence of moisture content on the FRA response of poles of synchronous machines is addressed in this paper. For this purpose, numerous experimental tests have been carried out on an extracted pole of a 40-MVA hydro-generator, with different moisture contents. The main contribution of this work is to prove that, in contrast to what occurs in ordinary insulation testing, the moisture content does not have a significant influence on the FRA response of the pole, discarding this method for moisture diagnostics.

articleTitle: Design of Hybrid Magnet IPM Machine for Traction Applications
abstract: This work proposes a hybrid permanent magnet material based synchronous machine design, combining the advantages of rare-earth free iron nitride magnets with rare earth magnets. The primary goal of the work is to propose a solution for automotive applications for a passenger car vehicle, capable of reaching the required performance and withstanding active short-circuit events without significant irreversible demagnetization. The study also aims to minimize the content of expensive and climate intensive rare-earth permanent magnet. The proposed design has a reduction of 70 % of the rare-earth materials content, without performance degradation. The cost and performance of the proposed design are compared to a benchmark machine with rare earth permanent magnets.

articleTitle: Innovative Rotor Winding Geometry for Synchronous Machine By Means of Additive Manufacturing
abstract: This paper presents an innovative optimized rotor winding for an electrically excited synchronous motor by means of additive manufacturing (AM). The new coil geometry was designed with the purpose of maximizing the filling factor keeping the cross section area of the conductors constant as only constrain in the geometry definition. The proposed solution allow to increase the machine torque density for the same rotor Joule losses or to increase the efficiency of the machine for the same output torque. Then a fluid pole shaping was study to reduce the mechanical stresses in the most critical points taking advantage of the fact that with AM the windings can be design following any kind of theet profile.

articleTitle: Optimization and Comparative Analysis of Magnet Shapes in 5-MW PM Vernier Motors for Marine Propulsion
abstract: Permanent magnet (PM) motors are increasingly used in high-power applications such as marine propulsion systems, where their exceptional torque density and efficiency are paramount. The configuration of PMs significantly affects the motor's performance and cost, making it a key design consideration. This study focuses on the design, optimization, and comprehensive comparative analysis of PM Vernier motors (PMVMs), specifically designed for a 5-MW marine propulsion system-a power level previously unexplored for Vernier motors. It examines four distinct magnet shapes: surface-mounted, spoke array, V-shape, and U-shape. Utilizing a Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) optimization algorithm, the study aims to minimize mass and cost. The optimally chosen models are then extensively compared, focusing on their cost and electromagnetic attributes, including airgap flux density, back-EMF, torque, power factor, self-inductance, loss, efficiency, and force performance. The findings underscore the significant role of magnet shape in enhancing the performance and total mass of high-power PMVMs, providing critical insights for the advancement of cost-effective and high-performing electric propulsion systems.

articleTitle: Effect of Rotor Step Skew on the Demagnetization Ratio of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
abstract: This contribution investigates the effect of a rotor step skew on the demagnetization ratio of internal permanent magnet synchronous machines. During the design of an electrical machine for an automotive traction drive different requirements such as torque ripple, cost targets, torque and power density need to be considered. Beyond this the reduction of heavy rare earth content is a current challenge to reduce the environmental footprint. A promising way to achieve the goals, is to reduce the magnetic field load on the permanent magnets and therefore the necessary coercivity, which is linked to the heavy rare earth content. To prevent partial demagnetization and decrease additional margins on the coercivity the consideration of side effects and local phenomena inside the electrical machine is essential. This paper shows that in case of a rotor step skew the effects in the transition area between the segments are important for the local demagnetization behavior of the permanent magnets. In a case study different skew variants are investigated and it is shown that 3-D finite element simulations are inevitable to consider these effects.

articleTitle: A Study on a Compact High-Efficiency Integrated Motor Using Layered Coil Ends and a Quadruple Inverter
abstract: In recent years, it has been an urgent need to develop smaller and more efficient electric vehicle (EV) power units and integrating the motor and the inverter into a unit is attracting attention as a solution. In this research, we propose a integrated unit that is smaller and more efficient than conventional ones by using layered coil end. The proposed motor is based on a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with 8 poles and 48 slots, and by using full-pitch concentric winding in 4-parallels and 4-inverters, it is possible to achieve improving efficiency, shortened coil ends, and fault tolerance.

articleTitle: Efficiency Improvement in Surface Mounted PMSM by Appropriate Management of Both Fundamental and Switching Frequency Iron Losses
abstract: The paper develops a particular methodology for modeling iron losses in inverter fed Surface mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (SPMSM), due to both fundamental and switching frequency iron losses. It introduces distinct variable lumped parameter equivalent circuit models for the fundamental and switching frequency, respectively, depending on the supply waveform and operating point conditions, evaluated through Finite Element Analysis (FEA). The proposed modeling procedure has been validated by measurements in a constructed drive system of a prototype vehicle, which participated successfully in an international competition for energy efficiency in transportation.

articleTitle: Slot Wedges with Integrated Grounded Electrodes for Suppression of Inverter-Induced Bearing Currents
abstract: Reliable operation of electric motors is vital for industrial applications. Yet bearing currents pose significant threats to their efficiency and longevity. Parasitic electrical currents, particularly prevalent in modern machines powered by advanced frequency converters, lead to various detrimental effects including overheating, increased vibration, and premature bearing failure. To address this issue, various countermeasures have been explored, with strategies targeting both the inverter and machine sides. Among these, the Grounded Electrodes approach and Winding Placement approach have proven promising in mitigating bearing currents. However, challenges such as complexity and practical implementation hinder widespread adoption of the technology. In this paper, a novel method integrating grounded electrodes into slot wedges is proposed, aiming to enhance practical applicability while maintaining efficacy. Numerical evaluations demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach compared to other methods, showing its potential to improve the reliability of electric machines by reducing the risk of bearing currents occurrence.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of High Performance Flux Reversal Motor with Cross-Pole Shape Stator
abstract: This paper designed and analysis of a high-performance flux reversal motor with cross-pole shape stator. Comparing with the conventional flux reversal machines (FRMs), the proposed FRM used fewer permanent magnets material to prevent magnetic saturation and enhanced torque density. Also, with proper design of the cross-pole shape stator that can tremendously reduce eddy current loss in permanent magnets (PMs) and increase motor efficiency, this paper shows an optimized design of cross-pole FRM and analyzed some important characteristics with 3D-FEM. Last part of this paper shows performance test process and results with proposed FRM prototype.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Double- and Single-Rotor Wound-Field Flux Switching Machines with Concentrated and Toroidal Windings
abstract: Wound-field flux switching machines (WFFSMs) have gained attention lately due to their robust construction, brushless operation and high torque density performance comparable to permanent magnet machines. However, conventional WFFSMs suffer from issues such as increased copper losses, low fault tolerance and reduced efficiency. In this study, double-rotor (DR) and single-rotor (SR) configurations of the WFFSM, with concentrated field windings and toroidal armature windings, are presented and their electromagnetic performance evaluated using the finite element analysis (FEA) technique. The no-load characteristics such as airgap flux density, flux linkage, back-EMF and cogging torque, as well as on-load and overload performance, including electromagnetic torque, torque ripple, efficiency and power factor are performed. The results show that the DR machine exhibits higher torque density and efficiency compared to the SR machines. The findings of this study give an indication into the influence of rotor topology and winding configuration on the electromagnetic performance of WFFSMs for high torque density applications.

articleTitle: Rotor Optimization of a Synchronous Reluctance Machine for Railway Applications
abstract: This article presents a design optimization strategy of a synchronous reluctance motor for railway applications, aimed at finding a trade-off solution among selected performance metrics in different operating points. The methodology consists in deriving, via finite element analysis, the machine fluxes-currents relationships required for calculating the torque-speed curve. Consequently, the trajectories relative to the main control strategies in the d-q axes reference frame are derived to obtain the torque-speed characteristic. By varying the rotor layout only, an optimisation is carried out by analysing two relevant operating points in the torque speed characteristic, i.e. rated torque - base speed point and the transition point between flux weakening and maximum-torque-per-voltage operations. Results reveal a clear trade-off among these performance indexes underlining the importance of a multi-objective design approach.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Hybrid PM Arrangement of RWAFPM Motor Considering Irreversible Demagnetization
abstract: In recent times, there has been a notable focus on emerging configurations of Permanent Magnet (PM) motors. However, these newly introduced PM motors lack maturity in their design and encounter various challenges from different angles. Consequently, it is imperative to establish a unified design methodology to address these limitations. One of these newly introduced PM machines is the Ring Winding Axial Flux PM (RWAFPM) motor. This motor is severely vulnerable to Irreversible Demagnetization (ID) at high temperatures. This paper aims to propose a resolution to mitigate this specific problem. In this paper, first a hybrid PM arrangement has been introduced for RWAFPM motor to minimize the risk of ID as well as the mass of the rare earth PM materials. Then, an algorithm to accurately consider the ID in the Finite Element Method (FEM) analysis of the RWAFPM motor has been introduced. Finally, a Design of Experiment (DOE)- based optimization algorithm has been implemented to improve the torque profile of the RWAFPM motor as well as to reduce the risk of ID.

articleTitle: A Study on Electrical Stress Distribution of Racetrack Coils Used in Ironless Linear Actuators with a Hybrid Modeling Approach
abstract: This study introduces a comprehensive model for racetrack coils capable of calculating the voltage distribution across their turns when subjected to fast rising voltage pulses. The coil is treated as a multiconductor transmission line, and the values of self and mutual impedances between the turns, as well as the inter-turn capacitances, are determined through finite element analysis and a physical model, respectively. The proposed framework is an accurate yet flexible tool for investigating the electrical behavior of air core coils with a high number of turns. It is validated using a prototype racetrack coil, demonstrating a reasonable level of accuracy. The results reveal that exciting the coil with fast rising voltage pulses causes enhanced over-voltages across some turns, directly impacting both the main and turn insulation in the coil. Additionally, it is observed that not only does the magnitude of the experienced overvoltage change with frequency, but its location may also vary. The developed model holds the potential to facilitate the design of a reliable insulation system for racetrack coils by predicting the electrical stresses they may encounter.

articleTitle: Comparison of Unbalance Control for High-Speed Active Magnetic Bearing System
abstract: Motors equipped with active magnetic bearing (AMB) systems need to cope with synchronous vibration problems caused by rotor mass unbalance at high speeds. This paper presents a comparative analysis between synchronous displacement suppression and synchronous current suppression strategies applied to a high-speed permanent magnet synchronous machine (HSPMSM). In the experiments, a phase-locked loop (PLL)-based estimator is utilized for precise rotor frequency detection. Rotor displacement and coil current are recorded and analyzed during AMB system operation, and the vibration acceleration of the motor casing is measured to evaluate the effectiveness of the two unbalance control strategies and identify the optimal conditions for applying each.

articleTitle: Reliable Detection of Non-Adjacent Broken Rotor Bars via the Analysis of the Zero-Sequence Flux
abstract: Rotor electrical faults may appear in induction motors. Typically, this fault evolves at a slow rate, thus making it prominent for early detection. However, it has been shown that multiple breakages at non-adjacent positions may not create signatures when the MCSA is applied. Although, the analysis of the stator current during the start-up transient can reveal this fault reliably, there are several industrial applications where the motors do not experience frequent start-ups making such methods obsolete. This paper addresses this need, that of detecting the fault reliably at steady state. The authors have utilized the zero-sequence stray flux and show that this methodology can identify the fault independently from the stator winding connection to the supply.

articleTitle: FEA Augmented Equivalent Circuit for Accurate Performance Prediction of Induction Machines
abstract: This paper describes a fast procedure for Induction Machines' variable speed performance computation. The approach is based on an improved equivalent circuit which utilizes lookup tables for the most critical parameters, computed through a combination of transient and magneto-static Finite Element simulations. The machine leakage inductance and rotor resistance are computed through a novel procedure which uses on-load transient simulations to derive the lookup tables as functions of the stator current and rotor frequency. The parametric analysis is optimized to maximize the accuracy of the equivalent circuit approach and minimize the simulation time. This method is adopted to compute the variable speed per- formance of a traction Induction Machine and the results are compared against a full Finite Element Analysis approach.

articleTitle: Effect of Eccentricity on PM Synchronous Machines With Different Rotor Geometries
abstract: In this study, we explore the influence of both static and dynamic eccentricity on PM synchronous machines featuring diverse rotor geometries through 2D Finite Element Analysis (FEA). We compare Surface Mounted (SPM), Interior Permanent Magnet (IPM), and Spoke PM machines, focusing on torque ripple, flux density, and back electromotive force (EMF). Our analysis reveals distinct responses among the rotor configurations to eccentric loading conditions, highlighting the Spoke rotor's heightened susceptibility due to flux concentration. Additionally, we examine the effects of eccentricity on flux density distribution, cogging torque, torque ripple, and back EMF unbalance, shedding light on critical performance metrics impacted by manufacturing imperfections. Insights from this research provide valuable guidance for selecting optimal rotor designs in practical applications, considering the implications of eccentricity on machine performance and reliability.

articleTitle: Robust Slot Harmonic Extraction in Varying Speed Operations
abstract: It is of great interest to extract motor slot harmonics for the purpose of studying motor efficiency, heat loss, torque ripple, as well as monitoring motor health condition and estimating motor speed. However, slot harmonics are typically of small magnitudes and of varying frequency in practice for motors operating at various conditions. In this paper, we propose a robust approach to extracting motor slot harmonics from the stator current when the motor is operating at varying speed conditions. First, a sparsity-driven method is proposed to estimate the frequency variation of slot harmonics due to varying operating speed. Then a singular value decomposition(SVD)-based method is used to extract the slot harmonics after compensating the corresponding frequency variation for each time window. In addition, the motor speed is also estimated according to the relationship between the slot harmonics and the motor speed. Experiments show that our method can extract slot harmonics from very noisy measurements and estimate motor speed with improved performance compared to the traditional method.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis of Magnetic Flux Density Spectrum Influence on Iron Losses in Electrical Machine Steel Sheets
abstract: This article proposes to experimentally study the relevance of a harmonic analysis for the calculation of iron losses in electrical machines magnetic sheets in order to improve the representativeness of their models. A test bench with a hysteresis-graph capable of generating waveforms and measuring the various iron losses induced on the magnetic samples is used. Sinusoidal waveforms of different frequencies, phases and amplitudes will be studied alone, then combined. Thus, it is possible to analyze the impact of complex waveforms on iron losses and to collect new data, which could be useful to subsequently establish iron loss models under complex induction spectrum in future, works.

articleTitle: Study of a Dual Stator PM Vernier Machine with Concentrated Windings and Low Torque Ripples
abstract: Dual stator PM Vernier machines can be an interesting solution to perform high torque and low speed application with high torque density. Such machines can suffer from cogging torque of significant magnitude. A solution to reduce it would be to phase shift a stator with respect to the other by a suitable angle. In the present paper, a study is conducted on a dual stator PM Vernier with fractional slot concentrated windings. The optimal phase shift angle is determined and thus, when applied on both stators, the performance of the obtained prototype is slightly reduced in terms of average torque but the torque ripples are highly reduced and the torque per mass and volume ratios are significantly improved.

articleTitle: Improved Electrical Braking of Synchronous Machines in Pumped Hydro Storage Plants
abstract: Pumped hydro storage plants (PHSP) are the leading solution to enable massive renewable energy penetration in power systems. In PHSP, the change of working mode of the synchronous machine (SM) from turbine mode to pump mode, or vice versa, requires disconnecting the machine from the grid, close the distributor, brake the machine through mechanical and/or electrical methods and start-up in the opposite rotation direction. In order to improve the electrical braking of SM in PHSP, in this paper it is proposed to short-circuit the high-voltage side of the main power transformer instead of the SM terminals, as it is normally done. Numerous experimental tests have been carried out to test the proposed method and to provide comparisons with respect to the conventional electrical braking method, obtaining satisfying results in terms of notable shortenings of the braking times.

articleTitle: Manufacturability Oriented Topology Optimization of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
abstract: A large number of studies in Topology Optimization (TO) have aimed to enhance Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (IPMSM) design. However, concerns persist regarding the manufacturability of the optimized designs, especially for simultaneously optimizing the geometry of permanent magnets (PMs) and back irons of the IPMSM. To improve the manufacturability of the optimized results of TO for the IPMSMs, this research proposes a manufacturing-focused TO approach for IPMSMs. Explicitly modelled basic components are initially developed and subsequently evolved through projective transformation and Boolean operations to generate novel topologies. Geometrical constraints are constructed and formulated to ensure the integrity of the iron in the optimized results. The numerical outcomes affirm the effectiveness of the proposed approach in substantially enhancing the performance parameter while preserving the manufacturability of the optimized designs.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured and Topology Optimized Heatsink for a Propulsion Motor
abstract: Additive manufacturing, used in conjunction with topology optimization, allows the realization of complex algorithmically generated geometries with improved physical characteristics. In this paper, these methods are used to enhance the performance of an electrical propulsion drive via improved cooling capabilities. An air-cooled heatsink is modelled, optimized, and additively manufactured, after which practical measurements are performed. Finally, comparisons to a similarly sized conventional heatsink are used to demonstrate the benefits and potential limitations of topology optimization and additive manufacturing in the field of electrical machines.

articleTitle: Sub-Optimal Flux-Weakening Control of Synchronous Reluctance Motors
abstract: This paper deals with the control of the synchronous reluctance motors in the flux-weakening operating range. Given the difficulties of implementing truly optimal control strategies, sub-optimal solutions, which require minimal parametrization and set-up efforts, are proposed and experienced. First, the proposed solutions are presented and discussed, considering the uncoupled, constant-inductances model of the motor in d-q components as an analytical basis. Then, the influence of the flux non-linearities is taken into account, considering a 75 kW motor designed for an electric vehicle as a test case. The deviation in performance compared with the computed maximum torque-to-current and maximum torque-to-voltage optimization criteria are outlined. Finally, experimental results are presented, demonstrating the practical implementation in a micro-controlled drive.

articleTitle: Performance Study of Surrogate Models for Large-Scale Optimization
abstract: As the role of simulation-based optimization grows in prominence for the design of advanced machines, its computation cost becomes a significant concern. Machine-learning-based surrogate models are expected to be a solution to solve the problem. Surrogate models need a certain amount of training, which requires simulation, such as Finite Element Analysis, to gain enough accuracy, which can be costly. The question is whether the use of surrogate models is cost-effective or not. To answer this question, we conducted numerical experiments. The study observed the initial acceleration of the optimization thanks to the surrogate model. However, the acceleration effect cannot be seen in the later stage, and the surrogate model misleads the optimization, preventing the gain of feasible solutions. This negative impact appears even in cases with a large amount of training.

articleTitle: Study on the Feasibility of Double Cage Induction Motors for Electromobility Applications
abstract: This research work focuses on the electromagnetic design of dual-cage induction motors for urban electric vehicles, leveraging local conditions for this purpose. Key load characteristics such as power, speed, and torque, along with mean values of supplied voltage and current, are established through simulations of the motor. Based on these variables, the sizing of four dual-cage motors is conducted, encompassing geometric measurements of the stator and rotor, an optimization of rotor slots to enhance starting characteristics, and cage material selection. To compare the proposed motors, finite element simulations are carried out, verifying the magnetic field distribution and current density from the designed models at different speeds. This comprehensive approach furnishes crucial insights to support decision-making in the design phase, evaluating the proposed motors' performance.

articleTitle: Impact of Model Fidelity on Control and Performance Analysis of Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
abstract: Amidst the rapid evolution of automotive drive systems, interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) remain the preferred option for their favourable performance qualities. This paper explores advanced mathematical models to accurately incorporate the nonlinear behaviour of IPMSMs. By coupling look-up tables generated from electromagnetic finite element analysis (FEA) with Simulink modelling techniques, the significance of considering factors such as cross-coupling, magnetic saturation, and spatial harmonics are explored to enhance model fidelity, ultimately enabling precise control algorithm development. Through simulation, the increased accuracy of including rotor position is validated by analyzing the torque ripple components. Experimental verification on an all-wheel drive (AWD) chassis dynamometer highlights the superior performance of the spatial flux-based model compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: A Magnetic Constant Torque Mechanism
abstract: This paper presents the design of a new type of magnetic constant torque mechanism. The constant torque is shown to be created over a prescribed ±65° stroke length and is shown to be highly uniform. The value of the constant torque is adjustable through the relative axial motion of the rotors. The constant torque is created using a simple magnet arrangement which makes use of the axial transverse-flux path of one rotor's magnetic field relative to the azimuthal field flow of the fixed secondary rotor. It is shown that the use of segmented magnets introduces torque ripple.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Hierarchical Optimization of Variable Flux Memory Machines with Diverse Operation Conditions
abstract: The design and optimization of variable flux memory (VFM) machines are investigated, with particular reference to the complicated permanent magnet (PM) rotor of the series-parallel structure with both variable PM (VPM) and constant PM (CPM). The multi-objective hierarchical optimization is developed to deal with the flexibly variable VPM MSs and diverse operation conditions. Aiming at the entire operation regions, the three-layer optimization with genetic algorithm is employed, and the different operations with diverse VPM MSs are included. The torque capability, electromagnetic efficiency, and pulsating torque during flux regulation are all optimized, whilst the unintentional demagnetizations are considered. A case study is conducted to clarify the optimization process and validate the effectiveness. The optimal cases with high maximum torque, low iron loss, and low pulsating torque can be obtained with good reliability and high accuracy.

articleTitle: Multipolar Halbach Bonded PM Rotors: Comprehensive Experimental Analysis of Non-Ideal Field Distributions and Manufacturing Imperfections
abstract: Halbach magnetized bonded rotors are widely employed for PM brushless AC machines across different industries and applications because of the sinusoidal airgap field distri-bution, high airgap flux density and no need for back iron yoke. The compression and injection bonding of the magnetic material can be done while a pre-orienting magnetic field is applied to enhance the fundamental field distribution, making the material an-isotropic. This paper analyzes field distribution measurements of several different multi-pole halbach rotors with bonded magnet rings or discs. It is shown how non-ideal pre-orienting/magnetization combined with the not sufficient PM thickness can cause harmonic presence in the field distribution. Furthermore, imperfections due the injection process also cause non-negligible harmonic presence and pole unbalance.

articleTitle: An Interpolation Based Meshed Magnetic Equivalent Circuit for Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
abstract: This article proposes a new modeling approach for V-shaped interior permanent magnet synchronous motors (IPMSMs) using Lagrange interpolation in mesh-based magnetic equivalent circuits (MECs). The method divides each MEC block in the air gap into several child angles, interpolating flux densities and scalar potentials to ensure smooth induced voltages and torque waveforms. The article introduces a new meshed magnetic equivalent (M-MEC) circuit model, which can be used for IPMSMs of any shape. The M-MEC model achieves an error of less than 5% for all electromagnetic parameters and is 13 times faster than finite element models. This innovative technique is suitable for various applications requiring accurate electromagnetic parameter predictions for different geometry and loading conditions compared to traditional MEC models.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Linear-Rotary Permanent Magnet Motor with Orthogonal Windings
abstract: A linear-rotary permanent magnet motor (LRPMM) is investigated, which can produce rotary, linear, and helical motion of the mover. It consists of a primary with stator core having circumferential and axial slots and two orthogonal rotary and linear windings, and a secondary with alternatingly arranged permanent magnets and mover core. First, 3-D finite element models of LRPMM are established to investigate and optimize the detent force during linear motion. Second, the electromagnetic performances under different degrees of freedom are calculated and analyzed. Finally, the force performance of LRPMM under helical motion is mainly focused since the linear magnetic field and rotary magnetic field exist in same iron core. After the impact of the shared magnetic circuit is analyzed, it is shown that the iron core has saturation problem, and then the force performance is lowered. The results can provide reference for further optimization of magnetic circuit design.

articleTitle: A Method for Modelling High Frequency Effects in Electrical Machine Windings for the Use in Circuit Simulation Programmes
abstract: In this paper, a method for modelling high frequency effects in electrical machine windings using an equivalent circuit model is presented. The parameters for modelling are derived from finite element (FE) calculations to predict a system behaviour. The equivalent circuit model is prepared for use in circuit simulation programmes like LTSpice. The goal is, to perform system simulations taking into account interactions between the inverter, transmission line and electrical machine winding. The proposed method enables the consideration of the influence of temperature and humidity in perspective. The results of the model applied on the winding of a transverse flux machine are validated by measurements. The influence of the temperature on the impedance of the machine winding is experimentally presented.

articleTitle: Six-State Angle Control Strategy for Doubly Salient Electromagnetic Generator System Based on Active Rectifier
abstract: In this paper, to ensure stable and safe operation of the doubly salient electromagnetic generator (DSEG) system over the wider load range, while further increasing the output power, the six-state angle control (SSAC) strategy for the active rectifier (AR) is proposed. The SSAC strategy controls the bridge arm where the armature windings are about to change phase, being centered on the six natural phase change points of back- electromotive force (EMF) in one electrical cycle of the DSEG, and controls the arm corresponding to the phase winding that is about to change phase conduction. Phase is brought forward for conduction and energy storage. Analyze and compare the proposed SSAC strategy, the conventional angular position control (APC), and advanced angle control (AAC) strategy. The output power of SSAC is significantly improved compared with that of other strategies for AR. The feasibility and superior performances of the proposed strategy are validated by the experiment results.

articleTitle: Pressure Controller Design in Electrified Hydraulics for Off-Highway Machinery
abstract: A pressure control loop for hydraulic systems powered by a fixed-displacement pump was analyzed, both theoretically and by means of simulations, and tested on a mobile construction crane. Dynamics of the speed control loop is included in the analysis. A comparison with a fixed-speed system was performed. Absorbed energy during a lifting-lowering cycle was reduced by approximately 10 % without introducing any hardware modification, except for the pressure transducers.

articleTitle: A Consideration of Continuous Conduction Mode of Switched Reluctance Motors Based on Vector Control Method
abstract: This paper discusses how to consider and control the continuous conduction mode (CCM) of Switched reluctance motors. Switched reluctance motors are suitable for high-speed rotation due to their rotor geometry, and it can maintain output power even at high-speeds by applying of CCM. However, the specific method of CCM has not been explained theoretically, but only experimentally. In this paper, a theoretical control method of CCM is investigated by using a mathematical model of vector control. It is found that the CCM can be interpreted as MTPV control by adjusting the ratios of negative d-axis current and zero phase current, and q-axis current and zero phase current under the vector control. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated by simulations.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Direct Drive Linear Motors: Tubular and Flat Permanent Magnet Vernier Machines
abstract: Direct drive linear machines are well known technology in industrial automation and for small linear actuators. When it comes to low-speed high-duty industrial applications the solutions out on the market are very rare and present many limitations. Vernier PM machines are very good candidates for this type of applications because of the high thrust density and efficiency. A comprehensive FEA performance comparison of different linear Vernier machine configurations including tubular and flat machines, different pole/slot combinations, permanent magnet placement is carried out in this paper. The best candidates are optimized electromagnetically and compared in terms of thrust density, efficiency, power factor, manufacturing aspects and cost to provide insight of the main trade-offs during the development phase.

articleTitle: A Design of Outer-Rotor Flux-Switching Motor with Segmental Rotors to Improve Torque Density
abstract: This paper presents the design study on high torque of the outer-rotor DC excited Flux-Switching Motor (OR-DCEFSM) with segmental rotors. The target is a torque of 100 Nm under a current density of 20 A/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, an outer diameter of 222 mm and an axial length of 70 mm. A 24/16 OR-DCEFSM is optimized and analyzed by using finite elemental method. The design process of the OR-DCEFSM with segmental rotors and simulation results are reported. After optimization, it is found that a torque of 119 Nm is possible at the current density of 20 A/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It is also found that the torque-volume density of 43.9 Nm/L. These results are comparable with permanent magnet synchronous motors.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Cost-effective E-Machines for Traction: A Case Study of 150kW V-shaped PMSM
abstract: With the increasing cost of raw materials used in electric machines, designing cost-effective machines has become a necessity for the industry. In this paper, we present a strategy that involves the use of aggressive cooling techniques and the reduction of costly rare earth materials. The V-shaped PMSM, widely used in electric vehicles, is selected for this study. Two solutions are proposed: a) a machine with water-jacket cooling and NdFeB magnets (with Dysprosium), and b) a machine with slot pipe cooling and Dysprosium-free NdFeB magnets. Both machines are optimized based on electric vehicle specifications, with cost, losses, and volume considered as objectives. The optimization results reveal that solution (b) achieves a power density of 46 kW/L and up to 40% reduction in the machine's raw materials cost compared to solution (a).

articleTitle: Design Aspects of Winding for Variable Reluctance Resolver
abstract: The paper considers the winding arrangement of variable reluctance resolvers (VR). Basic principles of the winding distributions are analyzed, and an advanced approach in the winding design is developed. The paper proposes the optimal combinations of the following parameters: number of stator teeth, number of saliency pitches (or pole pairs on the motor side), and winding distribution. The results are presented in a table, which makes it practical to select the appropriate number of stator teeth and winding arrangement for the case with a certain number of saliency pitches.

articleTitle: 2-D FEA Design of a Low-Cost and Self-Powered Sin/Cos Sensor
abstract: Diagnostic and prognostic became key activities in industry 4.0. This paper presents the design and validation of a low-cost and self-powered sensor for condition monitoring of a mechanical speed variator. This sensor can be easily coupled with commercial sin/cos sensors and used to plan a predictive maintenance policy. Specifically to the speed variator, thanks to the two sin/cos sensors mounted on the two shafts, the elasto-plastic deformation of the entire kinematic system can be estimated and predictive maintenance can be scheduled.

articleTitle: Experimental Comparison of Dual-Winding Configurations in Induction Motors Under Two Different Types of Supply Voltage Unbalance
abstract: This paper experimentally assesses the three-phase squirrel-cage induction motor tolerance to supply voltage unbalance for different dual-winding configurations, focusing on the phase current unbalance rate, the maximum amplitude of phase currents, and the per-slot stator conduction losses. Ten different dual-winding configurations were tested in an induction motor with externally reconfigurable windings at different load conditions under supply voltage unbalance resulting from increasing the resistance of one line between the power supply and the motor, which emulates a defective contact in the contactors and/or in the motor terminals. These results are compared to those obtained in previous experiments where the voltage unbalance was obtained by lowering the amplitude of one line-to-neutral voltage. The dual-winding configurations experimentally tested included the star-series and delta-series connection modes, with different angular displacements between the two partial windings, namely, 0, 20, 40, 60, and 240 electrical degrees. The experiments that were conducted allowed the identification of the dual-winding configuration, which led to the lowest per-slot per-unit conduction losses under the considered type of supply voltage unbalance. Compared to the commonly used delta- or star-connected windings, the best-identified dual-winding configuration may provide more motor tolerance to supply voltage unbalance, ultimately extending the service life of the stator winding. As far as the authors know, it is the first time such a study has been conducted.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Effect of Flux Concentration on Flux Switching Machines
abstract: Biased-flux topologies are a new type of stator permanent magnet (PM) machine that their PM protection and smooth torque profile have a promising performance index over other conventional topologies. In this paper, a new biased-flux PM motor is presented so that increases the torque density, power factor, and efficiency. The proposed structure not only has a biased operating point for each armature pole, but also the entire modules keep the same magnetization. This DC offset is mathematically analyzed to see how the flux density in the air gap is increased. The no-load and full-load operations are studied in terms of cogging torque, flux density, flux line, torque profiles, and overload capability. Moreover, a complete comparison has been made between the proposed structure and the inter-modular permanent magnet (IMPM) motor. The magnetic stresses on the PMs are studied to assess the demagnetization risks. It is been explained how the physical placement of the PMs has resulted in the superiority of the proposed IMPM motor. Finally, to verify the demagnetization assessment, a thermal investigation is conducted which shows that the proposed structure also operates in a thermally safe zone.

articleTitle: A Lumpted Parameter Thermal Model for Variable Flux Reluctance Machine Considering Relative Position of DC and AC Windings
abstract: Similar to other wound field flux modulation machines, the variable flux reluctance machine (VFRM) features a dual-salient pole structure. The DC winding and AC windings of the VFRM are both located on the same stator tooth. This paper proposes a lump parameter thermal model (LPTM) for the VFRM for the first time. The influence of the relative position of DC winding and AC windings on steady-state temperatures are considered. This study establishes a finite element analysis (FEA) model for the VFRM and compares it with the steady-state thermal simulation results obtained from the LPTM. Under different current densities, the maximum absolute error between the FEA and LPTM predicted temperatures for the DC winding is 2.71°C, and for the AC winding is 4.63°C.

articleTitle: Medium Voltage Sensorless Induction Motor Drive for Subsea Applications
abstract: In this paper, a MV induction motor drive for submarine oil pump applications is considered. The motor is usually connected to the inverter drive with a cable of tens of kilometres and sensorless control is a must since sensors can be replaced only with the use of submarine robots. For these reasons, instability phenomena can occur. To overcome these issues, a new control is proposed in this study, involving a compensated sensorless FOC algorithm based on the Luenberger observer. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is tested with simulations considering the MV drive parameters. Moreover, experimental tests are carried out on a small scale LV prototype.

articleTitle: Flux Weakening and Flux Strengthening Capabilities of Rotary Hybrid Excited Flux Switching Generator for Wave Energy Applications
abstract: The article presents a Hybrid Excited Flux Switching direct drive generator for wave energy applications. Flux Switching Generator has been proposed because of its variable speed capability and internal magnetic gearing effect making it one of the best candidates for direct drive applications. Hybrid excitation is considered with a Ferrite Magnet in the outer stator and a DC excitation in the inner stator. The rotor is in the form of a partition iron located between the two stators. Wave energy is the most abundant source of energy but among many problems most crucial one with harvesting the energy is the variable speed of the wave. An abrupt change in the speed required either a manual braking system or a technique to control the flux generation thereby the voltage and power generation. The presence of DC excitation provides advantages of weakening and strengthening flux according to the condition's requirements. Flux Weakening and Strengthening capabilities of the HEFSG will be analyzed, and the effect of different pole combinations on the speed and the general performance of the generator will be discussed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Forces in an Air-Cored Superconducting Machine for Direct Drive Wind
abstract: High Temperature Superconducting (HTS) machines offer potential for mass reduction in high torque low speed generators for multi-MW direct drive wind turbines. A fully air-cored HTS machine eliminates the use of mass dense materials such as iron and permanent magnets, as well as eliminating the saturation constraint in the more conventional iron-cored topology. In order to provide flux focussing an array of rotor field HTS coils supported in non-magnetic material is proposed, similar to an electromagnetic Halbach Array. Magnetic fields within the coil arrays produce tangential and normal forces, which need to be known for the structural design. As the array is air-cored the Biot-Savart methods lends itself to easy calculation of the magnetic fields and force distribution. In this paper we present an initial study into these forces to provide an understanding of the force distribution, and present simulation results for a 2-pole pair array with different coil arrangements within the array.

articleTitle: The Development and Application of Impingement Jet Cooling in the Small Traction Synchronous Machine with Permanent Magnets
abstract: The current research primarily focuses on minimizing machine dimensions and enhancing their power density. This paper details the development of impingement cooling systems for small traction machines, which are utilized, for instance, in driving small trolleys where compact size must be maintained while maximizing the power and torque output of the electric machine. The study elaborates on the development, testing, and performance evaluation of impingement cooling, examining its efficacy relative to the pressure and temperature variations of the cooling medium. Heat transfer coefficients were determined to assess the cooling efficiency achieved under different operating conditions. The developed cooling system allowed the maximum current capability of winding to reach 14 times higher power output than the original air-cooling technique while keeping the temperature below 40°C.

articleTitle: Encoderless Field Oriented Control (FOC) with I-F Starting for a Super-High Speed SPMSM (125 krpm, 30 kW) Compressor Drive
abstract: Super-high speed centrifugal compressor drives in the tenth of kW and speeds up to 125 krpm are applied in various industries. Typically, surface PMSMs are used as motors due to their high torque density, high efficiency and gearbox-free operation. While a rich literature is dedicated to the design of SPMSMs for such applications, this paper concentrates on the encoderless control of such a drive (up to 125 krpm and 30 kW), considering the compressor load notable torque ripple. A combined I-f for starting to “fuse” with “active flux” based FOC, at zero id current, is proposed and documented with full size digital simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Machine Inductance Variation on Loss Minimization Control
abstract: The influence of inductance variation on Interior permanent magnet synchronous motor performance under loss minimization control is analyzed. Firstly, simplified and improved loss minimization control methods are introduced. Secondly, the influence of inductance variation on motor efficiency and maximum torque is investigated. The results show that the inductance variation has limited influence on motor efficiency, while its influence on maximum torque is more prominent. Finally, the efficiency and torque performance are compared in simulation and experiment for three different motors when different inductances are applied. An instructive conclusion is built to analyze the choice of inductance value when the motor inductance varies because of magnetic saturation.

articleTitle: Effect of Independent Interior and Exterior Tooth Tips in U-Shape Modular Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of independent tooth tips, interior and exterior, in U-shape core modular stator permanent magnet synchronous machines (MPMSM). Radial flux machines are considered with inner and outer rotor, 12 slots, 10 and 14-poles, tooth-coil windings, and surface mounted magnets. Each of the four machine variants analyzed have different stator and rotor dimensions, each one optimized to have a high torque density. A sensitivity analysis of the tooth tip's dimensions is made, and a subsequent optimization problem is applied on each machine variant, utilizing the particle swarm algorithm (PSO), maximizing average torque and minimizing ripple torque with the dimensions of the tooth tips as the workspace. The resulting optimized dimensions are illustrated and compared, showing that adding tooth tips can reduce the ripple torque in some cases and they are not necessarily symmetric.

articleTitle: Comparison of Gear-Drive and Direct-Drive Systems for In-Wheel Motors
abstract: This paper proposes a direct-drive system of in-wheel motors and discusses its superiority compared with a conventional gear-drive system. The proposed technology enables the installation of high-power motor into the wheel and more expansive interior and battery installation spaces, thus moving the world one step closer to a zero-emissions society. The new motor transmits the high drive force directly to the wheels, and its lightweight design with 40 Nm/kg torque density significantly limits the weight increase traditionally associated with in-wheel units. We have theoretically quantified that the developed direct-drive system is 10-30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> lighter than the gear drive system. Moreover, the direct-drive system rotates much lower rotation than the gear drive, which allows for immersion oil cooling within the motor without the significant increase in fluid friction loss. Measurement of the prototype demonstrated the maximum output torque of 960 Nm at 600 min<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and high cooling performance at 50 % load condition.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Ferrite-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motors for Traction Applications
abstract: The paper presents a feasibility study on Synchronous Reluctance motors with and without the assistance of ferrite permanent magnets in the field of traction application. Three prototypes with slightly different specification will be compared in terms of electromagnetic performance figures, considering the effect on key performance indicators of the initial design choices and constraints. An example of permanent magnet motor with rare-earth magnets is selected as reference, to enhance the pros and cons of the rare-earth-free solutions. Furthermore, the environmental impact of the four motors will be considered, both in general terms and through specific indicators.

articleTitle: Effect of Eccentricity on Vibration and Noise of External-Rotor PMSM
abstract: Rotor eccentricity is an inevitable issue in industrial applications, adding complexity to the analysis of vibration and noise in external-rotor (ER) permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). This paper conducts a quantitative calculation of the spectrum features related to vibration and noise in ER-PMSMs, the effect of different kinds of rotor eccentricity on the vibration and noise are revealed. Moreover, the effect of rotor eccentricity and Doppler effect on the noise of ER-PMSMs are also analyzed. Finally, all analyses are validated through finite element (FE) simulation and experimental results.

articleTitle: Influence of Inter-Turn Short Circuits on Clamp Parameters of a Nine-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
abstract: The reliability of electric drives is a significant topic in safety-critical applications. Approaches such as multi-phase machines are widely discussed. Additional fault detection and control in a fault scenario are essential in such systems. In support of these efforts, this publication shall exhibit the influence of the resistance and number of shorted turns on the current and torque behavior of a nine-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine. Two distinct effects are to be observed, dubbed as active and passive. Their influence on current and torque is shown using 2D finite element analysis simulation data.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Different Skewed Poles Schemes for a 160W Brushless DC Motor
abstract: The cogging torque of brushless DC motors is crucial for reducing torque ripple and improving the control accuracy of speed or position. In the literature on weakening cogging torque through skewed poles, the changes in the torque-speed characteristic brought by skewed poles are usually ignored. In this paper, for a 160W brushless DC motor, three skewed poles schemes are proposed based on upright aligned permanent magnet: offset 1/4 pole, offset 1/2 pole, and continuous skewed pole. Cogging torque and torque-speed characteristics of upright alignment and three skewed poles schemes are compared and analyzed by finite element analysis using MagNet software and prototype experiments. Among three skewed poles schemes, cogging torque of offset 1/4 pole is relatively small, and the change in speed with torque is relatively small.

articleTitle: Demagnetization Detection, Misdiagnosis and Impact in Permanent Magnet Generators
abstract: Permanent magnet generators are key electrical machines in remote renewables power applications. Their ability to operate in direct-drive condition together with high efficiency and modularity are just some of the reasons. However, they may experience faults that if undetected will evolve. It is therefore crucial to detect faults reliably to avoid catastrophic failures. This paper deals with the detection of demagnetization in direct-drive permanent magnet generators. The paper focuses on the application of various diagnostic methods and compares their detection capabilities. Moreover, the authors will investigate cases of false negative diagnostic alarms that lead to misdiagnosis.

articleTitle: Permanent Magnet Cogging Motor, from Concept to Prototype
abstract: This article presents a description of research that has led to the development of a new design permanent magnet machine. The machine is based on the operational principle of the transverse-flux machine (TFM). In the proposed solution, a core commonly used in radial flux machines was employed, significantly simplifying the construction of the TFM machine. This simultaneously reduces flux leakage and enhances the value of the developed electromagnetic torque. The article sequentially outlines the stages of research on the new design, ranging from analytical calculations through Finite Element Method (FEM) simulation to the construction of a machine prototype.

articleTitle: Training Scheme for Convolutional Neural Network Based Multiple Fault Classifier of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Under Variable Speed and Load Conditions
abstract: This paper introduces a novel methodology for training Convolutional Neural Network models to detect multiple faults in permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs). The proposed method aims to mitigate memory overloading and overfitting for a neural network. Within the framework, measured current and flux signals from a PMSM under variable speed condition in time domain are converted into spectrogram images using short-time Fourier transformation. The suggested algorithm can classify inter-turn short-circuit faults, local de-magnetization faults, and mixed-fault in PMSMs. The proposed scheme is validated using data from an in-house experimental setup.

articleTitle: An Experimental-based Circuit Model of Motor Stator Poles for Impedance Spectroscopy Analysis
abstract: Permanent magnet motors are subjected to a variety of stresses, such as thermal, mechanical, and electrical, depending on the application requirements. Those stresses may lead to progressive degradation of the motor components until a failure appears. However, it is to be noted that the inherent manufacturing tolerances have a strong role to play in the ageing mechanism because the various stresses will have a stronger impact on them. Stator faults are among the most serious faults in all electric motors due to their fast evolution to a catastrophic breakdown, while also being linked with the degradation and failure of the insulation system. This paper will aim to provide a detailed equivalent circuit of a permanent magnet motor's stator poles with mounted armature coils for impedance spectroscopy purposes. The experimentally derived model is a sensitive map to manufacturing weaknesses in the insulating materials and can be used for identifying different defects, thus improving the quality inspection procedure before the assembly of the motor. This procedure allows to exclude poles with weak insulation and therefore significantly increase the longevity and reliability of the motors.

articleTitle: Mechanical Design Considerations of a Light-Weight Rotor for Brushless Double Fed Machines
abstract: This paper presents an optimised mechanical design aimed at reducing the rotor mass of a Brushless Doubly-Fed Machine (BDFM). The focus is on the rotor back iron, identifying specific areas where iron materials can be removed without compromising the magnetic performance of the rotor. Mechanical stress and vibration analyses are conducted using the Finite Element (FE) method in Ansys software to evaluate the feasibility of the proposed design. The study is performed on a prototype D400 250-kW BDFM, showing that the rotor mass can be reduced by approximately 24% while maintaining acceptable electromagnetic and mechanical performance under rated operating conditions.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Automatic Design System for IPMSM with Variable Magnet Properties
abstract: Interior permanent magnet synchronous motors are highly valued in electric vehicles for their performance, efficiency, and reliability. Optimizing their design often requires time-consuming finite element analysis. Deep learning can accelerate the design of interior permanent magnet synchronous motor, providing a faster alternative to finite element analysis. This study proposes a deep learning model capable of handling various inputs and outputs, including permanent magnet properties and temperatures. This system allows efficient optimization across different rotor designs and conditions, with the benefit of multiple iterations after training.

articleTitle: Stator Shaping of the Novel Hexane-Type Stator Permanent Magnet Flux Switching Machine
abstract: A comparative performance analysis of the C-core, E-core and T-core variants of the novel hexane-type stator permanent magnet (HS-PMFSM) is presented in this study. Finite element analysis (FE A) is employed to evaluate electromagnetic performance under no-load and on-load conditions. The proposed HS-PMFSMs adopts a hexagonal stator shape to enable more compact design and heat dissipation compared to conventional circular stators. The no-load characteristics show the C-core produced the highest flux of 0.025 Wb but the on-load performance shows the E-core produced the highest torque of 5.95 N m. The E-core also displays least flux leakage and widest overload operating range in terms of power factor versus efficiency, power factor versus torque and power factor versus torque ripple tradeoffs, indicating greater flexibility and robustness of the three machines. Therefore, the effectiveness of the proposed FEA study leads to the ongoing development and testing of an experimental prototype based on the E-core design.

articleTitle: 3D Numerical Modeling of Displacement Due to Magnetostriction in Silicon Steel Laminated Core
abstract: To evaluate and reduce the noise generated in the laminated iron cores of transformers and motors, accurate displacement calculation due to magnetostriction is important. In this paper, the authors proposed a 3D numerical modeling method to calculate the displacement due to magnetostriction in the silicon steel laminated iron core using homogenization technique. The proposed method is applied to a silicon steel laminated core under alternating excitation of 50 Hz. The calculated displacements obtained from the homogenization method are compared with those of the real laminated core model for validation. Compared to the conventional homogenization method, a much better agreement is achieved.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Inter Turn Short Circuit Fault Detection of a Segmented SRM Based on Multi-Path Convolutional Neural Network and fCWT
abstract: This paper aims to propose a fault detection model for inter-turn short circuit faults in a Segmented Switched Reluctance Motor. To this end, a method is developed in the input of which the raw current signal of the motor is processed by the fast Continuous Wavelet Transform (fCWT) to generate the input matrix for the two-dimensional convolution layer. Compared with the conventional wavelet transforms, this method has proved to be considerably faster. The resulting matrix is input into a novel multi-path Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). This model uses a multi-path block which prevents the unintended elimination of crucial features for fault detection by using the feature map construction of the multi-path of layers. To evaluate this method, a six-phase SSRM is simulated using FEM simulation under healthy conditions and different levels of ITSC fault. Then, the current is acquired in a dataset and used for training and testing the model.

articleTitle: Reduction of Stator Tooth Magnetic Saturation in Permanent Magnet Machines with Single-Layer Fractional Slot Concentrated Windings
abstract: This paper investigates the phenomenon of alternating tooth magnetic saturation in a permanent magnet machine with single-layer fractional slot concentrated windings (FSCW). The reason behind the phenomenon is identified by analyzing the stator and rotor fields with a two-dimensional (2D) finite element model, focusing on the field harmonics. To improve the utilization of electric steel, it is proposed to employ a combination of unequal width teeth in the stator and flux barriers in the rotor yoke directly beneath the permanent magnets. This combination is found to successfully reduce the magnitude of subharmonics, reducing unproductive flux and significantly improving torque density while reducing the torque ripple.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Experimentally Deriving Thermal Parameters in Design of Electrical Machines for Short-Duty Transient Operation
abstract: This paper describes a methodology for experimentally deriving thermal parameters in design of electrical machines, with focus on, but not limited to short-duty transient operation. Here, all key stator-winding thermal resistances and capacitances, which can be directly derived from thermal tests, are considered. The proposed approach is based on the transient thermal step-change response for a test specimen/mottorete under test, where the heat transfer is well-defined and limited to a single path, e.g. a heat source (stator-winding body) to a heat sink (machine housing). Any imperfections like the heat flux leakage from the motorette body/test rig are considered and experimentally compensated for. A detailed description of the underpinning assumptions, test procedure, required instrumentation, measured data post-processing is provided and supplemented with several examples from hardware tests. Applicability and limitations of the methodology are also discussed. The presented work provides a novel standardised testing approach, where the measured data can be simply shared across different electrical machine designs, to provide a mean for accurate, time and resource effective design /assessment process.

articleTitle: Optimization of Printed Synchronous Reluctance Rotor Based on Bézier Curves
abstract: This paper deals with the optimization of a multi-barrier synchronous reluctance rotor, in which the flux barriers are parameterized using Bézier curves. With this type of modeling, it is possible to explore more complex geometries that can be realized with new additive manufacturing techniques. A two-step optimization based on the NSGA-II genetic algorithm is proposed in the paper. In the first part, barriers are optimized using a simplified analytical model. In the second part, the rotor geometry is optimized using finite element analysis. Finally, a more detailed investigation is performed to calculate the overall performance of the optimized solution and compare them with those of a previously manufactured prototype.

articleTitle: Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces Structure for Efficient Heat Dissipation in Motor Housings: A Convective Potential Analysis
abstract: With the advent of 3D printing, advanced geometries started replacing the conventional designs in electric machines. Various modified rotor, stator and coil designs are 3D printed to enhance the machine properties and minimize the losses but there are still some heat losses generated which can cause temperature rise inside the motor and disturb the stability of machine, unless this heat is removed from the machine properly. Motors use conventional housing with fins or cooling systems to remove this heat but it provides poor heat transfer and affects the performance of the motor. This paper focuses on developing Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces (TPMS) housing structures with varying heights, volume fractions and cell sizes to optimize heat management in the motor. TPMS provides heat dissipation in multiple directions as compared to conventional fin. They provide a large surface area to volume ratio, hence better heat dissipation & heat distribution within the structure, improving performance and saving material. Mathematical modeling and numerical simulations of these structures using Finite Volume Method are done, and results of each structure are investigated and compared. Comparison with another research work is also done to justify the results. Finally, an optimal structure is chosen to replace the original housing structure. Comparative analysis is done to study the improvement in properties. Results are compared with conventional housing. Complete heat analysis of the original and proposed design is presented. Heat distribution and propagation is carried out. Improved results and the future scope of the project is presented.

articleTitle: PDIV Modeling for Rectangular Wire Turn-to-Turn Insulation of Inverter-Fed Motors at Different Cruising Altitudes
abstract: This study develops a predictive model for partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) in turn-to-turn insulation of form-wound windings for inverter-fed motors considering a range of altitudes, from ground to cruise levels. Emphasis is placed on the application of rectangular insulated wires (i.e., edgewise insulated wires). Using Schumann's streamer inception criterion (SCSIC), the PDIV predictive model explores six distinct air pressures corresponding to altitudes: 1013 mbar (6.8 ft), 800 mbar (6.4k ft), 600 mbar (13.8k ft), 200 mbar (38.6k ft), 150 mbar (44.3k ft), and 100 mbar (51.8k ft). PDIV estimations are conducted under AC 50 Hz, unipolar positive (UP), and bipolar (BP) steep-fronted square waveform excitations, characterized by a switching frequency of 2.5 kHz, rise time of 80 ns, and pulse width duration of 100 μs. The PDIV model supports aerospace coil winding design by guiding wire geometry decisions, eliminating costly insulation experiments, and ensuring reliability at operational altitudes.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study on Different Motor Topologies Used in Passenger Car EV Segment
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study between different electrical machine topologies used in automotive segment.
