To this end, 52 laboratory tests are generated with different fault severities, loads, voltage unbalances and supply conditions. In each test, the amplitude of up to 19 harmonics is extracted, first to determine the most sensitive indicators in each group and then to compare them with each other. Finally, a critical discussion is provided, clarifying the best approach to take.

articleTitle: Rotor Stray Currents in Large Salient-Pole Generators
abstract: In this paper, we present an investigation of the presence and impact of rotor winding stray currents on large salient-pole generators. Field measurements taken on several large hydro-generators suggest that stray currents can have significant impacts on machine sensor operations; they can also lead to incorrect diagnostics and even failures. Moreover, the interpretation of interturn short circuit of the rotor pole winding using airgap flux probes appears not to be sufficiently sensitive to detect rotor pole short turns at this early stage. An explanation of stray current circulation in rotor pole windings during machine operation under interturn short circuit conditions is proposed. Finally, it is shown that rotor stray currents require further investigation and that a better understanding of them could assist in detecting rotor winding short circuits at an early stage and even contains critical information on machine operations. The experimental results presented suggest that our understanding of the impact of overvoltages generated by the excitation system due to the thyristors' turn-off recovery current and induced shaft voltage also requires further investigation as it may cause bearing failures and appears to have caused the malfunction of some airgap sensors.

articleTitle: High-Speed Electric Machine Frame Design Process Using Topology Optimization
abstract: High-speed electric machines have been developed for decades thanks to their high efficiency and power density. The problem with the development of high speed electrical machines is the long and iterative design process which is usually tailored to each machine. One part of the design process is the design of the frame, for which there has been no systematic process in the past. In this work, a design process was developed in which initial values and a target are used to create frame structures optimized for specific or maximized frequency. The developed design process utilizes topological optimization to generate optimal frame structures for high-speed electrical machines.

articleTitle: Analytical Electromagnetic Force of Vernier Permanent Magnet Machine Considering Stator-Tooth Dual Modulation Effects
abstract: Vernier permanent magnet machines (VPMM) utilize the magnetic gear transmission principle by modulating harmonics through stator teeth. This design characteristic leads to the presence of abundant magnetic field harmonics in the air gap, resulting in high electromagnetic force acting on the stator, which has a significant impact on the vibration performance of VPMM. However, stator teeth not only affect the electromagnetic forces by influencing the magnetic field, but also have modulation effects on higher-order electromagnetic forces. Therefore, the structure of stator teeth significantly impacts the overall electromagnetic forces. To further elucidate the relationship between the electromagnetic force and the stator teeth, this article develops an analytical method to analyze the dual modulation effect of electromagnetic force. So that we can easy to understand the impact of the motor structural changes on the magnetic field and electromagnetic force. Finally, the finite element analysis is conducted to verify the validity of the analytical calculation.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Thermal Digital Twin of a High Power Density Motor for Automotive Applications
abstract: A multiphysic Digital-Twin of a high power density electric motor for automotive applications is presented in this work, with the objective of real-time monitoring of critical temperatures of interest. The model includes electromagnetic, fluid-dynamic, and thermal effects. The models developed are described and, aiming to achieve reduced computational cost, the Model Order Reduction strategy is presented. This allows compatibility with an on-chip implementation, thus unlocking advanced and informed control strategies. Experimental validations demonstrate the accuracy and the feasibility of the multiphysic Digital-Twin.

articleTitle: Modelling Framework and Insights About a Novel Low-Velocity Segmented Linear Motor Design
abstract: A novel concept for a segmented linear interior-mounted permanent magnet motor is introduced. The favourable scaling properties of permanent magnet motors are exploited by making the stator and mover out of short tubular sections. These are cooled with liquid metal cooling tubes and joined into motor fibres, thus improving force density and manufacturability. Motor efficiency is improved by independently controlling the coil repeat units and setting the coil electric current proportional to the local magnetic field. A low-computational-cost modelling framework based on a differential element approximation is adapted to this motor configuration and used to generate optimal motor geometries for a case study involving the upgrade of a shoulder-assistance motor. Design guidelines and trade-offs associated with this novel motor configuration are discussed and compared to existing tubular linear motors.

articleTitle: A Fault Tolerant Electric Propulsion Unit Based on Bifilar Coils
abstract: This paper presents a novel fault tolerant electric propulsion unit concept based on a permanent magnet motor with concentrated tooth-coil winding. A stator winding of an electrical machine is wound using bifilar coils, and each bifilar coil is supplied by separate inverter modules while ensuring the same current direction in the slots and, thus, an additive current linkage. The proposed design aims to prevent the possibility of inter-turn short circuit faults within the same coil. Such faults can cause the most severe local fault currents in a stator winding in case of a single-turn short circuit. The paper investigates the effect of turn-to-turn short circuits between bifilar coils and possible detection mechanisms using finite element analysis. The evaluation of differential current and zero sequence current is utilized to detect turn-to-turn faults at an early stage and are shown to provide sensitive detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Investigation of Worst-Scenario Rotor Tolerances in Halbach Machines
abstract: Tolerances are inevitable in machine manufacturing and additional low-frequency cogging torque harmonics with high-amplitude will be introduced. In this paper, a genetic algorithm combined with phasor diagram method is proposed to identify the worst-scenario cogging torque caused by rotor tolerances in Halbach machines, including permanent magnet (PM) thickness, angular width, position, and their combination. It is found that compared to the peak values of the worst-scenario cogging torques due to a single tolerance, the peak values of the worst-scenario cogging torque are significantly aggravated due to the combined tolerances, cogging torque caused by single PM thickness tolerance is more sensitive to segment number compared to the PM angular width tolerance, position tolerance, and all tolerance combination conditions. Meanwhile, PM thickness tolerance is more crucial in the Halbach machine with more segments no matter whether it is single tolerance or their combination.

articleTitle: Advanced Methodology for Magneto-Mechanical Topology Optimization of a Synchronous Reluctance Machine
abstract: This paper proposes a magneto-mechanical topology optimization (TO) for designing the rotor of a synchronous reluctance machine. The objective is to improve the mechanical strength while ensuring good magnetic performance. The two formulations are expressed in terms of energy. The magnetostatic formulation uses the magnetic energies obtained from the d-axis and q-axis to ensure a mean torque that meets specifications. Meanwhile, the mechanical formulation focuses on optimizing the structural compliance. A density-based TO solves the coupled problem with the adjoint variable method to compute the sensitivity. Moreover, the initialization of the algorithm is chosen to insure optimal design with multiple flux guides.

articleTitle: A Novel Non-Uniform Air-Gap Halbach Magnetic Gear with Modified PM Shape
abstract: Mitigating yoke flux leakage is crucial for enhancing the efficiency and volumetric torque density of magnetic gears. This paper presents a novel coaxial magnetic gear design, featuring an uneven air-gap and modified shape of permanent magnets arranged in a Halbach configuration. By leveraging the variable reluctance across the non-uniform air-gap, the coaxial magnetic gear effectively suppresses leakage flux along the inner rotor surface. Electromagnetic properties, including flux distribution, harmonic analysis, and torque transmission, are characterized and validated through finite element analysis. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed coaxial magnetic gear achieves a volumetric torque density of 172.8 kNm/m3, surpassing conventional and Halbach topologies. Additionally, various grades of permanent magnet materials are integrated into the design to assess the cost-effectiveness of rare-earth and non-rare-earth magnets.

articleTitle: A Modified Standstill Method Based on DC Step Voltage Test for Doubly-Fed Induction Generator-Motor Parameters Identification
abstract: The standard methods for identifying parameters of DFIGM include blocked-rotor and no-load tests. However, for large-capacity DFIGM, these tests are complex and have a high risk factor. Addressing this issue, this paper proposes a parameter identification method for DFIGM based on DC step voltage. It utilizes the operational circuit of DFIGM to derive the parameter identification model, to tackle the issue of noisy current response signals, an improved wavelet threshold denoising method is employed for filtering. Subsequently, the differential evolution (DE) algorithm is applied for time-domain fitting of the current response to enhance fitting accuracy. The parameters of the DFIGM are calculated by combining the analytic relations in the parameter identification model. Finally, experiments conducted on a 10 kVA dynamic simulation prototype validate the effectiveness of the proposed method. This method offers high safety, simplicity in operation, and minimal equipment.

articleTitle: Development of an Ultra-Lightweight PM Electrical Motor for Solar-Powered High-Altitude Platform Applications
abstract: This paper describes key aspects of the development process of an ultra-lightweight electrical motor for solar-powered high-altitude (20km) platform applications. A radial-flux permanent magnet (PM) machine topology with outer rotor and integrated air-cooling is considered here. The mission profile of the analysed solar-powered aircraft calls for a high-torque overload (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times \mathbf{2.5})$</tex> at take-off and a high-efficiency (>95%) at high altitude cruise operation. Consequently, a fine balance between both operating points needs to be seen when sizing the motor. Here, effective thermal management of the motor at take-off is critical for achieving a compact/lightweight motor design. Further to these, the motor design should enable a simple/cost-effective manufacturing and assembly process, which makes use of the lightweight composite materials for all structural subassemblies. In this work, a careful integration between both active and structural subassemblies of the motor resulted in a significant weight reduction, with contribution of all structural components less than 5% of the overall motor weight. The theoretical and initial experimental results discussed in the paper confirm that the developed motor meets the key design targets. Further evaluation will include the mission specific and aircraft integration aspects, i.e. high-altitude tests, aerodynamic tests and flight tests.

articleTitle: Similarity Numbers for the Scaling of Hydroelectric Generator Ventilation Flow
abstract: Recently, the design of cooling air circuits for hydro power generators has transitioned towards utilization of computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, increasingly supplementing or even replacing the previously favored network calculations. To validate the calculations for individual generators, common practice involves direct measurements of the pressure drop and volume flow characteristics using scaled models of the corresponding generators. This paper delves into the analysis of generator model ventilation flow and derives a set of similarity numbers to dimensionlessly represent this flow problem. The set of similarity numbers specified herein aids in determining the key considerations when scaling a generator for a ventilation model test. The focus of these similarity numbers lies on pressure loss characteristics, with no exploration of heat transfer aspects due to their usual exclusion from ventilation model tests. Two of these similarity numbers, although not appearing in existing literature, are predicted to significantly impact generator cooling flow. To evaluate and discuss this impact, CFD simulations of a generic generator cooling flow section are conducted. These CFD simulations primarily illustrate the importance of the newly introduced similarity numbers while maintaining adherence to the state of the art.

articleTitle: Superconducting AC Machines and Cryogenic Power Electronics for Reliable and Power-Dense Energy Conversion
abstract: Implementing superconductivity in rotating electrical machines has many advantages such as increased efficiency, smaller size, and lighter weight if compared to conventional electrical machines. Due to the operative limitation of superconductors, they were mainly used in the DC excitation field windings. However, to target ever higher power density values, there are considerable efforts to use superconductors for the AC windings. This paper reviews the main significant prototypes that implement partially and fully AC synchronous and asynchronous superconducting machines. In the perspective of future cryogenic and superconducting integrated electric drives, the paper also reports research activities on the power electronics components under cryogenic temperature. Moreover, considering the safety critical applications or harsh environments where these drives are expected to be used, recent advancements on diagnostic techniques for electrical machines and drives for cryogenic environments are included.

articleTitle: System Analysis of a Braking Energy Recovery Axle of Truck Trailer
abstract: The aim of this paper is reducing the emissions of refrigeration units used in the trucking industry. To lower the consumption of diesel fuel, an energy braking recovery (recuperation) axle is used to generate energy. To supply power to different refrigeration units, a synchronous reluctance generator is used together with a gearbox, inverter, and batteries of different sizes. A Simulink model is developed, using these components, which calculates how much energy is needed in a given drive cycle and how much of it can be generated through braking. The Vehicle Energy Consumption calculation Tool, developed by the European Commission, is used to generate driving scenarios for the truck. These provide the necessary information about power and energy availability, which differ between driving cycles. The generated results are then interpreted to find connections between the components and how they influence each other. Moreover, the results are evaluated using a target function chosen to represent the goals of the paper. Aspects regarding the pollution and costs of ownership are rated for every combination and compared. A preliminary best combination, can then be selected for each driving cycle and refrigeration unit.

articleTitle: Real Time Stator and Magnet Fluxes Estimation Based on Kalman Filters of PMSynRel Motor
abstract: This paper deals with the real time estimation of the stator and the permanent magnet flux components of the PM SynRel motor. This estimation can be fruitful for control, diagnosis, and supervision strategies. For this purpose, two interconnected observers of distinct dynamics were used, an Unscented Kalman filter to estimate the stator flux and a linear Kalman filter for the permanent magnet flux. A refined tuning of these approaches, corrections on measurement and modelling based on a sensitivity analysis, have considerably improved the online performance. Therefore, an estimation error within one percent on the permanent magnet flux and on the motor torque was shown by experimental results on several motor operating points.

articleTitle: Validation of Electrostatic Shieldings in Traction Motors to Mitigate Capacitive Bearing Currents
abstract: An uncommon but effective measure for mitigating harmful capacitive bearing currents in traction motors involves the implementation of electrostatic shieldings. This study focuses on different shielding designs for the stator part of a motor and assesses the shieldings' effectiveness by means of the influence on the electric fields and the associated shaft voltage. Based on the knowledge gained by FE analysis, motorettes with different slot-shielding designs and a complete motor with the most promising variant among all investigated slot-shielding options were built. Finally, the study presents the validation of the slot-shieldings' effectiveness by impedance and shaft voltage measurements. The measurements confirm a reduction of the winding-rotor capacitance up to 84% and a shaft voltage reduction exceeding 44%. Particular focus is given to developing a design suitable for series production.

articleTitle: Hybrid Open-Circuit Fault Detection Algorithm for Two-Level Three-Phase Automotive Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine Drives
abstract: Interior permanent magnet synchronous machine drives in Electric Vehicles operate in extremely harsh conditions, and open-circuit faults can be common. The incorporation of a fast and accurate fault determination algorithm is of great interest to protect the system, driving it into fail-safe mode, or even triggering a fault-tolerant strategy. This work considers the wide operating conditions of an electric vehicle, ranging from standstill to very high speeds, and from light to heavy load conditions. A novel hybrid detection and diagnosis algorithm that merges various techniques is proposed to accurately detect and diagnose open-circuit faults in the automotive context. Simulations that verify the correctness of the proposal are provided using a high fidelity drive model.

articleTitle: Power Losses and THD Analysis of Current Source Inverters in Motor Drive Applications: A Comparative Study of Control Schemes
abstract: Current Source Inverters (CSIs) for motor drive application historically suffered the need of a pre-stage to control DC-link current and the problem of CL resonance of output currents. The advent of innovative control schemes and architectures solved the need for a pre-stage, but the efficiency gain given by eliminating pre-stage has never been explored, as does the investigation of the CL resonance problem. While prior research has addressed resonance issues using various control strategies, few studies have delved into the efficiency implications of these solutions. This paper undertakes a comparative analysis of traditional CSI control schemes against innovative alternatives, evaluating power losses and Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) of the output currents. Specifically, two distinct control schemes are analyzed over the classical field oriented control: the first in- corporates an inner closed-loop on voltage to mitigate resonance, while the second obviates the need for a pre-stage in high-speed operations, demonstrating improved power loss performance.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Impact of the Cryostat Design in Wind Generators with Superconducting Excitation
abstract: Synchronous generators with high-temperature superconducting field winding in the rotor are a promising alternative to state-of-the-art permanent magnet generators for future wind energy conversion systems. To achieve sufficient superconducting field currents in presence of high magnetic flux densities <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B \geq 3 ~\mathrm{T}$</tex>, cryogenic temperatures of about 30 K are required. A sufficient thermal insulation of the cryogenic rotor section presupposes sufficient space in the magnetically effective air gap to accommodate a vacuum chamber and superinsulation foils. By means of 2D finite element calculations, this work analyses the trade-off between thermal and electromagnetic space requirements for an exemplary 13 MW, 600 rpm medium-speed generator. The additional excitation requirement due to a wider magnetic air gap is quantified. The eddy current losses in the vacuum chamber and in the cold rotor iron parts are calculated. We find that the loss in the cryogenic section can be limited sufficiently, even without an additional copper damper screen.

articleTitle: Impact Analysis of FOC-Based Synchronous PWM Strategy on Traction Induction Motor Drives Performance
abstract: This paper presents an accurate experimental analysis of the performance of an induction motor drive controlled with a soft switching frequency synchronous pulse width modulation strategy. A comparison with a conventional asynchronous pulse width modulation strategy has been conducted in terms of power quality and power losses, with the latter segregated into fundamental and harmonic power losses. For this purpose, a test bench has been set up and several experimental investigations have been carried out on a three-phase, 4-pole, 5.5 kW induction motor for sixteen different working conditions defined in the torque-speed plane. The results obtained are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of AC Winding Loss Calculation for Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Machines based on Finite Element Analysis
abstract: This paper addresses the computational methods for alternate current (AC) winding losses in electric machines. Four different calculation methods are employed; a full three-dimensional (3-D) finite element analysis (FEA) model, a 2-D model with the scaled factor, a 3-D hybrid of an analytical method with 3-D FEA, a proposed method based on the homogenization approach. The homogenization method is implemented in a post-processing similar to iron loss. Each method is compared in terms of its accuracy, computational efficiency, and versatility for addressing various emerging issues in electric machines. Results demonstrate an effectiveness of the proposed homogenization approach, emphasizing its suitability for electric machine analysis, especially at high speed.

articleTitle: Design of High-Speed Linear Induction Motors - Part II: End Effect Reduction
abstract: Traditional linear induction machines (LIMs) show a significant reduction of thrust as the speed of the machine increases, which is known as the end effect. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of end effect in LIMs and its relationship with the magnetic Reynolds number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{Re}_{\mathrm{m}})$</tex>. The relationship between end effect, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Re}_{\mathrm{m}}$</tex> and the type of electrodynamic regime (resistance limited or inductance limited induced currents) is analyzed in detail. It is shown that reducing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{Re}_{\mathrm{m}}$</tex>, by increasing the reaction plate's resistivity, reduces the end effect, resulting in marginal reduction of thrust in the high speed region. The paper presents a case study comparing a conventional LIM with respect to the proposed LIM with the appropriate reaction plate to reduce end effect, to illustrates the advantage of the latter in terms of thrust at high speeds.

articleTitle: Six-Phase Induction Machines: State of the Art on Design, Modeling, Control and Diagnosis
abstract: This review paper provides an overview of recent advancements in the design, modeling, control, and diagnosis techniques of six-phase induction machines. With an increasing focus on multiphase machines for various applications, the study highlights key developments in six-phase induciton machines, including innovations in design methodologies, advancements in modeling techniques, novel control strategies, and emerging diagnosis approaches. By synthesizing findings from recent research, this paper aims to offer insights into the current state of the field and inspire further exploration and refinement of methodologies for optimizing the performance and reliability of six-phase induction machines.

articleTitle: Comparison of Interior Permanent Magnet Machine Designs Aimed for City and Highway Driving - Consequences on Loss and Torque Performance from Degradation Due to Laser Cutting
abstract: This paper explores four interior permanent magnet machine designs to assess the impact of cutting degradation on their loss and torque. Predicting the electric machines' core loss is important for achieving a viable design. However, existing theoretical models for calculating core loss do not consider the degradation of electromagnetic properties in electrical steel sheets from manufacturing processes. Instead, constant empirical factors are introduced to bridge the gap between theoretical analysis and test results. The important key findings of this study indicate that designs with more stator slots are more susceptible to increased core loss, for instance moving from 48 slots to 72 slots can cause up to 20 % higher core loss increase due to cutting while the same would cause 0.5 % higher torque reduction. However, adding more magnet layers in the rotor, hence, increasing degraded cut edge area has minimal impact on core loss and only reduces torque production by 1 %.

articleTitle: Flat Integration of a Segmented Linear Motor Direct Drive to Activate an Active Stick System Façade
abstract: Ultra slim framed windows and doors allow extraordinary architectural creations and meet highest aesthetic requirements. This makes the stick system façade a solution that combines lightness and openness in design with a high degree of functionality. Especially active façade elements integrated into a smart home environment raise the functionality of the outer skin of the building to a new level. The proposed integrated linear motor drive solves the aesthetic issue of an additional framing and allows the sliding window sash to open fully and silently. From the technical point of view the main requirements are a durable and very flat motor design with a thermal and wind-load tolerance compensation. The segmented central direct drive is compact, does not require a gear box and reduces the noise level to the audible limit. The design of the proposed linear machine is aimed at energy-efficient integration into the façade, simplicity and comfort as well as robustness and durability. It is tolerant to weather influences and proposes solutions to the technical consequences of aesthetic benefits. The system is modeled and optimized using FE analyses and a genetic optimization algorithm. Finally the manufactured prototype validates the functionality of the system.

articleTitle: Opportunities for AC Loss Reduction in Metal Additive Formed Hairpin Windings
abstract: Rectangular bar, hairpin windings are increasingly being employed in power dense electrical machines, as they offer advantages of low DC resistance, good thermal performance and manufacture consistency. The comparably large section conductors used in hairpin windings are prone to high levels of AC loss, particularly when considering fundamental frequencies approaching or exceeding 1 kHz are now common in power dense electrical machines. Methods used to mitigate AC loss involve either reducing the conductor section, through introducing parallel paths or Litz stranding, or substituting a low electrical conductivity wire, e.g. aluminum. With all these approaches is a trade between AC loss reduction versus an increase in ohmic DC resistance. Advances in metal additive layer manufacture allows for complex 3D winding structures to be formed and near maximum (100% IACS) copper conductivity can now be printed. 3D printing allows for AC loss mitigation measures to be targeted to the active regions of the winding, where it is most needed, thereby minimizing the impact on the overall winding DC resistance. The paper develops a simplified analysis framework that enables the loss improvement of incorporating a 3D printed hairpin winding to be assessed for a target application. An EV propulsion motor case study is used to illustrate the methodology.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Synchronous Reluctance Motor and Switched Reluctance Motor for Forklift Applications
abstract: This paper introduces the synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM) for forklift applications for the first time and presents a performance comparison with the latest applied switched reluctance motor (SRM). Initially, the SynRM is designed according to the motor performance requirements of the 2.5t forklift. The design procedure and optimization process have been described in detail. Then, the comprehensive performance comparison of the designed SynRM and the applied SRM is given in terms of cost, torque, and efficiency under the same operation condition. It is demonstrated that the SynRM exhibits superior electromagnetic performance compared to the SRM at a reduced cost, making it a compelling choice for such low-speed and high-overload applications.

articleTitle: Aspect Ratio Optimization for YASA Machines Under Thermal Constraints
abstract: Aspect ratio of axial field permanent magnet machines (AFPM), i.e., the ratio of axial length to diameter of machines, is a key dimensional parameter. It significantly influences the torque capability and loss performances under specific thermal constraint. This paper analytically establishes the relationship between output torque and aspect ratio, as well as other design parameters of yokeless and segmented armature (YASA) AFPM machines. The prescriptive loss conditions are established, which correspond to different thermal limitations. It is found analytically, as verified by finite element analysis, that for YASA AFPM machines, the optimal aspect ratio exists and is significantly affected by the machine size and relatively less affected by the operating speed.

articleTitle: Transient Quality Assessment of a Novel Thermal Modeling Methodology for Electric Machines
abstract: Electric vehicles require electric machines with increasing power density, making precise thermal analysis critical during the design phase. Since these models ideally require computation times below one minute, achieving precision typically involves a trade-off between accuracy and speed, with existing models being either highly detailed and time-consuming or faster but less accurate. To address this issue, a new hybrid modeling approach has been introduced, which integrates 3D lumped parameter thermal networks with thermal resistances obtained from 2D finite element models (FEM). This method significantly reduces computation times while maintaining high accuracy. In a transient comparison with a 3D FEM simulation conducted in OpenFOAM, the temperature deviations for critical components remain below 0.75 °, closely aligning with the 0.39 °C uncertainty of the 3D FEM. Remarkably, the proposed model completes its simulation in just 43.5 seconds, compared to the 175 hours needed for the 3D FEM, demonstrating its efficiency without sacrificing the precision required for thermal analysis of key components.

articleTitle: Experimental Identification of the dqθ Flux Maps of Synchronous Machines
abstract: This work proposes a test sequence and data processing method for evaluating the complete <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dq\theta$</tex> flux maps of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine, including its spatial harmonics. The constant-speed measurement procedure of the fundamental (sinusoidal) flux linkage curves is complemented by the proposed method to extract space harmonic information from the measured voltage and current signals. The average between symmetric motor and generator operations, already adopted for fundamental flux maps to gain immunity from the stator resistance voltage, is extended here to the complete flux maps. In addition, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dq6$</tex> torque map, inclusive of the torque ripple component, can be calculated off-line by manipulation of flux and current quantities, without the need of dedicated torque measurement sessions. The outcomes of the proposed procedure are 3-dimensional flux maps representing the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dq$</tex> flux linkages function of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$dq$</tex> currents and the electrical rotor position <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta$</tex>. The results presented in the paper refer to the experimental characterization of a 40 Nm, 11 kW peak PM synchronous machine.

articleTitle: A Semi-Supervised Method for Key Performance Indicator Prediction of Electrical Machines Under a Self-Training Framework
abstract: Machine learning metamodels have been frequently used for predicting key performance indicators (KPIs) of electrical machines because of their rapid and precise predicting capabilities. However, the conventional procedure of data collection using finite element analysis is time-consuming. To shorten data collection time and improve the prediction accuracy of metamodels, we propose a semi-supervised learning approach using self-training techniques. Initially, we utilize the labeled samples to train a geometry classifier and a KPI predictor. We employ the classifier to eliminate geometrically infeasible designs from unlabeled data. For the remaining feasible designs, the predictor is applied to predict their KPIs. Since not all predictions of the trained metamodels are accurate and reliable, we introduce a confidence score using Monte-Carlo dropout to obtain trustworthy predictions as pseudo-labels for unlabeled data. Finally, the generated pseudo-labels and original labeled data are jointly used for metamodel retraining. The results show that the original dataset can be iteratively expanded in a short period of time, and the performance of both metamodels is improved.

articleTitle: Stator Slot Design Guidelines for Concentrated Windings with Direct Liquid Cooling Channels for Electrified Aviation
abstract: High power and torque densities are essential to achieve weight reduction in electric propulsion systems. For the future integration of highly utilised electric machines into aircraft propulsion, these must be evaluated also with a focus on service life and reliability. Typically, the components that limit the lifetime of electric machines are the bearings and the insulation of the stator winding. In addition, high power densities and efficiencies are essential for the realisation of electrified aviation. One method to achieve high power densities is to increase the current density. Direct liquid cooling can regulate the resulting temperature within the slot, thus managing thermal aging and increasing insulation reliability. This paper develops stator slot design guidelines for concentrated hollow conductor windings for direct liquid cooling to achieve higher power densities, highlighting the importance of current displacement and temperature-dependent resistance.

articleTitle: Global Sensitivity and Uncertainty Analysis for Thermal Design of Axially Laminated Synchronous Reluctance Machine
abstract: A polynomial chaos based surrogate modeling method to quantify the uncertainties and perform the global sensitivity analysis for a thermal model of the electrical machine is presented. The method is demonstrated using a 27kW 100 krpm axially laminated synchronous reluctance machine (ALAsynRM) as a study case. Exact thermal parameters and thermal conditions in any electrical machine are somewhat unpredictable. Sensitivity analysis provides a platform to determine the machine's thermal working condition. However, this analysis can be time consuming and requires a lot of simulations. A probability density function is utilized to show the impact of changing thermal coefficients and input and output cooling fluid temperatures on the machine output temperature. This probability density function can be obtained even with limited number of parameters. Most of the machines, especially those having complicated structures require three dimensional thermal analysis to determine the operating temperature of different components. Therefore, a 3D model of a drum wound liquid cooled stator and the axially laminated air cooled rotor is utilized as a case study. It is shown that before the experimental analysis if the thermal coefficients and fluid temperatures are not available, a probability density function can be utilised to determine the range with less number of simulations.

articleTitle: Extended HF Inductance Model of Multi-Salient Motors for HF and Pulse Voltage Signal Injection
abstract: Spatial saliencies of AC motors can be acquired in the form of a saliency vector using high frequency signal injection or voltage pulse excitation. In both cases, the frequency spectrum of the saliency vector shows a large amount of harmonics caused by different effects, not only the spatial saliencies themselves. In addition to the well-known harmonics caused by inverter nonllnearities, it was recently shown that saliency-harmonic-products emerge in the saliency vector under pulse excitation of multi-salient motors. All these harmonics are detrimental for encoderless control as they take out signal strength of the saliency used to extract rotor or flux position. In this paper, the saliency harmonic products will be investigated for both high frequency signal injection and pulse excitation. The high-frequency induction motor model will be enhanced, accounting for these frequency components. Experimental results measured in a multi-salient motor confirm the existence of these saliency harmonic products and the need for their consideration for improved encoderless performance.

articleTitle: A Novel Structure Fan to Reduce Noise and Mechanical Loss of Motors
abstract: In this paper, a novel structure fan passively switching between synchronous and asynchronous rotation is proposed as a novel fan system to reduce noise and mechanical loss at high speed, and the design method and measurement results of the fan speed are described. We select materials for each part to reduce leakage magnetic flux, and increase the torque (eddy current torque) of a torque limiter of the fan by increasing the number of magnetic poles in the torque limiter. Measurement and analysis results show that the eddy current torque of the torque limiter could be designed with high accuracy. The relationship between the eddy current torque of the torque limiter and the fan rotation speed is generally consistent between measurements and analysis. The measurement shows that the novel structure fan can reduce the fan speed by 11% at high shaft speed of 5000 min<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>, and the result can lead to lower the mechanical loss by 19% than a conventional fan. In addition, the measurement results revealed that the novel structure fan has the potential to reduce the fan loss by 51% by reducing bearing friction.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Synchronous Reluctance Machines for Electric Vehicle Application: A Feasibility Study Case
abstract: Synchronous Reluctance Machines (SynRMs) have gained considerable attention for their high-performance capabilities and simplicity. However, these machines can be prone to high torque ripple if not designed precisely. This paper conducts an analysis of the rotor geometry impact on the performance of SynRMs for electric vehicles applications. A rotor structure with three-flux barriers per pole is optimized using a Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm and Finite Element Method. The optimization was carried out for two different rotor configurations: one with symmetric flux barriers and the other with asymmetric ones. The assessment of different performance indicators was conducted at different operating points, showing the benefits of the asymmetric version with respect to the symmetric one. The results of this study provide valuable insights for the design of SynRMs with improved performance and reduced torque ripple.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of Ferrite-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor with Fluid Flux Barriers and Rectangular Magnets
abstract: This paper presents the design optimization of a 4-pole Ferrite magnet-assisted Synchronous Reluctance motor with fluid flux barriers. Though the rotor structure becomes intricate when fluid flux barriers are used, they generally yield a better saliency ratio and electromagnetic performance than rectangular-and circular flux barriers. This work reports the design and optimization of rotor geometry comprising rectangular blocks of ferrite magnets with fluid flux barriers. Such a rotor geometry facilitates the usage of regular-shaped magnets and simplifies the manufacturing complexity inherent to motors with pure fluid flux barriers. The rotor features four flux barriers per pole, each barrier being defined by three distinct geometric variables. These variables are subjected to a multi-objective optimization process, which targets maximizing the product of efficiency and power factor (to reduce inverter size) and minimizing the torque ripple. The optimized model exhibits better electromagnetic performance figures such as efficiency, power factor and torque ripple. In addition, the optimized model has less active volume, resulting in a higher torque density. Result of the optimization study is presented, showing the improvement brought into the various performance figures of the motor.

articleTitle: Experimental Verification of an Intermittent Stator Ground Protection in Large MVA Generators
abstract: The paper discusses the importance of detecting intermittent stator ground faults in large MVA generators. The detection of such faults can pose a serious challenge to the conventional and some newly proposed IEEE protection schemes. In response to this challenge, an intermittent stator ground fault protection method called the subharmonic current differential scheme (87S) is presented. The efficacy of the 87S scheme is verified by manufacturing an apparatus containing all the components of the neutral grounding circuit of large MVA generators which apply the subharmonic voltage injection-based methodology for 100% stator ground protection.

articleTitle: Geometry Optimization of an Interior Permanent Magnet Machine for Minimal Life Cycle Cost in City, Rural and Highway Driving
abstract: This paper presents Interior Permanent Magnet Machine (IPM) geometries that are customized for city, rural and highway driving in an electric car, using an optimization work-flow that minimizes the Life Cycle Cost (LCC) of the IPM and its feeding inverter. The work-flow includes scaling of electromagnetic finite element results to identify which size and current rating of each geometry that gives lowest LCC while meeting, thermal and mechanical constraints. The different driving types are considered either as single drive cycles or as distributions of logged driving. The IPMs optimized for city, rural or highway driving are compared to an IPM optimized for mixed driving, showing that IPM customization reduced the LCC by 7% in a city cycle and by 1% in a highway cycle. However, most of the driving scenarios, including all types based on logged driving, were found to be well met with an IPM optimized for mixed driving.

articleTitle: Analysis and Enhanced Modeling of Inductive Displacement Sensor in Active Magnetic Bearing
abstract: Inductive displacement sensors are commonly used in active magnetic bearing (AMB) applications. In most research, conventional models used to analyze inductive sensors in terms of determining sensitivity and obtaining a relationship between output voltage and displacement ignore the effects of fringing in air gaps. However, the effects of flux fringing on the performance of these sensors cannot be ignored in industrial applications. In this article, by using the Schwarz-Christoffel transformation, 3-D self-and mutual inductances for the radial and axial poles of a 3-degree-of-freedom inductive sensor are calculated, with the effects of fringing taken into account. The results of these calculations are compared with finite element results. The results show that the model based on the Schwarz-Christoffel method outperforms the ideal model in which flux fringing is ignored, with an inductance calculation error of about 8% for radial poles and 6.5% for axial poles, respectively.

articleTitle: Multidisciplinary Design Methodology for Ultra-High-Speed PM Motors
abstract: The design of ultra-high-speed PM machines requires a systematic multidisciplinary design approach to overcome the special need to consider the mutual influence of rotor dynamics, mechanical stresses, and electromagnetic aspects. To prove the effectiveness of the proposed design methodology, a 500 W, 500,000 rpm slotless PM has been calculated. The process starts by determining the initial rotor dimensions based on an air-friction loss analytical model. Then, the rotor dynamics problem has been solved using a three-dimensional finite element model, including the ball bearings suitable for ultra-high-speed applications. The radial, tangential, and axial mechanical stress analyses have been solved using an analytical model developed for the case study. Finally, the electromagnetic performance has been verified by bi-dimensional finite element models. The obtained results demonstrate the consistency of the proposed multidisciplinary design methodology.

articleTitle: Rewinding of Old 44 MVA Hydro Generator Considering Vibrational Forces
abstract: Renovating hydro generators improves their durability and boosts their effectiveness. Outdated generators exhibit decreased reliability and efficiency, along with a increased frequency of breakdowns, which can have significant economic impacts. The primary aim of the refurbishment is to enhance the cooling system, upgrade the materials, and boost the efficiency. Modifying the winding design is rare because it often requires changing the slot number, and a complex rebuild. Moreover, modifying the slot number affects the slots per pole per phase ratio of the machine, potentially altering the vibration characteristics of the machine. This paper focuses on a 68-year-old generator built by Westinghouse Electrical Corporation in 1956. The machine was initially constructed with lap windings. The goal is to rewind the generator using Roebel bars during refurbishment, but this requires a change in slot number. Various design sets are selected considering their electromagnetic performances. In this paper, their vibration characteristics are investigated. All four slot alternatives identical efficiencies sit around 98.20% efficiency, whereas 270, 300, and 324 slot alternatives include risky low-order spatial force harmonics due to fractional armature winding. 270 slot design has a dangerous vibration since it consists 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> spatial force harmonic with close proximity to power frequency, 100 Hz. 300 slot design achieve the best electromagnetic performance with sufficient vibration levels such that it is selected a viable slot selection. This study promises a guideline to hydro-generator designers who work on a refurbishment study on old hydro-generators that involves machine vibration concerns.

articleTitle: Influence of the Stator Winding on the Mechanical Eigenfrequencies of Hydro Generators
abstract: The vibrational behaviour of the stator of a hydro generator is an important aspect to be evaluated during the design of the machine, as it has an impact on its maintenance and life expectancy. This evaluation requires, in addition to the calculation of the exciting magnetic forces, the determination of the eigenfrequencies and eigenmodes of the stator structure. This task is particularly challenging for a large hydro generator due to its structural complexity, involving various components such as the laminated core, the ventilation air ducts, the frame, the winding, and the connections between these. This paper is dedicated to the experimental investigation of the influence of the stator winding on the mechanical eigenfrequencies of the stator assembly. For this purpose, a series of experimental modal analyses is performed in different assembly phases of a real 55 MVA generator. It turns out that, from the stator's point of view and by considering the typical winding insertion methods without global impregnation, the winding is only weakly coupled to the laminated core. Thus, the mass and the stiffness of the winding have no substantial effect on the system's eigenfrequencies. This finding contributes to the selection of appropriate simplifications and assumptions in the modelling of the complete stator including the winding for the prediction of structural vibrations in future works.

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Compensation for IPMSM with Minimum Loss
abstract: This study presents an in-depth analysis of the torque ripple compensation methods, comparing current har-monics injection (CHI) in d-axis, q-axis, and dq-axes including instant Maximum Torque Per Ampere and Direct Flux-and-Torque Control, which targets the minimum loss for an interior Permanent Magnet synchronous motor. The performance of different CHIs has been evaluated by finite element simulations, highlighting the importance of the selection of the CHI technique for torque ripple compensation considering minimum total loss.

articleTitle: Systematic Approach for EMI Equivalent Model Derivation of Three Phase DC-Fed Motor Drives
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) is a critical concern in DC-fed motor drives, as it can degrade system performance and reliability. This paper presents a systematic approach for deriving the filter design oriented EMI equivalent model of a three-phase DC-fed motor drive system, aiming at enhancing the understanding of EMI mechanisms and facili-tating effective mitigation strategies. The methodology involves deriving common-mode (CM) and differential-mode (DM) equivalent models for the motor drive system by identifying critical components and paths for EMI propagation. A time-frequency analytical modeling approach is proposed in this paper, providing flexibility in the modeling process. Ultimately, the proposed methodology facilitates accurate EMI prediction which helps in filter design during the design phase.

articleTitle: Influence of Flux Screen and Clamping Materials on Eddy Current Losses in End Region of High-Power Electrical Machines
abstract: Calculating additional losses in electrical machines has always been a challenging task. This paper investigates losses in the plates and clamping fingers of high-power electrical machines. The study examines the impact of both axial and radial components of end-region leakage flux on losses. This is conducted using a finite element numerical model of a setup designed for this purpose. The losses are quantified for various plate and clamping fingers materials. Furthermore, the impact of the flux screen made of copper is analyzed on overall end-region losses.

articleTitle: Flying Start of a Synchronous Reluctance Machine Based on Opposite Active Voltage Pulses
abstract: Synchronous reluctance machines (SynRMs) are increasingly used in various applications, such as energy conversion systems and electric drives. In addition to standard control algorithms, some of these applications also require the implementation of flying start methods that aim to estimate the rotor speed and angle before the SynRM is connected to the converter. In this way, synchronization between the SynRM and the converter is achieved, and the inrush current is reduced. This paper proposes a new method for the flying start of SynRMs based on symmetric and opposite active voltage vectors and a second-order generalized integrator (SOGI) with a frequency-locked loop (FLL). Applying such a voltage vector pattern to the terminals of a rotating SynRM induces phase current spikes whose sampled counterparts have a sinusoidal waveform. According to the derived mathematical model of the SynRM in the stationary <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha\beta$</tex> reference frame, the induced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-axis current contains no DC offset and is therefore passed to the SOGI-FLL structure to estimate the rotor angle and speed. Moreover, applying the opposite active vectors ensures a lower current distortion, guarantees the accuracy of the estimation and reduces the generated torque. The proposed method was verified by simulations in Matlab Simulink.

articleTitle: A Sensor Fusion Based Temperature Estimation Model for Oil-Cooled Windings
abstract: This article introduces an innovative method to monitor the average winding temperature in real-time during the operation of an oil-cooled electric motor, particularly suitable for high-performance automotive applications. It is based on the sensor fusion of two distinct dynamic models: one considering the measurement of local temperature through a thermal sensor positioned on the end-winding of the motor, and the other utilizing a first-order model to predict the average winding temperature. The integration of these models significantly enhances the accuracy in estimating the average winding temperature, particularly for short-duty and high current densities.

articleTitle: Compensation of Current Measurement Error in PMSM Drives Based on Virtual Windings
abstract: In permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs), aging, thermal drift, and parameter inconsistency can lead to current measurement error (CME) in motor drive systems. The CME can result in extra current and torque ripples in the motor drive system, which seriously affect the control performance of the PMSM. This paper proposes a CME compensation algorithm based on virtual windings. Firstly, the three-phase PMSM is regarded as a multi-three-phase PMSM by constructing two sets of virtual windings. Then, a new VSD decoupling transformation matrix is designed to realize the current harmonics separation caused by CME. Only the separated fundamental currents are regulated to prevent the influence of the additional current harmonics caused by CME. Finally, the simulation and experimental results validate the proposed CME online compensation algorithm.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of PMaSynRM with Short-Circuit Fault Tolerance
abstract: This paper presents electromagnetic design and optimization of a fault-tolerant permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance machine. The fault tolerance against three-phase short-circuit in the stator winding is ensured by utilizing a double three-phase system and by using optimized rotor geometry. The chosen optimization method is the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II; its particular settings for the given problem are suggested and described in detail. As a result, machines with steady-state three-phase short-circuit ratio equal to 1 and lower have been managed to achieve within ten generations. However, the cost of such an improvement is the reduction in the average torque of a machine, although without a drop in its rotor torque density, compared to the initial design.

Author Keywords: Permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance machine (PMaSynRM)

articleTitle: Sensorless Control for Six-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines Based on Back-Electromotive Force Estimation
abstract: This paper presents a sensorless control algorithm based on back-electromotive force estimation for a six-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine drive. The proposed solution employs a hybrid state observer that uses two different flux estimators. To find the rotor flux position, the first observer uses the fundamental harmonic of the magnetic field, while the second observer uses the fifth harmonic. The control scheme fully exploits the degrees of freedom of multiphase machines and reduces the dependence on electrical parameters that may vary during motor operation. The experimental results confirm the robustness of the proposed solution and its independence from machine parameters. The experimental tests also demonstrate the satisfactory dynamic response and stable behavior of the drive at low speeds.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Extended State Observer Design for Torsional Vibrations Estimation in PMSM Drive
abstract: In every drivetrain, torque harmonics coming from electrical and mechanical sources lead to torsional vibrations. In this paper, a Nonlinear Extended State Observer (NESO) is designed to estimate the shaft torque in a Two Degree-of-Freedom (DOF) system, comprising a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM), an elastic shaft, a rotating load. The system is modeled as a Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) nonlinear system. Being the NESO commonly defined for single-output systems, a procedure to implement it for the MIMO nonlinear system under consideration is presented. Moreover, a general method to transform a generic MIMO system into an integral-chain form is provided, enabling NESO application. The observer performance is evaluated through computer simulations.

articleTitle: MWFA Model Based Synthetic Data Creation and Utilization for the Training of XGBoost Based Fault Diagnostic Algorithm of a Squirrel Cage Induction Motor
abstract: The use of AI trained algorithms can be considered as a paradigm shift in the field of predictive maintenance of electrical machines. However, the accuracy of the trained algorithms depends on the accuracy, versatility, and the amount of training data set which should provide all possible faulty scenarios under different operating conditions. The collection of this huge data set is almost impossible from industry and for the laboratory test rigs. This is due to the availability of a fewer number of motors with known faults working in industry and economic restrictions on the destructive tests in the lab. This fact has increased the importance of mathematical models which can be used for the training of AI algorithms under different conditions. This paper proposes the utilization of modified winding function analysis (MWF A) model of three phase induction motor for the creation of training data set. For the simulation time, complexity, and accuracy comparison the same data set is prepared using finite element method (FEM) as well. Both trained models are blindly tested on the data set taken from the laboratory test setup and the comparative analysis is performed for accuracy, time, and complexity.

articleTitle: Parametric Optimization of Flux Barriers for Torque Ripple and Tooth Force Minimization in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
abstract: This paper introduces a parametric optimization method employed to reduce the torque ripple and tooth forces related to noise, vibration, and harshness (NVH) respectively to an existing dual-V shaped permanent magnet (PM) electrical machine designed for automotive application. The general sources and contributors of NVH in electric vehicles are discussed where the electrical machine is one of the components acting as a source of noise. Different components which may affect how the NVH from the electrical machine is experienced is discussed and the different design parameters affecting the NVH generated from the electrical machine are briefly highlighted. Two of these design parameters are flux barriers and cutouts in the rotor; feature which may be introduced by designers to reduce the noise levels generated by the electrical machine and is utilized in this paper. The two different parametric optimizations are employed, one to reduce the torque ripple and one to reduce the forces acting on the stator teeth. The optimization methods selected both prove to be efficient in achieving their respective aims showing significant reductions in torque ripple and tooth forces, when compared to the reference machine while both the torque and efficiency is maintained.

articleTitle: Investigation on AC Losses in the End Conductors of Additively Manufactured Hairpin Windings
abstract: Hairpin windings (HWs) have recently been one of the most adopted solutions to enhance torque and power density of electrical machines (EMs) in automotive applications. However, they are typically characterized by high AC losses at high-frequency operation. While several research works have focused on how to model and reduce these losses within the active parts of HWs, only a few studies on their impact in the end winding (EW) regions are available, and mainly for classical HWs featuring constant cross section. This work investigates the AC losses occurring in the EWs of a traction motor with an asymmetrical HW printed with additive manufacturing (AM). The analyses are carried out through 3D finite element (FE) simulations over a wide frequency range. The losses in the EWs are determined for both copper and AlSi10Mg conductors. Comparative considerations are finally drawn, with the aim to providing general guidelines on how to model and print the EWs of asymmetrical HWs.

articleTitle: Impact of an Open-Switch Fault in T-Type Five-Phase Inverters for Induction Motor Drives
abstract: The combination of multiphase and multilevel technologies enables the achievement of higher power density in motor drives as well as generating systems for wind energy and aircraft applications. Multiphase systems are inherently more reliable than traditional three-phase systems, even though the multilevel technology utilizes a greater number of switches than traditional two-level converters. Consequently, it is crucial to select an appropriate strategy to manage faults. The T -type converter is a popular choice in industrial applications due to its promising efficiency performance. This paper presents a detailed analysis of the impact of an open-switch fault on the performance of a five-phase induction motor drive. Experimental tests have been carried out on a three-level T -type inverter connected to a five-phase induction machine to validate the analysis.

articleTitle: Multi-Rate Vibration Signal Analysis for Enhanced Data-Driven Monitoring of Bearing Faults in Induction Machines
abstract: In the realm of data-driven condition monitoring for induction machines, the widespread adoption of machine learning has been notable, particularly for identifying bearing faults from noisy vibration signals in electrical setups. However, the quality of the signals used to train these machine learning algorithms is important to ensure good classification performances. This paper investigates whether optimizing the Fast Fourier Transform of a vibration signal through multi-rate resampling and windowing techniques enhances the quality of the statistical features used for data-driven condition monitoring of ball bearings in induction motors. To do so, the features obtained under different frequency resolutions have been studied along with the performances of two classes of machine learning algorithms trained with them: support vector machines and random forests. The results show that for a given frequency resolution, higher sampling frequencies generally lead to improved machine learning performance. However, they also highlight the trade-off between high-frequency resolution in the Fast Fourier Transform and the number of samples available in the dataset for training. Finally, the use of the Hanning windowing technique was found not to significantly improve the quality of features for machine learning performance.

articleTitle: Comparison of Time and Frequency Domain Methods for High Frequency Voltage Distribution Simulations in Concentrated Windings
abstract: Wide band-gap devices supply voltage pulses with short rise times to the motor terminals, potentially causing bearing currents and additional voltage stresses leading to partial discharge issues. Accurate high frequency (HF) models able to predict these voltage stresses are required for a proper insulation system design. Distributed parameter circuits can be used to compute the voltage distribution within windings in high frequency. Some of the parameters in those circuits are frequency dependent due to eddy currents generated in the winding and the core. The circuit can be solved in the frequency domain, allowing to directly take the frequency dependent components into account, or, in the time domain by approximating the frequency dependent resistances and inductances by passive resistive - inductive (RL) ladder circuits. This paper compares these two methods to investigate the effect of RL-ladder approximations on voltage distribution simulations. In the frequency domain these approximations cause additional damping at the resonance and antiresonance frequencies of the common mode and differential mode impedance of the winding. In the time domain these errors are visible as the additional damping of the transients following a voltage pulse. The approximations also have an impact on the maximum voltage stress observed along the coil, which is important for a proper lifetime estimation and insulation system design.

articleTitle: PWM-Induced Losses Estimation in Electrical Motor Driven with GaN-Based Inverter
abstract: High-performance switches such as Gallium Nitride (GaN) devices offer designers the opportunity to increase the switching frequency with minimal impact on the converter losses, particularly when compared to classical silicon-based devices. This additional degree of freedom in the selection of the switching frequency can be exploited to reduce the losses on the electrical machine and therefore to maximize the efficiency of the overall drive. In this paper, the impact of the PWM switching frequency on the machine losses is investigated and a methodology for the prediction of PWM-induced losses is provided. The proposed approach enables the prediction of the PWM-induced losses, starting from the machine impedance, measured with an LCR meter. This allows the selection of the optimal switching frequency minimizing the machine losses. Experimental validation is provided, together with additional consideration on the overall drive efficiency, where both the losses on the converter and the machine are measured for different switching frequencies.

articleTitle: Analysis of Multiphase Permanent Magnet Motors via Space-Harmonic Model
abstract: Multiphase permanent magnet motors are gaining popularity thanks to their advantages, which include reduced torque ripple, enhanced torque capability, and fault tolerance. However, their modelling and control is more complex. Different harmonics in multiphase motors are separated in different orthogonal planes, each one having a different inductance value. This has different implications in airgap flux and torque generation. In this work, we present a space-harmonic model to analyse the torque production and the inductances in multiphase motors. This contributes to understand the interaction between different harmonics and their implication on the motor characteristics, which can be helpful for the motor design. To further verify the results, a three-phase and a dual three-phase motor are compared with finite element models. The case study confirms the results obtained from the space-harmonic model.

articleTitle: Experimental-Based model for Turn-to-Turn PDIV Prediction Dependent on Temperature
abstract: Turn-to-turn insulation partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) plays a crucial role in the design of the insulation system of inverter-fed motors for the automotive sector. This paper presents a turn-to-turn PDIV estimation model as a function of temperature, insulation thickness, and its relative permittivity for round and rectangular conductors. The model addresses constraints identified in other published methodologies, in that it does not require FEM simulation, experimental results as reference data, and γ or Schuman's constant adjustment. The model was validated with over 100 experimental self-measurements and literature results. For almost half of these, the PDIV value was estimated with an error of less than or equal to 5%, and the 87% of the estimated values did not exceed an error of 12%. This figure is in good agreement with other literature models. The maximum error obtained was 18%, however this can be attributed to the assumption of unknown insulation thickness and ambient relative humidity condition differences during experiments. By employing the model, coil winding designers or wire manufacturers can quickly and effectively estimate turn-to-turn PDIV at the required operational temperature for round and rectangular conductors.

articleTitle: Estimation of PM Temperature Distribution for Flux-Switching PM Machine by Synergy of Lumped-Parameter and Analytical Thermal Models
abstract: This paper proposes an analytical thermal model for permanent magnets (PMs) in the flux-switching PM machine to estimate PM temperature distribution and local hotspot temperature. The analytical thermal model is obtained by solving Poisson's equation with inhomogeneous boundary conditions, where the non-uniform PM loss distribution is also considered. Furthermore, it can be synergized with the conventional lumped-parameter thermal model accounting for the load-dependent thermal conditions. It is shown that the maximum PM temperature will be concentrated adjacent to the airgap due to convection heat transfer of airgap and local PM loss concentrated caused by the skin effect. The electromagnetic-thermal coupled finite element model is used for validation.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Stator Winding Technologies for Coreless Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: Recently, axial flux permanent magnet machines with coreless windings have been proposed for many applications, from low-speed servo systems to high-speed electric propulsion. These machines have zero cogging torque and core losses, a highly linear behaviour, and remarkable overload capabilities. Conversely, thermal behaviour, efficiency, torque density and power density strongly depend on the specific stator winding technology. This paper reviews stator winding technologies for coreless axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) machines, focusing on their potential benefits and limitations. Additional contributions include the analysis and comparison of different winding solutions for low-speed and high-speed machines. The presented results can be used as guidelines for the selection of the most appropriate winding technology for a number of practical applications.

articleTitle: Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Machine for a Power-Split Flywheel Storage System
abstract: A power-split flywheel storage system is explained to support and stabilise local grids. The concept involves a grid-connected conventional synchronous generator that is mechanically connected to a flywheel via another electrical machine. This machine is driven by an inverter and can also be used to feed electrical power into the grid or to recharge the storage system. Compared to the usable system power for the grid, the inverter only needs to be sized with a smaller partial power for this purpose. The paper focuses on the design of the coupling machine as an external rotor synchronous reluctance machine integrated in the flywheel.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of an Actuator with High Power Density Permanent Magnet motor for Bipedal Robots
abstract: Recently, bipedal robots that utilize electric rotary actuators have attracted much attention since they can walk on any kind of path or terrain and can jump or step over obstacles. In addition, bipedal robots are designed to pick up and put down various types of heavy objects for industrial applications. To achieve the specified functions, the electric rotary actuators, as the core driving unit of bipedal robots, need to possess characteristics of high power density and large output torque. This paper presents the design of an electric rotary actuator based on an outer rotor permanent magnet motor for bipedal robots. The proposed electric rotary actuator includes a 36-slot/42-pole permanent magnet motor, a 10:1 planetary gearbox, and an integrated gear shaft. The electromagnetic performances and overload capability of the proposed 36-slot/42-pole outer rotor permanent magnet motor are analyzed by the finite element method. Finally, a prototype of the proposed electric rotary actuator is tested by a customed high-torque testing bench. The experimental results are in good agreement with the finite element analysis results.

articleTitle: Model Order Reduction Based DQ Axis Parameter Extraction Method for IPMSMs
abstract: Accurate estimation of motor parameters is key for optimal motor control performance. This paper proposes a novel and fast method to extract motor parameters based on Reduced Order Model (ROM) combining Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and Kriging surrogate models. The POD method is applied to reduce the data dimensionality of the air gap magnetic density matrix in the motor. It extracts magnetic density information and integrates to derive flux linkages at various motor operational points. Utilizing the Kriging interpolation method, the ROM becomes applicable across a wide range of motor currents, thus enhancing its extension capability. Our results reveal that the ROM closely agrees with the Finite Element Method (FEM) output, offering comparable precision while achieving much higher computational efficiency than FEM. Finally, the computational feasibility of the proposed ROM is validated through simulations on a 70kW motor.

articleTitle: Application of Structural Composite Materials in Synchronous Reluctance Motors
abstract: The technology of electric motors for automotive applications is moving toward high rotating speed to enhance the power density of the machine. High-speed operations introduce mechanical constraints on the design of the rotor core that often heavily affect electromagnetic motor performance. These aspects are particularly relevant in the design of synchronous reluctance motors where the rotor shape strongly drives the motor performance. This paper investigates the adoption of carbon fiber sleeves and structural adhesive epoxy resin potting in a simple synchronous reluctance rotor, attempting to analyze the potential benefits and generalize adoption strategies. The investigation will focus on the analyses of the pre-compression, the required thickness of the carbon fiber, and the bonding properties of the epoxy resin.

articleTitle: Empirical Study on Heat Transfer Coefficients in Lumped Parameter Thermal Network of Direct-Oil Cooled Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
abstract: This paper presents an empirical study on heat transfer coefficients within a lumped parameter thermal network (LPTN) applied to a direct oil-cooled permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The study focuses on identifying unknown parameters within the LPTN, specifically the convection heat transfer coefficient (HTC) of automatic transmission fluid (ATF) oil, as well as the equivalent thermal conductivity and heat capacity of the coil. To improve the reliability of the LPTN, a proposed model for heat transfer by ATF oil is introduced. Additionally, the parameters influencing the convection HTC of ATF oil, including geometry, velocity, and temperature, are analyzed. These unknown parameters are crucial for accurate thermal analysis but those are challenging to determine due to the composite nature of the coil and the complex behavior of ATF oil. To address this challenge, a correlation process with temperature results is conducted, employing Design of Experiment (DOE) with Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS), surrogate modeling with the Kriging method, and optimization with a genetic algorithm (GA). Future work will involve expanding the scope of experimentation to include a wider range of operating points and flow rates, thus providing more comprehensive empirical data for correlation.

articleTitle: An Innovative Electric Motor Topology Developed for 2- and 3-Wheelers
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study between the state-of-the-art electrical machine topologies and an alternative innovative rare-earth-free solution. Focus is placed on the electric 2- and 3-wheelers. This application requires electrical machines typically in the range of 4 kW to 10 kW, to be manufactured and designed for cost-effective small to mid-size vehicles. The comparison is made taking into account major 2- and 3-wheelers attributes of efficiency, cost, sustainability, weight and performance. The different electrical machine topologies discussed in this paper are interior permanent magnet machines, axial flux permanent magnet machines, and axial flux electrically excited synchronous machines. This study is carried out on a 5.5 kW electrical machine. However, this paper results and conclusion may be extended also to other power levels in this segment. Besides the comparison in attributes, production aspects are also taken into account in this study. Focus in this research is put on central-drive propulsion architecture which covers majority of 2- and 3-wheelers market today. In-wheel configuration will be addressed in future publications.

articleTitle: Stray Fluxes Amplitude and Phase Shift Monitoring for Interturn Short Circuits Detection in Induction Motors
abstract: In this paper considerations about the time-domain amplitudes and phase shift between diagnostic signals measured in induction machines will be presented. In particular, the line to line voltage, stator current and axial and radial stray fluxes have been considered in various conditions. Since the phase shift between signals is rarely considered in the diagnostics of electrical machines, even in multi-sensor system, this represents a quite strong novelty of the presented method.
