The machine considered, a small-size induction motor, has been fed by the mains and with an open-loop PWM inverter. Tests with different load conditions and with three severity levels of stator inter-turn short circuits are presented. The phase-shifts between the fundamentals and third harmonics of the signals are considered, giving good diagnostic results.

articleTitle: Utilising the Core Capacitance Achieved Through Ultra-Thin Soft Magnetic Sheets and Insulators
abstract: Wide-bandgap semiconductors are employed for improved power density by leveraging their superior switching frequency capabilities. Nevertheless, the introduction of switching harmonics results in increased losses on both the drive and machine sides. Slotless permanent magnet (PM) machines are most susceptible to this issue due to their inherent low inductance. Therefore, it is necessary to implement a filtering mechanism to remove these high-order harmonics from the phase currents. This paper presents a novel integrated filter scheme that utilises the interlaminar core capacitance. The stator is fabricated through the process of creating spiral laminated sheet with a thin layer of insulation film. Thin nature of the recent state-of art magnetic sheets helps to get capacitance values in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu F$</tex> range. Various capacitor orientations are proposed for different filtering topologies. Furthermore, the obtainment of available capacitance values is accomplished through the utilisation of sizing equations that have been derived specifically for slotless permanent magnet machines, ranged from 400 W to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${200}\ kW$</tex>. A capacitance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0.25}\ \mu F/kW$</tex> is obtained with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${3}\ \mu m$</tex> Mylar film and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${20}\ \mu m$</tex> soft magnetic sheet for 2 pole slotless machines with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${100}\ m/s$</tex> rotor tip speed. The magnitude of this parameter is correlated by the number of poles <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\propto 1/p)$</tex> and the linear velocity of the rotor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\propto 1/v)$</tex>, and it is subject to thorough and comprehensive analysis. The objective of the survey is to demonstrate the potential benefits, and challenges of employing the core capacitance acquired through the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Hydro-Generator Electrical Signature Analysis for Detection of Hydraulic Instabilities
abstract: This study investigates the use of electrical signatures to diagnose turbine disturbances of hydro generator. The stator-terminal and rotor-field current measurements were used to characterize hydraulic instability zones. The spectral signature of the draft-tube pressure signal during hydraulic instabilities was compared to the signature of stator and rotor currents. Tests were conducted under steady-state and transient conditions over the complete hydro-generator operating range. A perfect match between spectral signatures was observed for all types of instability. We show that the signature of hydraulic instability can be detected in generator field and line current. This proposed methodology can be used in the future for realtime monitoring and detection of hydraulic instabilities-an asset in the context of the energy transition, especially when pressure sensors are not available.

articleTitle: Effects of the Inter-Turn Short-Circuit Fault in the Stator Winding of a 5-Phase Induction Motor
abstract: Electrical machines have infiltrated the current industrial reality dynamically, including applications in renewable energy, traction, aerospace, etc. Despite the domination of three phase machines, in special applications such as automotive and aerospace, options for multiphase electrical machines are continuously explored, as multiphase machines increase fault tolerance, efficiency, and reliability. This paper investigates the behavior of a 5-phase induction motor with inter-turn short circuit faults during the steady-state operation under two different winding configurations, notably the star and pentagon ones. Extensive finite element simulations have been performed for the healthy and faulty machine to examine the effect of the fault accounting for the winding connection, fault location, and severity.

articleTitle: A Holistic Optimization Method for the Electromagnetic Design of Radial-Flux, High-Power-Density Synchronous Reluctance Machines
abstract: In this paper, a comprehensive, multi-variable, multi-objective, optimization method is proposed for the design of radial-flux synchronous reluctance machines with high efficiency and power density. In the constrained multi-objective optimization problem, a relatively large number of critical parameters of the stator core, rotor core, and stator winding are simultaneously controlled through an evolutionary algorithm. A novel flux barrier shape and position mechanism, based on polynomial functions, is proposed to evaluate a greater number of cross-sectional geometries. The electromagnetic performance of the solutions is assessed with a non-parametric magnetic equivalent circuit method, which allows for fast and accurate calculations. A design optimization example is provided for validation of the proposed method. The selected design has a peak power density of 6.5 kW/kg at 5000 r/min and a peak torque density of 12.4 N. m/kg. The weight of the active parts is 32.8 kg (winding and electrical steel cores) and the volume is 8.1 liters, which can be considered within the published state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of an Oil Jet Cooled Electric Motor with Hairpin Windings
abstract: This paper proposes a multiphase CFD model to analyze the heat transfer in oil jet cooled electric motor hairpin end-windings. The model includes a detailed and representative end-winding geometry for both crown- and weld-side end-windings of a state-of-the-art electric motor hairpin winding. The convective heat transfer of the cooling method is studied, and a set of heat transfer coefficients is derived. These heat transfer coefficients are imported in a multi-sectorial lumped parameter model of the stator. Finally, the global heat transfer within the stator is evaluated for three different flowrates.

articleTitle: Low Loss Permanent Magnet Motor Design Methodology Using a Particular Infeasibility Driven Genetic Algorithm Technique
abstract: This paper introduces a particular design procedure based on genetic algorithm optimization technique targeting reduced losses in permanent magnet synchronous motors intended for electric vehicle applications. The proposed optimization methodology is constituted of an infeasibility driven differential evolution algorithm involving a novel constraint handling technique, associated to combined finite element and equivalent circuit appropriate models. The initial motor topology is obtained by implementing a classical preliminary design stage while the critical design stage is based on a proposed algorithm with target objectives the output torque and motor efficiency maximization and the torque ripple minimization. The methodology introduced presents stable and fast convergence characteristics for this specific machine type (PMSM) and has been applied to optimize the geometry of surface mounted configuration. The proposed motor is the outcome of the multi-objective optimization methodology, and the presented results outline the effectiveness and the accuracy of this method.

articleTitle: Hairpin Winding with Direct Oil Cooling
abstract: Hairpin windings are often applied in propulsion motors of electrical vehicles. There are several reasons supporting the technology. In mass production, hairpin winding work can be effectively automated, rectangular conductors offer a high copper space factor, a relatively simple structure and improved thermal management capability. However, due to additional AC losses generated at higher operating speed, there is a risk of local hot spots within the stator slot region, which might lead to overheating risk and insulation damage. There is also a growing interest to produce higher and higher specific power machines. Therefore, a new cooling concept is proposed that further improves the thermal management of the hairpin winding and allows to increase the specific power of the machine. The proposed method is based on direct oil cooling (DOC) through the channel of the hollow conductor. Special inlets and outlets in each hairpin coil are arranged. Comparison of the proposed cooling arrangement with the traditional cooling of machine with hairpin winding is provided by applying finite element method (FEM).

articleTitle: Online Fault Diagnosis for Multiple Open-Circuit Faults in Multiphase Drives with Current Harmonics
abstract: In the event of open-circuit (OC) faults, electric machines suffer from torque deviations and undesired radial forces causing vibrations and noise. In safety-critical applications, multiphase machines are utilized because of their higher degrees of freedom (DOFs) for OC fault mitigation in post-fault operation, enabling fault-tolerant operation and preventing the system from further damage. Therefore, a reliable and fast fault diagnosis is crucial to monitor the systems' behavior. In this paper, a real-time fault diagnosis method for multiple-phase OC faults is developed using only the measured current sensor signals that are inherently available due to the control task. The proposed fault diagnosis method is independent of fundamental wave assumptions and electric interconnection knowledge. Advantageously, the proposed method gives reliable fault diagnosis results even if the measured currents include higher harmonic orders, which is frequently the case for high-performance permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs). Experiments on a test stand verify the immunity to false diagnosis under fast load changes and show the performance of the proposed fault diagnosis method in combination with a fault-tolerant control (FTC) strategy. Simultaneous and sequential triple OC faults are investigated for a twelve-phase (1 × 12) and a quadruple three-phase (4 × 3) PMSM at several operating points.

articleTitle: Vertical Vibration Control for Half-Vehicle with In-Wheel Motor-Suspension Integrated System Under Braking Condition
abstract: Considering the coupling impact of the vehicle braking strength, road surface excitation, and unbalanced vertical force on the vehicle vertical dynamics, a vertical vibration control strategy aimed at enhancing vehicle ride comfort is presented during braking condition. Initially, a vehicle dynamic model is built, involving switched reluctance motor drive system, vehicle braking system, and in-wheel switched reluctance motor-suspension integrated system. Then, the vibration response characteristics of the integrated system are discussed. Subsequently, considering the limitation of the traditional braking force distribution approaches, a partitioned braking force distribution approach is proposed and applied to ensure the vehicle braking performance. Furthermore, a linear quadratic regulator control approach optimized through genetic algorithm is proposed to decrease the vehicle vertical vibration. Finally, simulations are conducted to validate the efficacy of the proposed control methodology under braking condition. The results demonstrate that the introduced method comprehensively enhances the vehicle vertical dynamics.

articleTitle: Analysis of Externally Excited Synchronous Motors Operation Under Joule Losses Minimization Control
abstract: The interest in rare earth-free traction motors is significantly increasing due to cost and sourcing challenges related to rare earth hard ferromagnetic materials. Among rare earth-free solutions, the externally excited synchronous motor (EESM) is currently the most studied machine topology in automotive. In this paper, an analytical solution for a Joule losses minimization control strategy for EESMs is presented. The model is based on the assumption of linear inductances and constant stator and rotor resistances, and aims at identifying the optimal current references for each speed and torque request. The operating range of the motor is divided in different regions, depending on whether the stator current, rotor current or voltage result constrained or not. While analytical solutions for Joule losses minimization have already been presented in literature, in this work the model is developed with a higher level of generality, considering both the case in which the optimal control zone at partial load is constrained by rotor excitation current limit and the case in which it is limited by stator current. In addition, also the case in which the maximum rotor current is not sufficient to enter unity power factor operation at full load is considered. A separate finite element analysis is also proposed to evaluate the effects of magnetic saturation on the optimal control strategy. The aim of the work is to provide an insight and a clear interpretation of the EESM operation once controlled with a losses minimization strategy, possibly suggesting a control-oriented design approach of such machines.

articleTitle: High-Speed Induction-Machine Squirrel-Cage Rotor Mechanical Design Evaluation
abstract: The design of high-speed electrical machines requires pushing the boundaries in each area of the multidisciplinary design process to achieve a high-performance product. The design process needs to employ rapid and efficient, yet accurate enough and realistic design tools. This study focuses on exploring the design of a high-speed electric machine rotor, specifically concentrating on thick-laminated squirrel-cage structure. The study aims to evaluate different short-circuit ring configurations to identify a configuration that can be built without resorting to novel manufacturing methods. Utilizing the well-known finite element method, the study incorporates material yielding, an essential factor for accurately assessing contact status in multi-layered rotor structures. Analyzing the yielding is also crucial when assessing the realistic load capacity of the machine. Squirrel-cage configurations were analyzed based on a megawatt-sized machine from literature. Resulted maximum surface velocities of the case study rotor lined up with the high-performance squirrel-cage rotor presented in the literature.

articleTitle: Investigation on Insulation Failure Mechanisms of Stators used for E-Mobility
abstract: The upheaval in industry and in the private sector towards electrification and mobilization is associated with the increasing use of electric motors, for example in cars, bicycles, robots, wheelchairs and also in the aircraft industry. Therefore, developments on the production technology for E-motors are necessary in order to meet the increasing demand and to ensure all actual requirements. This development includes the quality and service life. This contribution describes insulation failure mechanisms that can occur in a stator and examines the effect on various diagnostic options. For this purpose, faults in the slot insulation of a stator are modeled and then investigated with regard to partial discharges and insulation resistance. The modeled faults, holes, cracks, conductive particles and the layer thickness, are varied in size and amount. In this study it was shown, that insulation resistance provides more valuable information about the magnitude and number of faults than PDIV.

articleTitle: Stationary Wave Flux Pump for Energisation in High Temperature Superconducting Machines
abstract: High Temperature Superconducting (HTS) machines are being developed to address mass issues in large direct drive generators for wind turbines, and for high power density propulsion motors and generators in aerospace applications. The standard method of energising HTS coils is by direct current injection through copper leads connected to HTS tapes. Since HTS coils must be strictly operated in cryogenic environments, current leads can bring considerable thermal loads because they bridge the ambient temperature with the cryogenic system. In the case of rotating coils, direct injection can be more challenging, because of the need to transfer large DC currents across a rotating joint, requiring the use of sliprings and brushes. In this paper the authors focus on the use of HTS flux-pumps to energise rotating HTS field coils used in HTS synchronous machine topologies. A new type of flux pump is presented, which is both stationary and is excited with single phase, unlike current technology which either have rotating parts or require complex power electronic control. Results are presented to show how the design variables affect performance.

articleTitle: Investigation on Stator Core Losses in High-Speed PMSM Considering Current Harmonics
abstract: Stator core losses are one of the major loss components in high-speed permanent magnet synchronous machines. The accurate analysis of the stator core losses is crucial to the thermal design and the operating efficiency of the machine. In this paper, issues such as minimum calculation time, minimum time step number and the influence of mesh settings during dynamic time-stepping finite element-based core losses evaluation are discussed. The analysis result can help to minimize the calculation time of core losses. The characteristics of flux density and the core losses under no load, sinusoidal current and current with harmonics are compared and the compositions of the core losses under different operating conditions are then analyzed. Finally, the possibility of modifying slot opening and carrier frequency to minimize the core loss is explored. It is concluded that careful selection of slot opening width and the yoke thickness can lead to both low core losses and satisfying torque.

articleTitle: Extension of Analytical Methods for AC Copper Loss Estimation in High-Speed Axial Flux Machines with Concentrated Flat Wire Coils
abstract: Modern trends in electrical machine design aim for high torque density and high power density within a cost-efficient framework. High power density suggests a shift towards high-speed operation. To meet these demands, high-speed axial flux machines (AFMs) are being investigated. Flat wires are chosen in the winding design of high-speed AFMs to accommodate the AC copper loss at the high-speed. A discrepancy is observed between the classical analytical method and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) in assessing the AC copper loss in such windings. This paper investigates the cause of this discrepancy and attempts to decompose the roots of AC copper loss. Building on the classical analytical method, which traditionally considers conductors of different phases on top of each other, this paper extends the method to cases where conductors from different phases are positioned next to each other. The validity and limitations of the proposed method are reported, comparing the results with FEA for different slot designs. The investigation shows that not only the conductor height but also the conductor width influences the AC copper loss, and an optimal aspect ratio can be derived based on the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improving Motor Torque Estimation and Energy Efficiency for an Electric Vehicle by Compensating the Influences of Initial Permanent Magnet Temperature
abstract: The torque production of IPMSMs depends not only on the d-q-currents but also on the temperature-dependent permanent magnet rotor flux. Therefore, to ensure accurate torque production, it is vital to know the permanent magnet temperature with sufficient accuracy at all times. Electric vehicle manufacturers are nowadays extensively using IPMSMs as electric drives. This paper explains the consequences of neglecting permanent magnet temperature estimation and the consequences of ignoring the estimation of the stator-winding temperature. The motor torque accuracy, demagnetisation, stator-resistance temperature adaptation, and motor efficiency are majorly impacted. The paper then theorises the possible ideas for determining initial permanent magnet temperature estimation. The paper focuses on the most ignored topic in most research articles based on the thermal modelling of electric motors, i.e., the initial temperature estimation of each thermal node and its algorithm using the non-volatile memory of the ECU. Finally, the results prove the necessity of implementing an initial temperature estimation algorithm, which reduces torque estimation errors and improves the electric vehicle's total energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Robust Optimization of a Stator Tooth Chamfering IPMSM for Electric Power Steering Applications
abstract: The impact of manufacturing errors on motor performance is a crucial issue in the mass production of electric motor products. However, robust indexes are complicated to consider in the design process due to the enormous computational complexity. This paper presents a surrogate- assisted robust optimization method that integrates sensitivity analysis with Pareto front infill criteria. The approach enables efficient sampling in the regions where the optimal solution is most probable, thereby ensuring the local generalization capability of the surrogate model. As a result, robust optimization of probabilistic manufacturing error variables is effectively accomplished. An interior permanent-magnet synchronous machine (IPMSM) employing the stator tooth chamfering technique to mitigate cogging torque is examined for electric power steering applications. To verify the effectiveness of this approach, a limited series of prototypes were fabricated and rigorously tested, confirming the practicality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Improved Methodology for Considering the Frequency-Dependent Behaviour of Electrical Machine Windings in Transient Simulation
abstract: The development of electrical machine winding models capable of predicting the inter-turn voltage distribution has been widely reported in the literature. However, the existing models have difficulty in accounting for the frequency evolution of the winding parameters during transient simulation. The aim of this paper is to present an improved method for incorporating the high frequency-dependent behaviour of electrical machine windings in transient simulation. First, the proposed lumped parameter model of the winding is presented. The particularity of the model is that it includes the resistive and inductive coupling between the turns of the winding. The parameters of the winding model are estimated using the finite element method and analytical equations. The circuit model incorporates frequency-dependent parameters through the utilization of behavioural volt-age sources. The proposed equivalent circuit is then transformed into a reduced nodal admittance matrix in order to estimate the node voltage at a particular turn in the frequency domain. An inverse Fast Fourier Transform is then performed to calculate the node voltage in the time domain. As a first step in the validation of the proposed methodology, a series of comparison tests with previous models have been carried out.

articleTitle: Density Analysis Based on Normalized Process Diagrams : A Comparative Review of Ferromagnetic Alloys Produced by Laser Powder Bed Fusion
abstract: This research explores additive manufacturing of magnetic materials via Selective Laser Melting (SLM), integrating insights from prior studies. Emphasizing density variation concerning applied energies, our methodology incorporates normalized process diagrams. This analysis revealing an identification of different density regions in the case of Fe-6.5%wt. Si alloy. These regions show the interplay between process parameters and thermophysical material properties, encompassing lack of fusion, keyhole pores and balling. Further, density variations of Fe-3% wt. Si, Fe-6.7%wt. Si, and Fe-6.9% wt. Si alloys are studied, highlighting the impact of silicon content on final density. The present study contributes to understand dynamic interactions shaping magnetic material density. By optimizing process parameters based on density considerations, microstructure tailoring becomes possible, and, so far, an optimization of the magnetic properties.

articleTitle: Toward an Accessible Electrical Conductivity Characterisation Method for Additively Manufactured Conductors
abstract: The use of metal Additive Manufacturing to form electrical winding and busbar components is gaining popularity as both a prototyping and a production tool due to the ability to realise complex geometry, unparalleled by other production methods, and advantages in digital rather than physical tooling. However, the many different manufacturing processes and feed-stock materials available, the number of parameters attributed to each process, and differences among Additive Manufacturing practitioners leads to significant variation in the resulting electrical material properties of fabricated components. Such data is critical at the design stage and throughout production for quality control. This paper presents a standardised serpentine sample geometry, test fixture, and measurement procedure to reliably determine the electrical conductivity and temperature coefficient of resistivity. The procedure is based on an existing standard while the sample geometry, test fixture and suggested apparatus are designed to be simple and accessible to encourage adoption across disciplines along the Additive Manufacturing production chain and end-application.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of the Local Heat Transfer Coefficient in a Rotating Hollow Rotor Shaft Liquid Cooling System for Electric Traction Motors
abstract: This paper presents the fluid flow and local heat transfer coefficient associated with a rotating liquid hollow rotor shaft cooling system for electric traction motors. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is utilized to simulate the fluid flow and heat transfer phenomena to obtain the local heat transfer coefficient. A comparison is conducted between a stationary and a rotating hollow rotor shaft cooling system using 50/50 ethylene glycol water mixture. The shaft rotation is found to alter the fluid flow through the development of vortices and a secondary flow due to the Coriolis and centrifugal effect. The alteration of the fluid flow is found to enhance the fluid turbulence, significantly increasing the local heat transfer coefficient when compared to the non-rotating case. This results in a significant decrease in the maximum operating temperature of the shaft surface. It is concluded that the local heat transfer coefficients change significantly along the length of the hollow shaft resulting in non-uniform temperature distributions. This can allow for the identification of regions of low thermal performance within the cooling system.

articleTitle: Recyclable Electrical Machine Designs: Current Approaches and Perspectives
abstract: The increasing demand for electrical machines underscores the urgent need to address their end-of-life disposal. Traditional designs rely on complex assemblies of diverse materials and pose significant challenges for recycling and resource recovery. This review explores current approaches and perspectives on designing recyclable electrical machines, emphasizing the integration of recyclability without sacrificing performance. Key materials are examined for their properties and recyclability. Design for Recyclability principles are highlighted through various case studies. The review concludes with comparative analyses of material choices and their impact on performance and recyclability. Findings demonstrate that low to mid-power applications are more adaptable to recyclable designs. Future research should focus on developing innovative design ideas and assessing their recyclability.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a 4-6 Brushless Doubly Fed Induction Generator
abstract: This paper provides an outline of the brushless doubly fed (induction) machine (BDFM) design process, introducing modifications to the comprehensive BDFM power ratings formula. The modifications introduced seek to simplify the calculation methodology for the D2L design coefficient, offering a more simplified approach. In this paper, insights regarding the selection process involving the stack length ratio, electric loading, and airgap flux density and distribution are presented. The analytical design methodology is subsequently applied to an 11 kW BDFM housed in a D225M frame, followed by optimization using the NSGA-II (Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II). This BDFM features a nested loop rotor, enabling unity power factor on the grid-connected winding.

articleTitle: Development of an Axial Flux SRM Through Additive Manufacturing
abstract: Axial-switched reluctance machines have a higher torque density compared to radial-switched reluctance machines, making them a preferred option for applications that require high torque. Due to the intricate three-dimensional design of axial machines, production poses substantial challenges. Additive manufacturing has simplified the process by allowing to produce complex shapes. This paper presents a systematic design approach that utilizes output equations to establish the geometrical parameters of a machine analytically. The proposed machine design was validated using 3D finite element analysis with JMAG software after the analytical phase. The study proposes a design feature to address the challenges associated with the mechanical assembly of machine. This design modification introduces a lip feature on the stator segments to mechanically join all the segments. Furthermore, this study evaluates the impact of this modification on the machine's performance by comparing it to a base design without this feature. The paper outlines the fabrication of a physical prototype utilizing Selective Laser Melting employing an advanced additive manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Minimizing Torque Ripple in 5-Phase Switched Reluctance Machines Using Half-Sinusoidal Current Pulses
abstract: Switched reluctance machines feature interesting characteristics such as manufacturing simplicity, no need for costly permanent magnets, excellent robustness, decoupled phases and high fault tolerance. Nevertheless, when designed according to the classic operation principle, i.e. featuring just 3 phases to be supplied with ideally rectangular current pulses possibly under deep saturation conditions, they exhibit large torque ripple, vibrations and noise. This paper proposes a different concept based on 5 phases to be supplied with half-sinusoidal current pulses under linear or mild-saturated conditions, ideally permitting to suppress torque ripple. The concept is investigated using a magnetically linear analytical model and is then validated by means of simulations including finite-element analysis, which confirm the theoretical expectations.

articleTitle: Intensified Field Winding Heat Transfer Through Triggered Axial Flow in Radial-Radial Ventilated Large Hydro Generators with Interpolar Air Guides
abstract: Detailed numerical conjugate heat transfer investigations of radial-radial (rim) ventilated generators with interpolar air guides have shown that axial flow components in the cavities between two neighboring field winding cooling fins occur. These axial flow components result in massively increased heat transfer coefficients especially for the field winding suction side and can be triggered for each generator with interpolar air guides by modifying the rim channel geometry only. Consequently, interpolar air guides cannot only be used to avoid unwanted flow patterns in the pole gap but also to intensify the field winding heat transfer for all rim ventilated generators. In this case they contribute to increase the utilization of the generator limits.

articleTitle: Mechanical Modelling of Electric-Machine Core Laminated Stack
abstract: A modelling strategy has been defined to predict the mechanical behaviour of a core laminated stack during the assembly phase of a rotor or a stator and its life cycle. First, the contact between two laminates or sheets is defined. Then, a scale transition procedure is introduced to simplify the behaviour of two sheets in contact, based on an energy equivalence. This method has been applied to an elastic behaviour. The results show a good approximation between full and approximated models.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of a Levitating Linear Motion Platform
abstract: This paper explores the application of a levitated linear motion platform implemented using linear flux-switching permanent magnet bearingless motors (LFSPM BMs). Flux-switching permanent magnet (FSPM) motor is an attractive motor type owing to its cost-effectiveness, which is achieved by placing the permanent magnets in the mover. Levitated linear motors are beneficial in special applications where, e.g., cleanliness and frictionless motion are needed. The paper focuses on accurate system modeling and control of a scaled -down proof-of-concept. The motor under study was modeled using the finite element method, yielding look-up tables of the force model, and by employing analytical equations of the motor. Simulation results are provided for a model-based levitation controller and a proportional-derivative (PD) traction controller. Challenges arise from the inherent force ripple when moving along the rail and from the slow inner loop bandwidth of the small-scale design of the system.

articleTitle: A Novel Axial Flux Magnetic Suspension Motor With Hysteresis Rotor for Heart Pumps
abstract: Bearingless motors can be used in special applications such as heart pumps due to the elimination of mechanical wear and contamination. The hysteresis motor has a rotor made of solid alloy which is resistant to high temperature, as well as better reliability and applicability. In this paper, a novel axial flux magnetic suspension hysteresis motor structure is proposed. The rotor is located between the upper and lower stators, and is actively controlled in rotation, axial and tilting motion. It has good stability and enough output torque, which can meet the needs in the application of heart pumps. The electromagnetic structure, working principle, tilt winding configuration and tilt characteristics are explained, and the tilt torque magnitude and stability of 4-phase and 6-phase tilt windings are compared. Experimental tests are in progress.

articleTitle: Active IGBT Temperature Equalization in Field Oriented Control Motor Drives by Magnetic Energy Management
abstract: This paper presents an active approach to equalizing the operating temperature of IGBT devices within three-phase inverters used in Field Oriented Control induction motor drives. The proposed approach represents a significant departure from previously developed techniques because managing the magnetic energy stored within the induction machine to periodically reduce the average current circulating across specific IGBTs. A key feature of this approach is its ability to control the operating temperature of the IGBTs of one leg, or even individual IGBTs, while driving the induction motor to deliver the required electromagnetic torque free of fluctuations. After providing an in-depth theoretical analysis of the proposed technique its consistency and dynamic performance are assessed by simulations. By actively equalizing the operating temperature of the six devices of the inverter, the expected mean time between failures can be significantly extended. Although this paper focuses on IGBT -based three-phase inverters, the outcomes can be readily applied to inverters using other types of power devices and with a different number of phases.

articleTitle: Design Strategies for Scalable and Modular Aerospace Electrical Machines
abstract: In his study, innovative design approaches for scalable and modular inverter-fed electrical machines, tailored for aerospace applications, are explored with the primary goal of achieving unparalleled power density within powertrain systems. Three distinct design frameworks are introduced: the utilization of separate machines for individual functions, the deployment of a singular machine capable of performing dual functions, and the adoption of a high-speed machine with gearbox configuration. Each concept is subjected to rigorous multi-objective optimization analysis, with an emphasis on both power density and operational efficiency, to determine the most optimal design strategy for revolutionizing aerospace electrification.

articleTitle: Analysis of Torque Upper Limit of Electrically-Excited Salient Machines by Flux Modulation Theory
abstract: Electrically-excited salient machines (EESMs) constructed with salient iron cores and stator-located windings have drawn increasingly more attention due to their compact structure, robust rotor and low cost. However, the torque performance of various EESMs, including synchronous reluctance machine (SynRM), brushless doubly-fed reluctance machine (BDFRM), vernier reluctance machine (VRM), and variable flux reluctance machine (VFRM), are different considering the different air-gap structures, slot/pole combinations and fed-in currents. This paper is devoted to propose a comprehensive analysis and comparison of various EESMs, and reveal the theoretical torque upper limit. According to flux modulation theory, the torque production mechanism is uniformly classified into two types, where the differences and relationships between various EESMs can be reflected by the corresponding working harmonic combination numbers and harmonic orders under the proposed condition 1 and 2. Moreover, the preferable slot/pole combinations and air-gap structures for each topology are determined.

Author Keywords: brushless doubly-fed reluctance machine (BDFRM) and variable flux reluctance machine (VFRM)

articleTitle: A New Approach for Diagnosis Demagnetization in a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Different Fault Severities Using Current Signals
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for detecting demagnetization across various severities of faults in a 1 kW prototyped permanent magnet synchronous motor utilizing current signals. The core of this detection technique is the variational autoencoder, which accurately reconstructs data while selecting optimal features for fault classification. The study not only assesses the detection method's effectiveness for demagnetization faults but also evaluates its performance for bearing and eccentricity faults. Furthermore, it examines the method's performance across different loads and speeds, both with and without feature extraction. The detection algorithm's performance is increased through the integration of principal component analysis and linear discriminant analysis as additional feature extraction techniques. Through performance evaluation, it is determined that the proposed method exhibits strong performance in detecting various classes of demagnetization faults, achieving a 99% accuracy when employing feature extraction. Additionally, compared to conventional machine learning methods, it demonstrates superior performance in terms of training time.

articleTitle: Early Stage Design of an Electric Drive Train for a Heavy Duty Transport Vehicle
abstract: This paper presents design considerations for the creation and optimization of the electric drive train (EDT) of an electric heavy duty vehicle (HDV). An analytical sizing tool is also created that takes into account the requirements and guidelines for HDVs, a comparison of state-of-the-art electric trucks, and an estimation of the physical demand of a sample long-haul transport drive cycle (DrC). As an EDT evaluation criterion, compliance with the ideal DrC of the vehicle is analyzed and a rough design for an axial flux machine is developed. By this method, the groundwork is laid to carry out a multi-domain optimization of the entire EDT in the future.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Closed-Loop Startup Strategy for Sensorless Permanent Magnet Motor Drive
abstract: This paper introduces an efficient startup approach for a sensorless Permanent Magnet Motor (PMM) drive. The proposed method utilizes a closed-loop strategy aimed at minimizing output power to reduce the current needed for the application's load torque. A particular closed-loop PI controller is used to stabilize the applied current reference, with the motor's output power serving as feedback. In addition, a parallel acceleration feedforward algorithm improves control response during speed changes. This method lessens drive losses common in the open-loop sensorless startup, especially where traditional stator flux-observer models for position estimation are ineffective at zero or low speeds. The shift from the open-loop to closed-loop sensorless control is smoother and more reliable, keeping the motor current near its optimal level. The controller's design and simulation in a precise discrete transient model shows this method's benefits over traditional open-loop startups that use the motor's rated current. This is evident in enhanced motor drive efficiency and stability.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Analytical Model of Large-Scale Doubly-Fed Induction Generator-Motor Based on Coefficient Transfer
abstract: In the variable speed pumped storage unit, the doubly-fed induction generator-motors (DFIGMs) often operate in the high saturation region within power control due to the extensive speed range. To address the issue of motor saturation effect analysis and enhance the calculation accuracy for various operating conditions, this paper proposes a high-saturation analytical calculation method for DFIGMs based on model coefficient transfer learning to analyze the electromagnetic characteristics under extreme operating conditions. The unsaturated condition source domain data were obtained by constructing an accurate subdomain model. Fourier transform was applied to decompose the air gap magnetic density obtained from both the analytical model and finite element model respectively, to achieve precise correction of undetermined coefficients for each harmonic. Consequently, a highly accurate and efficient analytical calculation model for DFIGMs under high saturation was developed. The harmonic and torque characteristics of 10 MW DFIGMs under overload conditions are analyzed based on the model. Subsequently, an experimental test is conducted on a prototype to validate the accuracy of the analytical transfer model.

articleTitle: Eddy Brake Reaction at Bus Structures of Medium-Large Caliber Electromagnetic Launchers
abstract: An important application for large-scale pulse power supplies (PPS) is electromagnetic launchers (EMLs). These devices turn stored electrochemical energy, measured in megajoules (MJ), into linear mechanical energy. Simulations play a vital role in EML research due to the presence of challenging physical conditions. As the level of operational risk increases, the addition of more energy to the system enhances the accuracy of the model. We encountered an unforeseen surge in rail current during our recent 8 MJ launch experiments. Underestimating peak current can be dangerous due to the potential risks it poses, such as armature stall leading to contact meltdown and overheating of cables. This phenomenon did not occur with small and medium calibre EMLs, specifically the EMFY-l and EMFY-2. A comprehensive analysis is performed to reveal the fundamental physical root-cause for the current overshoot. It has been found that the bus structure acts as a shield against eddy currents, leading to a decrease in the machine's inductance. This reduction is crucial as it has an impact on the dynamics of the start-up launch. The hypothesis is tested using a combi-nation of simulations and experimental results. Electromagnetic calculations are investigated by measuring rail currents, breech voltages, and muzzle voltages. The results demonstrated a strong correlation with the experimental data, particularly when the bus structure was explicitly modelled.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization of Unbalanced Magnetic Pull for Eccentric Doubly-Fed Induction Motor
abstract: Due to the frequent switching of working conditions, the large doubly-fed induction motors (DFIMs) utilized in variable speed pumping units are subjected to intense hydraulic shock, thereby significantly increasing the risk of rotor eccentricity fault and posing a substantial threat to the safe operation of the motor. This paper proposes a method for suppressing the unbalanced magnetic force in DFIMs caused by eccentricity, through the injection of excitation compensation current in groups. Firstly, the air gap magnetic field of DFIMs with eccentricity is modeled using the subdomain method. Then, the optimal compensation current is efficiently calculated using the eccentric subdomain model in conjunction with the particle swarm optimization algorithm. Finally, the proposed method is implemented on a 10MW DFIM. By injecting the optimal compensation current, the unbalanced magnetic pulling force caused by eccentricity is effectively suppressed. The comparison with the finite element simulation results showed that the unbalanced magnetic pulling force is reduced by 81.6%.

articleTitle: Duty-Ratio-Based Direct Torque Control Strategy for a Novel Dual-Armature Winding Dual-PM Machine With Array Torque Components
abstract: A duty-ratio-based direct torque control (DTC) strategy for a novel dual-armature winding dual-PM machine (DWDM) with array torque components is proposed in this paper. The novel DWDM has armature windings and PMs arranged in both the stator and rotor, which enables the machine to output array-distributed torque components. The mathematical models of the stator and rotor torque components are developed, respectively. DTC enables the direct control of the torque components of DWDM. By adjusting the torque allocation coefficient, the ratio of the stator and rotor output torque components can be regulated. However, conventional switching-table-based DTC DWDM drives are afflicted by large torque ripple due to the unbalanced effect of torque variations within a sampling period. Therefore, a duty-ratio-based DTC strategy is proposed, taking into account the effect of the torque allocation coefficient. Finally, the torque ripple of both the stator and rotor torque components can be reduced using the proposed duty ratio determination method. The simulation results verified the superiorities of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Detection and Mitigation of Hotspots in Electrical Machine Windings Using 3D Printing Technology
abstract: Electrical machines are integral to various industries, and their reliable operation is crucial for smooth processes. This paper investigates the common reasons for electrical machines failures and proposes effective mitigation strategies. The advent of additive manufacturing (AM) technology has unlocked previously inapplicable design possibilities, making them feasible and practical in ways that were not possible with conventional techniques. This research explores innovative design solutions in the fabrication of machine windings and their thermal management components. With AM technology, the study involves the design and prototyping of 3D-printed coils specifically built for high-power density electrical machines. The primary causes of hotspot in the machine windings are identified, and their locations are detected by scanning the coil at stranded level. Mitigation measures, such as advanced cooling, and improved materials are presented to minimize winding failures. Finite element modeling is employed to compare the performance of these innovative 3D coils with conventional windings in the high-frequency domain. The findings reveal that the 3D coil designs offer a combination of improved performance, simplified manufacturability, and significant weight reduction.

articleTitle: Fast Procedure for the Electromagnetic Sizing of Axial Flux PM Motors
abstract: This paper presents an algorithm for the preliminary design of three-phase surface mounted permanent magnet axial flux motors. The algorithm starts from a limited number of machine specifications, related to the rated performance, few geometrical specifications, and the main material properties. The sizing of the stator and rotor lamination is accomplished through self-consistent analytical formulations. Then, the parameters of the machine equivalent circuit are computed considering both distributed and fractional-slot concentrated winding arrangements. To assess the accuracy of the proposed algorithm, two study cases are presented. The validation is carried out comparing the performance predicted by the proposed procedure with 3D finite element analyses. The results show good agreement between the sizing algorithm and the numerical simulations.

articleTitle: CDC-GANs: Bridging Innovation and Efficiency in E-Machine Design with Advanced Generative Models
abstract: This paper introduces the Correlation-Diversified Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (CDC-GAN), a new model that automates and speeds up electric machine (E-machine) design exploration. Traditional methods in this field are slow and rely heavily on costly simulations. Without extensive simulations, CDC-GAN overcomes these limitations by generating diverse design candidates that align with key performance indicators (KPIs). By combining conditioning correlation and diversity losses, CDC-GAN produces designs that are both varied and performance-aligned. Our results show that CDC-GAN helps to significantly streamline the design process of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet machines, offering a promising solution for near-optimal design with fewer variables and faster optimization. It also allows efficient optimization in multi-physics and inverse E-machine design. This puts into place the strengths of CDC-GAN, leading to a significant reduction of the need for resource-consuming simulations and iterative design adjustments, thereby accelerating the design procedures and ensuring high accuracy, diversity, and meeting the KPI requirement—these are improvements over traditional approaches in efficiency and effectiveness. The capability of such a deep-learning framework in improving E-machine design efficiency and innovation is detailed.

articleTitle: Influence of Slot-Pole Combination on Electromagnetic Performance and Efficiency of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Motor for Electric Vehicles
abstract: This paper focuses on the effects of slot-pole combinations on the electromagnetic performance, and efficiency of motors based on axial-flux permanent magnet motors (AFPMs) with fractional-slot concentrated windings (FSCWs). The aim is to find the slot-pole combination scheme with the best overall performance: increasing the winding factor, increasing the torque density, reducing cogging torque, reducing the harmonic effects of the magnetic potential, decreasing the effects of eddy current losses, and improving the overall motor efficiency. In this study, a three-dimensional finite element analysis method was used, and the conclusions comparatively analyzed the electro-magnetic performance of different slot-pole coordination schemes and confirmed the best performance of the 24-slot-28-pole configuration. In order to verify the accuracy of the analyzed results, a 24-slot-28-pole prototype was finally successfully fabricated, and the accuracy of the analyzed data was verified by experimental results.

articleTitle: Hollow Direct Air Cooled Rotor Windings: Experimental Verification
abstract: This paper presents the experimental verification of a cooling concept based on hollow direct air cooling windings for the rotor of an electrically excited synchronous machine (EESM) with the application of traction drive for electric vehicles (EVs). Developing the performance of EESMs is important for the EV industry since it is today so reliant on permanent magnets. The idea behind the cooling concept is explained and the prototype machine made for the experimental verification presented. The results of the experimental work show that the direct air cooled hollow windings can maintain a continuous current corresponding to a copper current density of 21.1 A/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> or a rotor slot current density of 8.5 A/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimisation of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Motor for Super-Car Application
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to the design and multi-objective optimisation of a double stator axial flux permanent magnet (AFPM) motor, specifically tailored for super-car applications. The process begins by extracting performance and efficiency criteria for the electric motor based on vehicle specifications and established driving cycles. An analytical design process is then conducted, considering the requirements from the driving cycle analysis. This stage determines the geometric and electromagnetic parameters used to model three e-motors with different slot and pole combinations. The performance of these motors is evaluated to ensure they meet the torque and power demands of the mission profiles. A Quasi-3D FE modeling approach is used to verify the analytical design, followed by a multi-objective optimisation process with the genetic algorithm (GA). Finally, the three optimised motors are compared based on driving cycle performance and energy consumption to select the final design.

articleTitle: Comparative Stability Analysis of IPMSM and SPMSM Machines Under Flux-Weakening Control
abstract: The flux-weakening (FW) method is employed to extend the operation speed range and maximize the torque/power capability. Compared to the feedforward FW control method, the feedback FW control method is simple and robust against parameter mismatches. The stabilities of two forms of feedback FW control method, i.e., d-axis current-based voltage feedback FW control (DCVFC) and current angle-based voltage feedback FW control (CAVFC), are investigated in this paper. Firstly, the stability characteristics of two FW control methods are analyzed in interior permanent magnet synchronous machines (IPMSMs) and surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous machines (SPMSMs), respectively. Then, a comparative analysis is conducted between IPMSMs and SPMSMs under two FW control methods. The findings indicate that there are inherent differences not only between the DCVFC and CAVFC methods when applied to the same machine but also between IPMSM and SPMSM machines when the same FW control method is utilized.

articleTitle: Core Loss Tracking of Stator Core Testing via Inverse Jiles-Atherton Hysteresis Model
abstract: This paper presents a novel optimization strategy for fitting the Jiles-Atherton (JA) hysteresis model to experimental stator yoke core loss measurements and locked-rotor IPMSM calculations. The first study aims to identify a single set of JA model parameters that track sample core losses at different magnetization levels at a given frequency: the analytical model is compared with finite element method simulations that include hysteresis modeling and core losses. The challenges of the second calculation are the inclusion of PM in the FEM simulation with the JA model, the torque computation, and the comparison with conventional calculation methods for soft magnetic cores. The FEM calculations have been performed with the Comsol multiphysics, which allows the use of the JA model.

articleTitle: Temperature Compensation for Measured Efficiency Maps of an Electric Drive Unit
abstract: In variable speed applications, one objective of an electrical drive system is to maximize efficiency across a wide torque-speed range. To achieve this, efficiency maps are derived through simulations or measurements. This work presents the creation of efficiency maps for motor and inverter based on dedicated measurements, with a focus on addressing the problem of varying temperatures during the large number of required sample points. To obtain representative and reliable efficiency maps, a method is presented to harmonize all measurements to a common temperature.

articleTitle: LCC-S Compensated Wireless Power Transfer: System Optimization Using Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper presents a novel technique based on Genetic Algorithms for the design of Inductive Wireless Power Transfer systems with LCC-S compensation. The proposed approach sizes the primary coil and selects the resonant tank components to achieve the desired output power with high transfer efficiency for any given load connected to the receiver coil. Mathematical models for self-inductance and mutual inductance are integrated into the algorithm, allowing the inclusion of the primary coil geometry and the system positioning (horizontal alignment and distance between coils) as optimization variables. A Monte Carlo analysis is implemented to investigate the effect of component values and positioning variations on the output power and efficiency. A simulated case study is proposed to illustrate the functioning of the algorithm. The presented methodology is thought to be highly flexible, easy to adapt to other compensation configurations and tailored to meet specific requirements resulting in a valuable instrument for the design of wireless power transfer systems.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization for Enhancing Electric Machine Performance: A Review
abstract: Exploring the design space is essential in the pursuit of developing high-performance and power-dense electric machines. This article explores the transformative potential of topology optimization (TO) in enhancing the performance of electric machines. Conventional techniques for optimizing the design of electric machines use optimization algorithms to determine geometric variables within a predefined range. However, these methods are limited by manufacturing constraints and the designer's expertise in parameterization. On the other hand, topology optimization aims to enhance the performance of electric machines by manipulating the distribution of materials as a design factor. The enhancement is facilitated by additive manufacturing (AM), particularly via the manufacturing of intricate metal parts. In this paper, the main concepts of topology optimization in electric machines are reviewed. Firstly, the requirement for topology optimization is illustrated, and both the achievements and challenges of this technique over the traditional parametric optimization are described. Then, a description is given of different topology optimization methods that were reported in the literature. Finally, the development opportunities of this technology are shown in the electric machine design field.

articleTitle: Measurement-Based Optimal Current Angle Identification of an Electric Drive Unit
abstract: This work targets analyzing the system efficiency of a permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) and its associated power electronics based on measurements. Therefore, a test bench is built and efficiencies of the motor and the power electronics are measured over the full torque-speed range of the motor under test, where the current angle of the motor and the PWM frequency of the voltage source inverter (VSI) is varied. From these measurements, temperature-harmonized efficiency maps are derived and optimal current angle values for VSI-, PMSM-, and system efficiency are evaluated. In addition, the differences between motor-optimal, inverter-optimal and system- optimal current angles are examined.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Flux-Switching PM and EE Machines with Dual Armature Winding Configuration
abstract: Flux-switching electrically excited (FSEE) machines offer appealing advantages, including low cost, no risk of demagnetization, and good flux regulation capability. Nonetheless, they typically exhibit much lower torque density compared with flux-switching permanent magnet (FSPM) machines. To overcome this limitation, FSEE machines with dual armature (DA) windings wounded on both stator and rotor teeth are proposed by full utilization of rotor space. It is found that increasing field current is not effective to enhance torque output for both the FSEE and DA-FSEE machines, because it deteriorates flux leakage for the stator armature winding. In contrast, the rotor side of the DA-FSEE machine generates relatively large torque per unit loss. As unique for DA-FSEE machines, the strong interaction between the two sets of armature windings entails an optimal combination of stator and rotor armature current phase angles for high torque output, whereas the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>=O control is optimal for FSEE and DA-FSPM machines. The final results show that the DA-FSEE machine can generate up to 75% more torque than the FSEE machine.

articleTitle: A Synergistic Suppression Method of Noise and Torque Ripple for PM Motor with Axial Heterogeneous Structure
abstract: The optimal suppression scheme of permanent magnet (PM) motor noise is often not the optimal suppression scheme of torque ripple, which is a contradiction point in the multi-objective optimization design of noise. In this paper, a synergistic suppression method of noise and torque ripple based on axial heterogeneous structure is proposed. First of all, the principle of synergistic suppression of torque ripple and motor noise by using the axial heterogeneous structure is introduced. Besides, noise analysis of axial homogeneous and heterogeneous structures is clarified in detail. Then, the method is applied to a 48-slot/8-pole PM motor, and the optimal angle of skew is determined by the finite element method (FEM). One rotor segment is slotted to suppress the motor noise without affecting the suppression of torque ripple. Finally, the synergistic suppression effect of noise and torque ripple is verified by FEM.

articleTitle: Optimizing an Interior-Permanent-Magnet Tooth-Coil-Winding Traction Motor for its Entire Operating Range
abstract: Design and optimization of an interior-permanent magnet motor (IPM) with tooth-coil-windings (TCWs) for traction motors are studied. Main goals are to deliver high torque and low torque ripple in the entire range of operation with lowest possible magnet usage. Design of an IPM-TCW motor with acceptable torque ripple in its entire operation range is challenging due to several reasons such as variation of harmonics of stator and rotor current linkages with saturation, slotting effects, and unity winding factor for all harmonics (for 12 slot 8 pole). Moreover, torque ripple varies based on the requested current angle and current density. In this study, an effective optimization method is proposed to reach an acceptable average torque and torque ripple in the whole range of operation. To further decrease the torque ripple utilization of notches on the rotor surface and semi magnetic wedges in the stator are proposed and compared with rotor skewing as an alternative. A model of IPM traction motors, with single V positioned magnets for an electric motorcycle is implemented and investigated. The Optimized machine has a power rating of 6 kW with maximum speed of 10,000 r/min operating speed with a 48 V battery. Finite element method is utilized to optimize the geometry of the IPM motor.

articleTitle: A Scaling Procedure for Electrically-Excited Synchronous Machines Utilizing Flux and Loss Maps
abstract: Electrically-excited synchronous machines are a promising alternative to permanent magnet-based counterparts for traction applications. Besides being rare-earth magnet free, EESMs offer great flexibility of control and high efficiency over a wide range of speed and torque values. This paper introduces a rapid and precise method for scaling the dimensions of electrically-excited machines, leveraging a reference design as a starting point. The proposed procedure utilizes the pre-calculated flux and loss maps of one existing machine to ensure compliance with new peak torque and power, maximum operating speed, voltage, and current specifications, all achieved within minimal computational time. The efficiency map and operating limits of the scaled machine are rapidly derived without necessitating additional finite-element simulations. The efficacy of the procedure is demonstrated by scaling the electrically-excited traction motor of the Renault Zoe to match the performance of the permanent magnet synchronous motor found of the Nissan Leaf drivetrain.

articleTitle: Design, Construction and Test of a Magnetically Geared Induction Machine
abstract: This paper describes the realization and the test of a 1 kW- 45 rpm magnetically geared induction machine. The principle of operation and the design procedure are firstly described, then the prototype construction is detailed. Finally, measurement results are presented and compared to the computations under full load conditions. It is the first prototype for this type of machine never built and tested under rated condition.

articleTitle: Analytical Calculation of the Airgap Flux in PM Vernier Machine Considering Pole Transition Over Slots Effect
abstract: Based on the flux modulation theory, PM vernier machine has features including high torque density, low cogging torque, which makes it preferable for low-speed-high-torque fields such as marine propulsion system and wind generator. Accurate calculation of the airgap flux densities is significant for the analysis and optimization of electromagnetic performances in PM vernier machines. Based on conventional MMF-permeance model, the radial airgap flux density can be calculated instantly but with relatively low accuracy, while it cannot calculate tangential flux. Based on finite element analysis or subdomain model, the radial and tangential airgap flux can be calculated precisely. However, these methods need longer time to solve matrix equations. In this paper, through mirror magnetic circuit and leakage flux circuit analysis, the calculation error brought by pole-transition-over-slot effect in vernier machines is corrected. Then, through modified complex MMF-permeance model, the airgap radial and tangential flux densities are calculated precisely and instantly. On this basis, the no-load back EMF of PM vernier machine is calculated, and the calculation result is proved to be corrected combining FEA method.

articleTitle: A Slot Model for Loss Estimation in Superconducting AC Electrical Machine Windings
abstract: The use of superconducting AC windings in rotating electrical machines is usually avoided due to the non- negligible hysteresis losses of superconductors. However, if these AC losses are mitigated, their implementation may allow to further increase the power density of electrical machines. This paper proposes a methodology for evaluating the AC losses in superconducting tapes when applied to the realization of slotted stator windings in AC electrical machines. In particular, the approach allows to reduce the computational requirements when the geometrical nature of the considered superconducting electrical machine requires 3D finite-element models, as in the case of axial flux machines. The machine is first simulated with a 3D FEM model without superconductors. Then, using a 2D single-slot FEM model, the superconducting AC losses are computed. The methodology is applied to a case study of an axial flux permanent magnet machine with AC superconducting stator windings. The model is validated by comparing the magnetization and the transport current losses estimated in the superconductors by the FEM simulations with those by analytical formulations.

articleTitle: Achieving Greater Efficiency in Long-Distance Applications: The Novel Implementation and Validation of a Linear Flux-Switching Permanent Magnet Motor
abstract: Linear efficient high-speed transportation is increasingly introduced for continental travel, e.g. maglev trains and hyperloop applications. The urge for such novel modes of transportation is a result of the trend current society has developed: travelling longer distances in a shorter amount of time. A key part of an efficient mode of transport is an efficient motor. This paper describes the implementation of a 2.5 kW Linear Flux Switching Permanent Magnet (LFSPM) machine for linear high-speed transportation. Special attention is given to the optimization and performance analysis of energy efficiency, with a key consideration being its operational air-gap of 15 mm. Prototype validation shows an average motor efficiency of 82.4 % and a regenerative braking efficiency of 96.8 %.

articleTitle: Impact of the Control Strategy of a Multiphase Non-Sinusoidal PMSM with Phase-Shifted Stars on Non-Intrusive Fault Indicators
abstract: Multi-star permanent-magnet synchronous machines (PMSM) are more and more used in several domains. They are fault-tolerant and have a high torque-to-power density ratio and a good efficiency at a variable speed operating. Moreover, when the stars comprise 3 phases each, they can be coupled to converters that are originally designed for 3-phase machines. Besides, two approaches can be used for the study of a multiphase machine with phase-shifted stars: a 3-phase approach, where each star is considered as a 3-phase machine, and a multiphase approach, where all phases are considered together. Both approaches are used more specifically for the field-oriented control of the machine. However, they do not lead to the same global performances. In this paper, the impact of the control strategy on the evolution of non-intrusive fault indicators is studied in the case of a 9-phase PMSM, with three 3-phase stars phase-shifted by an angle of 40°.

articleTitle: Line-Start Permanent Magnet Machines for Low-Power Applications
abstract: The improvement of efficiency is one of the main areas of research in electrical machines today. Three-phase induction machines are widely used in industry, motivating researchers to explore methods to increase their efficiency or replace them with more efficient alternatives. A line-start synchronous machine is a promising machine design for achieving high-efficiency classes even for low-power applications. The main contribution of this paper is to show the achievable performance of the LSPMSM by simply replacing the rotor of an induction machine. In this work, two different geometries suitable for low-power machines are optimized and studied in terms of electromagnetic parameters. Finally, the results of the start-up simulations for both machine designs are presented. The presented method shows that by replacing the induction machine rotor with a line-start permanent magnet rotor, it is possible to significantly enhance machine efficiency, even for low-power applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Electromagneticthermal Coupling Performance for High-torquedensity PMSM based on Multi-dimensional Correction Techniques
abstract: To address the precision limitation of traditional thermal models and the computational inefficiency of electromagnetic-thermal coupling finite element models, this work proposes a multidimensional correction-based electromagnetic-thermal coupling design optimization method for electric machines. Firstly, this method corrects the sensitive parameters in the analytical lumped parameters thermal network model (LPNM) based on prior information from historical experimental data to ensure the accuracy for thermal performance analysis. Subsequently, to enhance computational efficiency, a large number of low-fidelity (LF) samples are obtained using the corrected thermal model in a serial electromagnetic-thermal field calculation manner, complemented by a small number of high-fidelity (HF) samples obtained from the electromagnetic-thermal coupling simulation model. Then, by employing a transfer learning technique, the data information from the low- to high-fidelity sample sets is comprehensively utilized to train a multi-fidelity (MF) surrogate model for the final optimization. The proposed method applied to a high-torque-density aerospace propulsion permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with short-term strong overload capability, it not only significantly improves the accuracy of LPNM, but also reduces the training sample acquisition time by over 50% under the same model accuracy. Finally, a prototype is tested to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: 3D Multibody Simulation of Realistic Rolling Bearing Defects for Fault Classifier Development
abstract: Rolling bearing faults stand out as the most prevalent type of fault in electrical machines. In this study, we leveraged geometry-based 3D multibody simulation to facilitate data-driven fault diagnosis. A comprehensive dataset was generated, encompassing data from both healthy and faulty bearings with realistic outer ring and inner ring faults of different types and sizes, operating at varying rotational speeds. Spectral analyses of the simulated bearing shaft displacement data proved that the bearing faults consistently appear at expected characteristic fault frequencies, with peak amplitudes correlating to the given fault size and rotation speed. Using the simulated data, we evaluated numerous feature engineering methods for machine learning-based fault classification. The classification results demonstrated a successful differentiation of simulated faults, whether on the outer ring or inner ring, from the healthy counterparts.

articleTitle: Wound Rotor Synchronous Motor Design for a Mining Application
abstract: The rising global focus on environmental issues and strict regulations on greenhouse gas emissions are propelling a significant shift towards widespread electrification of wheeled vehicles. The high costs and decreasing availability of rare earth materials, along with their environmental impact, require exploring alternatives that minimise or eliminate their usage. This momentum extends comprehensively to the off-highway sector. This paper proposes the design feasibility of a wound rotor synchronous machine to replace an interior permanent magnet motor in a mining truck propulsion system. The evaluation encompasses crucial parameters such as torque, torque ripple, efficiency, thermal overload capacity, dimensions, and structural constraints, necessitating in-depth finite element electromagnetic, thermal, and structural analyses. Cost reduction and constructive simplicity are the guidelines of the project. Three optimal configurations emerge as prime candidates from an optimisation study, each meticulously assessed and compared against the defined design criteria. This comprehensive analysis conclusively demonstrates that the proposed wound rotor motor perfectly meets the performance expectations, positioning this machine type as optimal contender to interior permanent magnet motors in mining truck applications.

articleTitle: A New Hybrid Control Strategy in Flux-Weakening Region for High Performance Traction IPMSM
abstract: This paper investigates a novel hybrid flux weakening (FW) control scheme for interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) drives operating in a wide DC-link voltage range. Due to possible fluctuations in the motor parameters or considering dc-link voltage variation, the available voltage margin can be really too small and therefore the dynamic performance is degraded. One of the main objectives of the proposed FW regulator is to maintain the modulation index within a certain range, in order to exploit most of the battery voltage and minimize the losses and total harmonic distortion (THD) of the power converter. To control the motor in the FW region the proposed method exploits a hybrid control strategy based on a feed-back voltage controller feeding a virtual DC voltage variation into a DC-voltage, torque, and speed dependent look-up table (LUT) which sets the optimal current references also considering variable motor inductances.

articleTitle: A Saturation Model Based on a Simplified Equivalent Magnetic Circuit for Permanent Magnet Machines
abstract: This paper proposes an explicit mathematical model to describe the nonlinear behavior of the permanent magnet synchronous reluctance machine. Although different models for the synchronous reluctance machines are available, extending them to the case of the permanent magnet machine is not trivial due to the effect of the permanent magnets on the rib saturation. This work uses a simplified equivalent magnetic circuit to derive the structure of the proposed model. A nonlinear reluctance is introduced to model the rib saturation. It can be added to the existing model for the synchronous reluctance machine to take into account the effect of the permanent magnets. A simple fitting procedure based on the steepest descent method is proposed to estimate the parameters of the model.

articleTitle: Direct-Drive Wind Turbine Generator Vibration Induced by High-Order Air-Gap Nonuniformity
abstract: Direct-drive (DD) permanent magnet (PM) wind turbine generators (WTGs) require a substantial amount of expensive rare-earth PM material in their construction. The quantity of PM material required depends on the air-gap clearance, yet despite the importance of this parameter studies on DD PM WTG design commonly employ simple “rules of thumb” to determine its value. Vibration is often cited as a limiting factor for electrical machine air-gap clearance specification: if nonuniformity of the air-gap is significant then vibration may be excessive. This is well documented for conventional high-speed machines but there is limited information available for DD PM WTGs which differ in their behaviour due to their high pole count, large-scale, and low rotational speeds. In this work, the mechanism in which nonuniformity of a DD PM WTG air-gap leads to vibration via air-gap radial Maxwell stress harmonics is investigated. An analytical model for determining the air-gap radial Maxwell stress harmonics is introduced and validated through full-scale 2D finite element method (FEM) simulation of the International Energy Agency (IEA) 15 MW reference WTG. It is shown how air-gap nonuniformity can introduce a wide variety of air-gap radial Maxwell stress harmonics that have the potential to induce problematic vibration.

articleTitle: Comparison of a Direct Drive and a Geared Drive for Electric Light Sport Aircraft
abstract: This paper compares two drive concepts for an electric light sport aircraft (LSA): a direct drive and a geared drive with a transmission ratio of 4.5. According to sizing estimates, this ratio minimizes the system overall weight representing a considerable advantage in this application.
