The design process and assumptions are illustrated before evaluating the final designs on their weight and specific power. The drive weight is indeed reduced by 38 %. The performance comparison of the two drive systems is made across the entire operating region of the motors by calculating performance maps with a regression model fitted on finite element analysis simulations. The efficiency, loss distribution and mission energy demand are discussed.

articleTitle: Influence of a combined star-delta winding on the operation behavior of a line start permanent magnet synchronous machine
abstract: This paper investigates a combined star-delta winding for a line start permanent magnet synchronous motor and compares it with a standard star winding by analytical, Finite Element and experimental methods. The winding increases the machine's d- and q-axes inductances and induced voltage. At grid operation, this yields lower stator currents and stator ohmic losses as well as lower flux and core losses. Circulating currents in the delta sub-winding are found to be a minor problem at the investigated prototype.

articleTitle: Offline Parameter Estimation of Isotropic Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Based on Regular Operational Data and Probabilistic Error Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a novel estimation method of the stator resistance and rotor flux linkage in isotropic permanent magnet synchronous machines. Rather than using ad hoc tests or signal injection required by conventional offline and online approaches, the proposed method aims at estimating the motor parameters using data collected during the regular motor operation. To solve the rank deficiency issue that affects the parameter estimation problem, the proposed method exploits data from two different steady states of the motor. An estimation error analysis which considers the paramater variation, the measurement errors and their stochastic nature is proposed to support the choice of the motor steady states that optimize the estimation accuracy. The proposed estimation approach is validated on a dataset generated by means of a high-fidelity Simulink model also analysing the method's robustness against the variation of the algorithm parametrization, i.e. its hypothesis.

articleTitle: A Primary-Controlled Wireless Switched Reluctance Motor with Receiving Coil Multiplexing
abstract: Wireless motors have the potential to greatly enhance air tightness, waterproofness, and dustproofness in confined spaces. Currently, one of the most promising areas of research in this field is wireless switched reluctance motors (WSRM). However, previous works of WSRMs still face challenges such as complex motor structures and a lack of efficient and simple speed control methods. This paper presents an innovative solution by introducing a primary-controlled WSRM structure based on secondary coil multiplexing. This structure successfully reduces the number of secondary coils by half. The article proposes a novel dual-band resonant compensation circuit that utilizes a secondary receiving coil to establish two independent power channels, effectively supplying energy to the two motor windings. Furthermore, the compensation circuit enables multi-channel constant current output, providing the necessary hardware foundation for direct control of the motor winding current on the primary side. Detailed analysis is conducted on the circuit structure and current status to achieve closed-loop speed control. To validate the proposed system and the accuracy of the analysis, an experimental platform was built.

articleTitle: Consideration of Thermal Ageing in Digital Twins of Automotive-Grade Electric Motors
abstract: Lumped-parameter thermal networks (LPTN) feature an excellent tradeoff between computational cost and accuracy, and are an effective option to model thermal phenomena in electric motors. The key to obtaining a high-fidelity LPTN model resides in the identification of its parameters. These, however, may experience modifications over time. Thermal ageing is one of the main causes of the gradual deterioration of the insulation system in electric motors, which leads to changes in the thermophysical properties of its dielectric materials. This effect considerably decreases the expected lifetime of the insulation. Hence, thermal ageing should be considered in order to increase the fidelity of the LPTN models. In this work, an experimental campaign is presented together with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations to obtain a law of deterioration of the equivalent conductivity of the insulation system in a complete automotive-grade stator. The obtained rules are subsequently implemented in LPTNs. These can increase the fidelity of the representations used in digital twins (DTs) of motors. Indeed, the thermal characterization obtained in this work is to be implemented in an eMotor DT, where the virtual model is bidirectionally connected to a motor in a test bench used for model-based validation and model calibration.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Static Eccentricity Between Squirrel-Cage Induction and Wound-Field Flux Switching Machines
abstract: The practical manufacturing of electrical machines is vulnerable to inaccuracies during production and assembly, leading to rotor-stator misalignments. This misalignment creates an uneven air-gap magnetic density, significantly impacting machine performance. Utilizing finite element analysis, this study is used to evaluate and compare the electromagnetic performance of both the squirrel cage induction motor (SCIM) and wound-field flux switching machine (WFFSM) under 0%, 10% and 40% static eccentricity. The magnetic flux density near excited poles increases with eccentricity, distorting torque waveforms. Developed torque decreases up to 12.3% for induction motor and 8.4% for flux switching motor at 40% eccentricity. Torque ripple variation reaches 91% for induction motor and 72.2% for flux switching motor. Core losses rise to 10.96% for induction motor and 10.52% for flux switching motor, decreasing efficiency by 1.16% and 1.1% respectively. This study provides quantitative insights into performance deterioration mechanisms and aids understanding machine behavior under eccentricity.

articleTitle: Integrated Modern Technologies for Teaching in Electric Engineering Laboratories
abstract: In this paper, the transformation of a set of synchronous machines in a workstation that integrates modern technology is presented. The transformation is realized following a paradigm composed by four characteristics: Industrial equipment incorporation; variables visualization, monitoring, and registration; safety and ergonomics; and connectivity and communication. The incorporation of industrial equipment is illustrated using pictures and schematic diagrams. The workstation improves traditional laboratory practices and creates the opportunity for new laboratory tests motivating the students to involve in the topic of synchronous machines. The results presented in this paper make evident the opportunities that arise when updating a set of synchronous machines that exist in power engineering laboratories for teaching.

articleTitle: A Feasibility Study of Oil Spray Cooling on the Stator Core Outer Surface of Electric Motors for Automotive Applications
abstract: The paper presents a feasibility study of oil spray cooling on the outer surface of a stator core for traction electric motor applications. Combined experiments and thermal simulations lead to the conclusion that oil spray cooling on stator laminations may be a more effective cooling approach than water jacket cooling. Tests are carried out on a single tooth segment as well as on a full stator. A unique data set of the Heat Transfer Coefficient (HTC) of oil on lamination stacks is presented, including the influence of spray angle and flow rate. Test results show that oil spray cooling on lamination outer surface can achieve a high HTC locally but lead to significant temperature variation around a stator. The results also identify optimal fluid flow rate, and recommendations on nozzle shape. Thermal simulation is carried out to compare oil spray cooling with water jacket cooling.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic and Mechanical Design Optimization of High-Speed PMASynRM Utilizing Different Magnet Combinations for EV Application
abstract: The trend towards electrifying transportation systems has stimulated research endeavors aimed at enhancing the development of low-cost, high-speed, high-efficiency and high-power density electric machines. As a result, the US Department of Energy (DOE) has set a target of achieving $7/kW and 12 kW/L for the electric drivetrain. This paper attempts to achieve the DOE targets by proposing high-speed Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Machine (PMASynRM) topologies enabled by low-cost non-Rare-Earth (RE) magnets blended with heavy RE-free magnets. At high speeds, the high mechanical stress developed in the rotor laminations poses a major challenge. To address this problem, design modifications are implemented in the rotor. Further, rotor design optimization is performed to minimize the RE magnet volume as well as magnet demagnetization and achieve the desired electromagnetic performance. Detailed analysis and comparison of the optimum rotor geometries based on various performance metrics is also presented.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of a Complete Reluctance Machine with no Initial Information on its Geometry
abstract: This paper addresses the topology optimization of an entire multiphase reluctance machine. Multiple materials are automatically and simultaneously distributed in the rotor and stator to maximize torque, minimizing the designer bias. As an extension of density-based techniques, this methodology relies on the multidimensional interpolation of the physical properties of the candidate materials. To handle a large number of design variables, projected gradient descent is used, and the sensitivities are computed efficiently using the adjoint variable method. A wide variety of optimized structures is obtained and discussed.

articleTitle: Evaluation of PCB End-Windings for Low-Voltage Stators of High-Speed Electrical Machines
abstract: The state-of-the-art slotted stator windings used in low-voltage, low-power, high-speed electrical machines are wound to a great extent with random round wires. Automating the assembling process is still challenging due to the small stator inner diameter and the difficulties associated with the pull-in technique. Almost all the stators are wound using the trickling method, where the pre-fabricated coils are dropped into the slots. This paper evaluates the suitability of rectangular wires (in the form of a hairpin structure) from a manufacturing standpoint, developing a proof of concept for a novel method. A novel way to connect the end-windings using multi-layer Printed Circuit Boards (PCB), thereby allowing a certain level of automation, is evaluated.

articleTitle: Comparison of Impedance Spectroscopy and Partial Discharge Analysis as Insulation Health Diagnosis Techniques
abstract: The ageing of insulation systems in electric machines can compromise partial discharge-free designs. Regularly monitoring insulation health is crucial to prevent unexpected failures. Several authors have proposed health markers from impedance spectroscopy and partial discharge analysis. Nevertheless, no comparative study has evaluated their sensitivity as health monitoring techniques for complete windings tested until failure. This paper compares both techniques for a thermally aged electric machine winding until failure, with impedance spectrum and partial discharge measurements taken every 24 hours. Markers from impedance spectroscopy (resonance frequency, impedance above/below resonance frequency, and capacitance) and partial discharge measurements (partial discharge inception voltage and charge) were compared considering: (1) deteriorated insulation identification, (2) sensitivity to changes in the insulation, and (3) near breakdown indication ability. While impedance spectroscopy markers varied with ageing, partial discharge analysis proved more meaningful. Regular monitoring of partial discharge inception voltage and charge can identify deteriorated insulation and prompt necessary maintenance.

articleTitle: Impact of Controller Bandwidths on Bearing Fault Diagnosis
abstract: The analysis of motor stator current has been documented in the literature as a reliable method for the detection of bearing faults. Nevertheless, the efficiency of this approach is diminished in the presence of closed-loop control. This paper examines the impact of closed-loop control, particularly field-oriented control, on the diagnosis of bearing faults in permanent magnet synchronous machines, using solely electrical and control structure signals. An experimental diagnostic test bench was designed for this purpose. First, the spectra of the measured stator current as well as the outputs of the speed and current controllers are calculated using the fast Fourier transform, and localized bearing fault features are extracted. Subsequently, the impact of varying speed and current controller bandwidths on the detectability of localized bearing faults is assessed. Consequently, the q-axis component of the current controller reference is proposed as a robust fault index.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Conventional and Amorphous AM-Built PMSM
abstract: The performance of additively manufactured electrical machines could see improvement through the utilization of iron-based amorphous materials. These materials exhibit a notable combination of high magnetic permeability and increased specific electrical resistance, albeit with a lower saturation flux density compared to conventional electrical steel. In this study, two identical permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) are compared, differing only in their soft-magnetic components (SMCs). While one PMSM incorporates electrical steel, the other utilizes bulk metallic glass (BMG) fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM). The BMG-based machine demonstrates a noteworthy reduction in torque output at equal current levels, yet it exhibits superior efficiency under certain operating conditions compared to its electrical steel counterpart. Moreover, the temperature of the BMG-based machine tends to be higher than that of the sheet-based machine.

articleTitle: Demagnetization Risk Mitigation for a Traction IPMSM Using Mixed-Magnet Configurations
abstract: The instability of prices, dominance of the market by monopolies, and limited availability of rare-earth (RE) permanent magnets have led North American companies to seek cheap reliable alternatives for electrical motors in traction applications. Consequently, the exploration of low-cost, high-performance RE-free magnets has emerged as a notable trend in current research. This paper explores the performance of RE magnets in electrical machine structure compared to lower-cost, RE-free magnets. Results reveal that while RE magnets such as neodymium iron boron (NdFeB) excel in back-EMF and torque RE-free magnets such as ferrites are more susceptible to demagnetization under extreme temperatures. To address this issue, the concept of substituting demagnetization-prone areas with stronger RE magnets such as NdFeB and samarium iron nitride (SmFeN) is presented in the paper. This strategy reduces RE material usage while upholding motor performance and mitigating demagnetization risk. Finite element analysis (FEA) demonstrates that mixed or hybrid magnet configurations strike a balance between minimizing RE content, sustaining acceptable output, and enhancing motor stability.

articleTitle: Improved Equivalent Model-Based Control PMLSG for Maximum Energy Harvesting in Irregular Waves for Direct-Driven Wave Energy Converters
abstract: In this paper, a control method for a permanent magnet linear synchronous generator (PMLSG) using an improved equivalent circuit model (IECM) is proposed for maximizing energy harvesting under irregular waves. Compared with the conventional equivalent circuit model, the IECM incorporates a new impedance to characterize the radiation impulse response and provides a method for controlling the PMLSG to conjugately match the external parameters in the hydrodynamic equation in real time under irregular waves. First, the hydrodynamic equations of DDWEC and the energy harvesting mathematical model of the PMLSG were analyzed. Then, the principle of maximizing energy harvesting using the IECM-controlled PMLSG under irregular waves and the calculation of IECM parameters are explained. Finally, it is verified that the harvested energy is maximized based on the superposition principle and through simulation. The results show that the proposed method enables the PMLSG to harvest the maximum energy from irregular waves over a long period of time.

articleTitle: Flux Density Waveform Reconstruction Method for Efficient Finite Element Analysis of Electric Motors
abstract: This paper proposes a procedure for optimizing the electromagnetic finite element analysis of synchronous electric motors. The methodology allows for the retrieval of the solution of the problem in an entire rotor rotation starting from simulations carried out within a reduced angle range, corresponding to the half of the electrical period divided by the number of phases of the motor winding. This is achieved by exploiting the geometrical periodicities of the motor and by dividing the static and rotating parts of the model in homologous sectors, which will undergo the exact same magnetic state, but with shifted waveforms with respect of the rotor angle. By properly rearranging the parts of the waveform taken from the different sectors, it is possible to reconstruct the full waveform in each part of the motor. A method to determine the waveform reconstruction sequence, i.e. the order in which the information should be taken from the different stator and rotor sectors, is defined as a function of the motor parameters. While a similar approach has been already presented in literature for specific motor designs and with the purpose of estimating iron losses, in this paper the methodology is generalized for motors with an arbitrary number of phases and is valid both for integer and fractional winding motors.

articleTitle: Modelling of Magnetization Processes of 3D-Printed Fe-Si Components by Means of an Artificial Neural Network Implemented in a FEM Scheme
abstract: In this paper the magnetization processes and power losses in an additively manufactured Fe-Si alloy with 3.7% wt. Si are studied. The material sample of interest is structured with air gaps to limit the dynamic losses by eddy currents. The magnetic behaviour of the material is modelled using an artificial neural network (ANN) trained on the experimental quasi-static hysteresis loops of the material, using a sample with the same geometry but a full section without gaps. The predictions are verified on a test set of experimental loops not involved in the training phase of the ANN. The ANN is later implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>to simulate in a finite element method (FEM) scheme the dynamic losses of the sample with air gaps and compared with the measurements to validate the results.

articleTitle: Ground Fault Detection Method for Doubly-Fed Induction Generators with Crowbar Circuits
abstract: Doubly-Fed Induction Machines (DFIM) are widely implemented in the wind energy electricity production due to their operation flexibility and the low cost of their excitation electronic power converter. To protect DFIM from ground faults, the neutral of the main power transformer and/or the DC midpoint of the converter DC bus are grounded. However, when wind turbines must dissipate large amounts of energy, crowbar devices are coupled to the DFIM rotor, disconnecting the excitation converter, and isolating the rotor from the rest of the circuit. This fact causes the lack of selectivity of the ground fault detectors. In this paper, a method to keep the selectivity of the ground fault detectors is proposed. The method allows to detect ground faults that happen in the crowbar or in the DFIM rotor once the crowbar is in operation. The detection is achieved by using a contactors system that switches between the DC midpoint of the converter and the AC neutral of the crowbar circuit depending on which circuit is governing the DFIM. In order to observe the operating behavior of the method, several simulations have been carried out in MATLABSimulink, obtaining promising results.

articleTitle: Design of a Cryogen-Free HTS Excitation Coil for a Homopolar Alternator
abstract: For the transition to future electric flight high-power-density superconducting machines may be an enabling technology. This also requires accurate thermal models to simulate superconductor cooling. A thermal model was designed for a cryogen-free, high-temperature superconducting coil in the temperature range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{20}\ldots \mathbf{30}\ \mathbf{K}$</tex>. The coil will be used to excite a high-speed homopolar inductor alternator. Data for heat transfer at low temperatures is presented, particularly for the thermal connections, which make up a large part of the temperature gradient along the heat-conducting cooled system, which does not need any cryogenic fluid (“cryogen-free”). Hence, particular attention is given to the conduction-cooled current leads, as they are responsible for the main heat inflow from outside. A novel approach to thermally connect the current leads to the cold head is presented.

articleTitle: Robustness of Grounded-Electrode Approach to Mitigate Bearing Currents in Electric Machines with Semi-Closed Slots
abstract: Electric motors are integral to diverse industrial applications, yet their reliability is hampered by bearing currents-a parasitic phenomenon causing excess wear and damage to the machine's bearings. This paper addresses the pressing issue in modern electric machines, particularly those powered by frequency converters, focusing on non-circulating bearing currents and the Grounded-Electrode Approach (GEA) as a countermeasure. While the approach is promising, a critical aspect remains unexplored-the influence of electrode misplacement, especially in machines with semi-closed slots. Extending previous research, this study numerically assesses the impact of misplacement on bearing currents reduction, crucial for practical implementation. The GEA involves inserting thin grounded wires into stator slot clearance, acting as electrostatic shields. This paper extends the investigation, numerically assessing the impact of grounded electrode's misplacement on bearing currents reduction, specifically addressing machines with semi-closed slots. Scenarios with different misplacements are examined, offering valuable insights for optimizing this mitigation strategy. Understanding the nuances of electrode positioning enhances the ongoing dialogue on reliable electric machine design, with a focus on the effective mitigation of bearing currents.

articleTitle: Multisensory Approach to Diagnose Bearing Faults Using Cohen Class Bilinear Distributions
abstract: Monitoring the bearings of induction motors is essential to avoid downtime and optimize maintenance schedules. Manufacturing processes are typically dynamic, requiring time-varying methods to diagnose faults. The Wigner-Ville distribution is renowned for generating high-resolution representations in both time and frequency. Unfortunately, cross-terms are the primary problem of this technique, impairing many monitoring methodologies. Therefore, this work compares several modified versions of the Wigner-Ville distribution, known as Cohen-class bilinear distributions, in a multisensory strategy to diagnose the severity of bearing wear. Then, the Shannon entropy of each Cohen-class bilinear distribution is tested as a fault indicator using the Bhattacharyya distance to evaluate the potential of separability between the classes. The results demonstrated that Born-Jordan and Zhao-Atlas-Marks stood out among the Cohen-class bilinear distributions, whereas the entropy of vibration promoted more effective diagnostics than audio.

articleTitle: A Review of Modeling and Control of Multi-Phase Induction Motors Under Machine Faults
abstract: Multi-phase induction machines have attracted significant research attention in recent years due to the notable advantages they have over their standard three-phase counterparts. Particularly, their ability to continue functioning in the event of machine failure without requiring inverter modification has sparked considerable interest. This paper presents an overview of the state-of-the-art developments in post-fault control strategies for multi-phase induction machines, as documented in the literature. The investigation delves into various modelling approaches for the configuration of multi-phase machines. Additionally, it explores post-fault control methodologies utilising field-oriented control (FOC) and model predictive control (MPC). Furthermore, Section IV discusses the comparison between carrier-based PWM and space vector PWM techniques. In conclusion, this paper identifies areas within the field that warrant further investigation.

Author Keywords: Post-fault control of multi-phase induction motor

articleTitle: Broken Rotor Bar Fault Detection Using Machine Learning: Optimal Frequency Resolution
abstract: This paper explores the optimal frequency resolution of the current spectra for detecting the broken rotor bar fault in induction motors with machine learning and motor current signature analysis. Conventional methods of broken rotor bar detection usually advocate for a higher frequency resolution in the motor current spectrum, which requires longer current signal measurements that are difficult and expensive to conduct. Thus, this work aims to identify the limitations to frequency resolution for successful broken rotor bar diagnosis when applying machine learning algorithms. The study also provides recommendations on the signal processing for feature extraction to enhance machine learning model performance. The machine learning algorithms used in the study are support vector machines, gradient boosting machines, and multilayer perceptron.

articleTitle: Synchronous Reluctance Rotor Geometry for High-Speed Applications
abstract: This paper addresses a design case for a high-speed synchronous reluctance motor. First, we describe a combined EM-mechanical optimization process, carried out on a classical synchronous reluctance rotor geometry, aimed at maximizing efficiency and power factor, while keeping torque ripple and mechanical stress under control. We then apply this process to two different geometry classes, namely round rotor and a rotor with notches on the outer surface to reduce centrifugal load. We show how each class can improve the above-mentioned targets, allowing higher speed or improved performance, or both. With respect to a more traditional optimization process accounting only for electromagnetics, the combined EM-mechanical optimization allows to choose an optimal result for which structural integrity against the centrifugal stress is already considered, thus reducing the number of design iterations necessary for mechanical verification. The proposed approach allowed reaching overall better combination of efficiency and power factor values, while fulfilling the desired limits for torque ripple and mechanical stress.

articleTitle: Influence of Current Harmonics on Electromagnetic Force and Vibration Noise of Electrical Machines
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of low switching frequency current harmonics on electromagnetic force, noise and vibration of electrical machines. An analytical model considering slotting and harmonic currents is firstly used to qualitative identify the feature of electromagnetic force harmonics generated by harmonic currents. Then delicately designed case studies utilizing multi-physics FE simulation quantitatively investigates the effects of the harmonic current with varying frequencies and amplitudes on electromagnetic force and noise in a baseline motor. The relationship among the harmonic current, electromagnetic force and vibration noise are investigated and established. The difference of the sound characteristics between electrical machines driven by low and high switching frequency inverters are revealed. Experimental tests validate the simulations and the conclusions are drawn based on the analysis.

articleTitle: Synchronous Reluctance Motors: Opportunities in the Era of New Materials, Additive Manufacturing, and Machine Learning
abstract: This study investigates the potential of synchronous reluctance motors (SynRMs) as alternatives to conventional electric motors, with a particular focus on leveraging additive manufacturing and novel materials. It explores recent advancements in utilizing additive manufacturing techniques and new materials for motor construction, aiming to enhance performance and efficiency. Additionally, the study examines the development of control systems using machine learning and artificial neural networks (ANNs) to replace traditional PID controllers, thereby improving precision in rotor position and speed estimation. Moreover, hardware solutions such as multiprocessor systems and System-on-Chip Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (SoC FPGAs) are explored to optimize real-time control capabilities. These advancements highlight the transformative potential of SynRMs, including variants like line-start SynRM (LSSynRM) and Permanent Magnet-assisted SynRM (PMaSynRM), as leading options for future motors, offering superior performance, efficiency, and sustainability across various applications.

articleTitle: Real-Time Rotor Temperature Estimation in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Using Incremental Deep Learning
abstract: Rotor temperature estimation is crucial in permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) because it directly affects the performance, efficiency, and overall reliability of the motor. Accurately estimating the temperature in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSMs) is challenging due to their dynamic operation. However, placing sensors directly on the rotor is difficult because of its dynamic nature and mechanical constraints, which can also add to the costs involved in temperature monitoring. In this respect, it becomes imperative to develop effective methodologies that can cope with these dynamical changes for real-time estimation of the rotor temperature. This work puts forward a learning method that combines deep learning (DL) models with a novel incremental learning technique to achieve precise rotor temperature estimation in PMSMs. To mitigate the issues associated with catastrophic forgetting in incremental learning, it is proposed to preserve prior data streams in a buffer and selectively and periodically select the most informative ones. This technique enables DL models to learn from past experiences while mitigating the risk of losing valuable knowledge during the continuous learning process. Application of this learning scheme to real datasets from an experimental test bed demonstrates performance enhancement compared to models trained offline.

articleTitle: Thermal Model Calibration of a Squirrel-Cage Induction Machine
abstract: Accurate and efficient thermal simulations of induction machines are indispensable for detecting thermal hot spots and hence avoiding potential material failure in an early design stage. A goal is the better utilization of the machines with reduced safety margins due to a better knowledge of the critical conditions. In this work, the parameters of a two-dimensional induction machine model are calibrated according to evidence from measurements, by solving an inverse field problem. The set of parameters comprise material parameters as well as parameters that model three-dimensional effects. This allows a consideration of physical effects without explicit knowledge of its quantities. First, the accuracy of the approach is studied using an academic example in combination with synthetic data. Afterwards, it is successfully applied to a realistic induction machine model.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Performance of Radial-Flux Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generators with Different Winding Designs for Applications in Wind Turbines
abstract: In this paper is analyzed the effect of winding type on the performance of three-phase radial-flux permanent magnet synchronous generators for applications in wind turbines. The winding types considered for designing these generators are the concentric, integer and distributed windings. Moreover, a generator virtual prototype is obtained from each winding in software CAD. Then, each virtual prototype is simulated through 2D and 3D finite element analysis of each winding type to test performance variables such as the copper mass, losses, the power quality and, cogging and ripple torques. Finally, the performance results for these generator designs are shown in a comparative table and also, the main winding features are described for the purpose of being used in wind turbines.

articleTitle: Design of High-Speed Linear Induction Motors - Part I: Electromagnetic Modelling
abstract: This paper presents an analytical methodology to ob-tain the magnetic field distribution and calculate the performance of single-sided linear induction machines (SLIMs). The method-ology uses a permeance function to estimate the magnetic field in the gap, Fourier analysis to calculate the travelling harmonics and transfer matrices to solve the diffusion equation in a multi-layer model of the rotor. Key performance parameters such as thrust, losses and efficiency are readily calculated using the proposed methodology. Furthermore, the proposed methodology can be generalized for double-sided LIMs (DLIMs) and for machines with multi-material reaction plates. The methodology is applied to a case study of a SLIM for high-speed transportation, presents results and provides an insight into the end effect, the reduction of thrust as the speed increases.

articleTitle: Control Techniques for Dual-Three-Phase SPM Drives Including Voltage Limitation Strategies
abstract: This study examines the management of the voltage limits in the control of dual-three-phase permanent magnet drives. The research is centered on two main control methods. The first method involves the design of independent controllers to manage individual three-phase modules. The second method utilizes all controllers to optimize the tracking of the six reference currents simultaneously. Both strategies aim to optimize the use of the available DC-link voltage in each three-phase inverter while taking into account the full hexagonal limitation of the voltage vectors. Different algorithms and the main governing equations are presented. Simulations in Matlab/Simulink, which reproduce the behavior a dual-three-phase permanent magnet motor, show the differences for the developed techniques in the distortion of the phase current.

articleTitle: A Review on Properties of 3D Printed Magnetic Cores for Electrical Machines: Additive Manufacturing Methods and Materials
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) is a new topic in the field of electrical machines (EMs), offering the potential to overcome the limitations in the design of EMs. Through AM, complex 3D geometries and the utilization of Fe-Si cores with 6.5% silicon can be achieved, leading to enhanced EM performance without concerns about manufacturing cost and complexity. This paper provides an overview of various AM methods and materials used in manufacturing soft magnetic cores for EMs, with a particular emphasis on the multi-physics properties of these cores. Due to the distinct fusion processes in each AM method, the microstructural properties of the printed cores vary, leading to diverse multi-physics properties that require detailed investigation. The paper outlines both the benefits and challenges associated with AM techniques and materials. Importantly, it explores the detailed characteristics of Fe-Si and Fe-Co cores manufactured through different AM methods, comparing them with commercial laminations such as 35A300, JNEX Super Core, and Hiperco 50A.

articleTitle: Loss Minimization Control of PMSM for Electrified Non-Road Mobile Machinery Using Flux and Loss Maps
abstract: Loss minimization control (LMC) for permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) improves the efficiency compared to the conventional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i_{\mathrm{d}}=0$</tex> and maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control algorithms. Implementation of LMC for electrified non-road mobile machinery (NRMM) such as wheel loaders, excavators etc. is challenging due to parameter sensitivity. To improve the control performance, LMC using a lookup table (LUT) approach is applied. Using flux and loss maps, a LUT of optimal operating currents is built which is then utilized in the machine control. Simulations are performed with typical duty cycles of a wheel loader in MATLAB/Simulink, and the results show that the proposed approach has comparable dynamic performance to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$i_{\mathrm{d}}=0$</tex> control and higher efficiency than MTPA control.

articleTitle: Investigating PWM Scheme Effects on Power Loss in a Hairpin-Wound Traction Drive Unit
abstract: This paper explores the impact of Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) schemes, specifically Sinusoidal PWM (SPWM), Space Vector PWM (SVPWM), and Discontinuous PWM (DPWM) on power losses in a hairpin-wound interior permanent magnet motors paired with a two-level voltage source inverter. Through a comprehensive simulation approach combining MotorCAD and Simscape, both inverter and motor losses under varying PWM strategies and switching frequencies are assessed. SVPWM offers the lowest total drive unit losses due to suppress the lower-order harmonics, while DPWM, despite reducing inverter switching losses, leads to higher motor losses due to increased current Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). The study also illustrates that higher switching frequencies, although beneficial in reducing motor losses by lowering THD, result in increased inverter losses, thus presenting a trade-off for overall system efficiency. These insights contribute to the optimization of PWM strategies in electric motor systems, highlighting the importance of integrated design considerations for enhancing Electric Vehicles (EVs) drivetrain performance.

articleTitle: Thermal Modelling Improvement Aspects for Automotive Physically-Integrated Drives
abstract: Physically-integrated drive machines are a current research hotspot due to their excellent characteristics. The inherent nature of such drives fosters a seamless integration between the electrical machine, the power electronics and control system. This results in compact drives with lower component-count, thus delivering market-ready products that are much cheaper and sustainable. Literature has shown that a critical part of designing an integrated drive is the handling of the thermal management of both the machine and power electronics. The objective of this study is to design and optimize a thermal management system which enhances performance and sustainability. This work is applied to a fully integrated drive motor for use in a Formula SAE race car.

articleTitle: Alternative Test System for High Specific Power PMSM Using Passive Rectification and Compensating Capacitors
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) are increasingly used in diverse applications demanding high power and compact size. This trend necessitates high-speed machines with high fundamental frequency, posing challenges for conventional switching semiconductors. While wide band-gap (WBG) semiconductors offer solutions, their cost and immaturity necessitate alternatives. This paper proposes an alternative test system for high specific power PMSMs employing a passive rectified setup with parallel-connected capacitors. This approach avoids the limitations of commercially available converters in terms of high switching frequency at high powers. Such converters are not yet widely available on the market, but exploring the machine's true potential can be done without a converter. The paper details the high specific power PMSM design, followed by an explanation of the passive rectification system and its integration with parallel capacitors. A finite element analysis (FEA) simulation model is then described, showcasing its role in evaluating the system's performance. Finally, the paper presents and discusses the obtained results, highlighting the effectiveness of this approach.

articleTitle: Assessing Thermal and Efficiency Aspects of Aluminum Hairpin Motors in Passenger Cars
abstract: Aluminum represents a more sustainable choice than copper in windings of electric machine intended for passenger cars, offering cost and weight advantages at the expenses of higher DC resistance and ensuing losses at low frequency operations, such as in peak condition. However, the overall power loss and efficiency should be evaluated throughout the whole driving cycle of a specific application. This study demonstrates that the overall efficiency of aluminum solutions remains comparable to copper, primarily due to the fact that the most significant contributors to total losses are iron losses at low load and medium speed operations typical of passenger cars. Additionally, this research proves that, despite experiencing higher losses at peak conditions, the maximum winding temperature of the aluminum solution remains within acceptable limits throughout the driving cycle when using the same cooling system as copper. To validate these findings, a comprehensive assessment of the thermal performances of copper and aluminum is conducted using 3D finite element thermal analyses across the entire driving cycle. The analysis adopts a one-way coupled Conjugate Heat Transfer (CHT) approach to accurately evaluate the thermal behavior of both materials under real-world operating conditions.

articleTitle: Parameter Estimation of Five-Phase Induction Motors from Unbalanced Steady-State Tests
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new method to estimate the electrical parameters of five-phase induction motors from steady-state tests executed with the rotor at a standstill. The method is based on the unbalanced steady-state model and the corresponding equivalent circuits, from which we estimate all parameters related to the fundamental and the third-harmonic airgap induction using only measurements of stator voltages and currents. Additionally, the method requires a separate measurement of the stator resistance. Further, we validated the proposed method through practical tests taken on a prototype induction machine of 4.5 kW; these tests demonstrate not only that the proposed method gives accurate and acceptable results but also illustrate some of the relevant advantages compared with similar methods.

Author Keywords: steady-state model of five-phase induction machines

articleTitle: Design of Integrated Radiator for Aviation Propulsion Motor Based on Structural Reuse
abstract: Aircraft electrification is currently one of the best alternatives to address the rising demand for air transportation and mitigate the drawbacks of conventional aircraft systems. In this paper, an oil radiator integrated with the motor housing is proposed to construct a self-circulating oil cooling system for aviation propulsion motors. External circumferential square fins featured with staggered Pin-Fin array and internal axial hollowed-out channels are designed to enhance the heat dissipation rate of the housing. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is used to validate the thermal performance of the proposed structure. Cooling performance comparison with the normal housing is conducted in further research. Finally, a simplified housing structure is manufactured using 3D printing technology to verify the numerical analyses. The experimental results shows that the surface average CHTC increased by 105.6% and the oil outlet temperature of the proposed structure can be reduced by 6.6°C compared to the planar structure at an air flow velocity of 15 m/s.

articleTitle: Assessing the Impact of Stator Yoke on the Electromechanical Energy Conversion Performance of Switched Reluctance Machines
abstract: Switched reluctance machines have a bad reputation for acoustic noise emission. For mitigating such an annoying issue, the motor designer can act on the stator core dimensions, with the purpose of increasing its stiffness. The latter can be positively affected by extending the thickness of the stator yoke. Nonetheless, this design modification can have a detrimental influence on important performance metrics, such as torque density, efficiency, torque ripple and thermal behavior. This paper investigates the above, verifying that increasing the thickness of stator yoke to a suitable level can bring considerable benefits in terms of stator stiffness, and ensuing vibration modes' natural frequencies, without however detrimentally affecting other key performance indicators. The presented analyses are based on simulations through custom-designed scripts and tools, suitably complemented by electromagnetic finite element simulations.

articleTitle: Induction Machine End-Winding Leakage Flux Monitoring Using FBG Magnetostrictive Composite Flux Sensor for Broken Rotor Bar Fault Detection
abstract: Whilst monitoring magnetic leakage flux has proven effective in detecting faults in induction machines its functionality and ultimately feasibility can depend on the choice of the applied magnetic flux sensing device. This study examines the application of a small size and power passive Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) magnetostrictive composite magnetic flux sensor for localized magnetic leakage flux monitoring in the end winding region of an induction machine. The magnetic flux sensor's design, functional and installation features are presented first. A prototype sensor is then fitted in the end-winding region of an experimental test-rig induction machine to observe the frequency spectra of its magnetic leakage flux during healthy operating conditions and those including broker rotor bar faults. The results show that the reported method enables practical monitoring of the stray magnetic flux's frequency spectrum including the recognition of spectral components that can indicate the presence of a broken rotor bar fault condition.

articleTitle: Towards Data-Driven Strand Transposition Simulation of Multistrand Random Windings
abstract: The randomness of the conductor lay in multi-stranded windings used in power-dense electrical machines can cause a wide variation in AC loss across a manufacturing batch. There has been continued focus on the development of strand transposition simulation methods in multistrand random windings to support the estimation of AC loss magnitude and variability. This paper aims to mitigate the limitation faced by such approaches concerning the lack of available verification data by generating a feasible strand transposition dataset. Through characterising the intra- and inter-turn strand mixing present in the simulated strand transpositions, it was observed that the strand mixing distance is Exponentially distributed and that the probability of strand mixing occurring is significantly higher than previously assumed. In order to focus future studies in this area, a simplified strand transposition simulation approach is assessed to highlight the characteristics of strand transpositions that must be represented in future simulation methodologies.

articleTitle: Switched Reluctance Machines in 800-V Powertrains - A Focus on Voltage Distribution and Electrical Stress
abstract: Electrical machines for transportation applications need to be reliable and guarantee an appropriately long lifetime. These machines are today exclusively fed through power electronics converters, whose specs in terms of switching frequencies and voltage rise-times tend to improve at a fast pace. This can lead to extra stresses on machines' insulation systems, particularly with the recent tendency to higher DC link voltages. Therefore, in order to properly design the insulation system of traction motors, it is necessary to identify and quantify the entity and magnitude of voltage stresses within various insulation sub-systems. A widely accepted methodology for estimating winding voltage distribution and magnitude is based on the adoption of high frequency lumped parameter models, based on the transmission lines theory. These are extensively investigated in existing literature for distributed-wound machines, either random or form / hairpin wound. However, there is a lack of investigations for what concerns concentrated wound machines, and in particular switched reluctance ones. This paper thus aims at modeling the high frequency voltage stresses within the winding of a use-case switched reluctance motor, proving that such a machine topology could represent a valid candidate for future high voltage powertrains, operating at 800 V and above.

articleTitle: Fault Detection of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors Employing DQ Current Features and Isolation Forest
abstract: Early and automated fault detection is necessary for proper condition monitoring and operation management of electric motor and drive systems. This paper investigates fault detection of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) using Motor Current Signature Analysis (MCSA), d-q Transform and Isolation Forest (iForest). This approach utilizes statistical indicators for feature extraction from dq-transformed current measurements and Isolation Forest, for outlier and fault detection. The proposed methodology is tested in a PMSM test bench under multiple operating conditions.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Electric Motor Designs: Traditional Steel Laminations vs. Soft Magnetic Composite Materials
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of electric machine designs for vehicle traction using traditional steel laminations versus soft magnetic composite (SMC) materials in four radial flux magnetic topologies: Rare-earth interior permanent magnet synchronous machine (IPM), wound field synchronous machine (WFSM), spoke-ferrite permanent magnet synchronous machine (SP-FER), and induction machine (IM). In total, 32 machine variants are evaluated considering different materials, and they are critically evaluated against a reference IPM traction machine with regards to performance, material cost and environmental impact. Results show that while the IPM design remains superior in performance for a fixed geometry, the WFSM and SP-FER offer significant environmental advantages. The WFSM emerges as the most eco-friendly option, while the SP-FER represents a balanced choice considering environmental impact, durability, production simplicity, and inverter complexity. This study highlights the potential of SMC materials compared to steel laminations in reducing costs (16 % to 29 %) and CO2-eq. emissions 21 % to 38 % in electric motor manufacturing without significantly compromising on performance, making it a viable alternative in automotive applications.

articleTitle: Drive Cycle Comparison of a PMSM and an EESM for a Traction Application Utilizing Modular Stator Manufacturing
abstract: This paper investigates the performances of a permanent magnet and an electrically excited synchronous machine, that have a common stator for a traction application. Due to their reduced cost, lack of rare earth permanent magnets and high performance capabilities, the electrically excited machines can be a viable alternative to their permanent magnet counterpart. It is also desirable to utilize the manufacturing processes for the production of both types of machines, especially if one already exists. The permanent magnet and the electrically excited machines are designed and dimensioned with a common stator size and an axial length, and the machine performances are computed. The machines are further analysed for commonly used automotive drive cycles, in order to assess their suitability for the traction application. The study shows that the electrically excited machine has a 16% lower torque density, due to the thermally limited rotor current, however unlike the permanent magnet machine, the efficiency of it increases for the higher speed operations, thanks to the decreasing rotor current in the field weakening region. The drive cycle analysis shows that the electrically excited machine performance is improved circa 8.7% for the high speed motorway operation compared to the WLTP, whereas this improvement for the permanent magnet machine is less prominent at 3.7%.

articleTitle: Topology Optimization of Coaxial Magnetic Gear based on Reluctance Network Analysis
abstract: Coaxial Magnetic Gear (CMG) can transmit torque between an input and an output shaft without mechanical contact. The pole pieces in the middle rotor play a role in flux modulation. The geometry of the pole pieces affects the torque transmission capabilities and is one of the most challenging and crucial aspects of CMG design. Benefiting from the development of topological optimization methods for designing magnetic devices, we investigate the optimal material distribution in the middle rotor of a CMG. The topology optimization aims to create a meaningful geometry with improved performance (increased volumetric torque density, reduced torque ripple). Finally, the optimized result suggests a curved shape along both side boundaries of pole pieces and small holes on the boundaries close to the inner rotor. The parameter and performance are evaluated by the Reluctance Network Analysis (RNA), which accounts for magnetic material nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Hysteresis Feedback Linearization Control for Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
abstract: This paper presents a novel control technique for interior permanent magnet synchronous motors, addressing their dynamic complexity and nonlinearity. The technique involves linearizing the nonlinear model of the motor using a feedback linearization method and designing an integral state feedback controller optimized through the linear quadratic regulator. The method applies control constraints using a reference reforming technique and adopts the maximum torque per ampere strategy for reference current creation. The performance of the control technique is validated through simulations at various operating points, considering the alterations in motor parameters due to the specific operating point. To evaluate the sensitivity of the control system to uncertainties, the finite element method is employed to provide a precise model for the studied motor.

articleTitle: Robust Design of Six-Phase Segmented Switch Reluctance Motor Considering Punching Effect
abstract: A crucial aspect in the design process of electrical machines for high-volume production involves accounting for the impact of manufacturing uncertainties, material variations, and manufacturing processes on machine performance. This is essential for achieving a well-balanced adjustment between Finite Element (FE) modeling outcomes and experimental results, thereby mitigating the risk of obsolescence during mass production. This paper introduces an optimized procedure tailored to address the influence of the punching process in robust design optimization for electrical machines. The presented model is applied to a six-phase Segmented Switch Reluctance Motor (SSRM). The model incorporates a multi-layer FE model to account for the effects of punching on the magnetic characteristics of Electrical Steel Lamination (ESL). Additionally, to enhance the accuracy of FE modeling, a geometry-dependent excitation and control circuit are integrated within the FE model. The results obtained demonstrate that the developed optimization model effectively reduces the risk of obsolescence in mass production.

articleTitle: Torque and Current Ripple Analysis in Integrated DC-DC Boost Chargers Based on SynRMs and WR-SMs
abstract: The automotive industry is increasing the voltage level of electric vehicles from 400 V to 800 V to reduce charging time without increasing the current levels. The vehicle wiring and the connectors that link the external DC fast charger to the internal battery impose limits on the maximum charging current for thermal, mechanical, and reliability reasons. Despite the presence of 800 V vehicles in the market, only a small portion of charging stations across Europe currently support this higher voltage level. Consequently, electric vehicles must be inherently compatible with 400 V DC charging stations, albeit with a slight increase in both the cost and weight of the powertrain components. The solution outlined in this study involves reconfiguring the electric motor and the three-phase inverter into a DC/DC boost converter to adapt the high-voltage battery to the voltage level of the off-board charger. During the charging process, several constraints should be considered from both the machine's and the off-board charger's point of view. These aspects include the generation of a zero-mean torque independent of the rotor position and minimizing the output current ripple of the off-board charger and the torque ripple. The analysis presented in the paper considers synchronous machines without permanent magnets, such as synchronous reluctance machines and wound-rotor synchronous machines.

articleTitle: A Single-Platform Analysis of Selected Cooling Variants of Electric Machines
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical study of alternative thermal management systems in application to electrical machines. A case study permanent magnet (PM) motor for propulsion has been selected as a platform for comparing an array of cooling methods. Starting from commonly used techniques like air- or -liquid cooling via the motor housing and finishing with less conventional concepts, with integrated or embedded winding cooling including alternative coolants, e.g., deionised water, oil, or liquid metal. The single motor platform offers a unique insight into the key performance measures when comparing the alternative thermal management systems. Here, the commonly used figures of merit like winding/conductor current density and electric loading is supplemented with thermal resistance between the heat source (winding) and reference heat sink (coolant). Such approach provides more insight into the heat transfer effects, which would otherwise be difficult to deduce. The initial theoretical finings suggests that the integrated or embedded motor (winding) cooling offers clear performance benefits, i.e., significantly improved heat removal path. However, this is not very clear when comparing the current density or electrical loading data. E.g., liquid cooled hollow conductors and liquid cooled housing offer here similar current density and electric loading ratings, but significantly higher winding to coolant thermal resistance is found for the latter cooling variant. This highlights the importance of more in-depth data analysis when comparing alternative thermal designs of electrical machines, where multitude of design and manufacturing factors need to be accounted for.

articleTitle: An Adapted Constrained Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization Under Uncertainties: Application on a Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor
abstract: This paper presents a robust Bayesian design optimization of a permanent magnet-assisted synchronous reluctance machine. This robust optimization takes into account the uncertainties related to the geometrical parameters of the machine as well as the uncertainties related to the characteristics of the magnetic materials. To do that, a new version of the Expected Feasible Improvement with Stepwise Uncertainty Reduction sampling (EFISUR) optimization algorithm has been implemented allowing to reduce the number of finite element simulations. The results have shown the effectiveness of the Bayesian optimization approach in enhancing machine performances while requiring minimal computational resources.

articleTitle: Optimizing Mid-Drive Electric Motor Performance and Cost for Electric Bike Applications
abstract: The widespread adoption of electric vehicles is influenced by factors including consumer preferences, cost reduction in battery technology, and environmental regulations. Within this context, electric micro-mobility emerges as a crucial sector, providing sustainable transportation options in urban settings central to the efficacy of such micro-mobility solutions lies the electric motor. This study focuses on designing and optimizing a 12-slot/10-pole flat magnet motor configuration for e-bikes, tailored to a unique driving cycle that captures dynamic load profiles, computed with a backward model from real-world scenarios, encompassing factors such as rolling resistance, aerodynamics, climbing, and acceleration. A multi-objective genetic algorithm optimization, integrated with MATLAB and Ansys Motor-CAD, is employed for comprehensive optimization considering constraints like permanent magnet demagnetization, torque ripple, mechanical stresses, and weight. Additionally, a multiphysics analysis validates the optimized design, highlighting its applicability beyond micro-mobility to other fields utilizing permanent-magnet synchronous motors.

articleTitle: Open-Phase Natural Fault-Tolerant Scheme Based on Deadbeat Predictive Current Control for Symmetrical Six-Phase Vernier PM Motor
abstract: Multiphase vernier permanent magnet motor (VPMM) has attracted more and more attention due to high torque density and fault-tolerant capability. However, most of the fault-tolerant schemes involve fault diagnosis and control reconfiguration, which increases the misdiagnosis risk and complexity of fault-tolerant systems. This paper proposes a natural fault-tolerant control based on deadbeat predictive current control (NFTC-DPCC) for the open-phase fault of a symmetrical six-phase VPMM. The key is to automatically switch into the fault-tolerant operation by a threshold judgment of reference voltage on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\textit{x-y}$</tex> subspace without fault diagnosis. By a performance simulation comparison with the traditional natural fault-tolerant control based on field-oriented control (NFTC-FOC) of a symmetrical six-phase VPMM with neutral point isolation or interconnection, it is verified that a better dynamic performance can be achieved due to adopting deadbeat predictive current control in the proposed NFTC-DPCC.

Author Keywords: symmetrical six-phase vernier permanent magnet motor (VPMM)

articleTitle: A Single-Phase Outer-Rotor Generator Featuring Permanent Magnets and Conductive Shield
abstract: Electric users such as houses and small businesses are usually supplied from the utility through a single-phase low-voltage feeder. Anyway, especially in developing countries the grid is often not much reliable: in such cases, autonomous generation systems are often sought as a temporary back-up. However, such systems shall be as simple, inexpensive and reliable as possible. This paper describes a 1-phase generator designed upon industrial request for such purpose featuring some peculiarities: outer rotor, direct output, no voltage regulator, permanent magnets excitation and a conductive shield able to mitigate by means of eddy currents the adverse effects of the reverse m.m.f. wave due to armature reaction. The proposed design is validated by means of finite elements electromagnetic simulations, proving to be a viable solution.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a 4–6 Brushless Doubly Fed Reluctance Generator
abstract: This paper provides an outline of the brushless doubly fed reluctance machine (BDFRM) design process, in-cluding the complex rotor selection and dual three-phase stator windings. The presented outline aims to streamline the calculation process for the D2L design coefficient, offering a more simplified approach. In this paper, insights regarding the rotor topology selection process, investigating optimal flux barrier layouts, electric loadings and airgap flux density, are presented. Also, an analytical design methodology for an 11 kW BDFRM in a D225M frame, followed by its optimization utilizing the NSGA-II (non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II), is given. The results show that the BDFRM achieves a very low torque ripple due to the use of a ducted hyperbolic-polyline flux barrier rotor.

articleTitle: Semi-Analytical Calculation of AC Copper Loss in Flat Wire Windings Considering PWM Harmonics
abstract: This paper proposes an AC copper loss calculation method for flat wire windings of pulse width modulation (PWM) driven permanent magnet (PM) synchronous motors. To quickly account for the effect of high frequency current harmonics on the magnetic field and losses, a semi-analytical eddy current loss calculation method is developed. This method combined the two-dimensional (2-D) quasi-static finite element method (FEM) with the frozen permeability method and the superposition theorem to rapidly calculate the slot leakage magnetic field caused by PWM. The time-harmonic field distribution is obtained from the quasistatic field results combined with the Maxwell's equations, and the losses in the flat wires are calculated using the Poynting theorem. The proposed method has been validated using FEM. The calculation method features a good tradeoff between computational speed and accuracy, making it suitable for calculating copper loss and optimizing motor efficiency.

articleTitle: A Review of Recent Topologies of Variable Flux Machines
abstract: Variable flux machines (VFMs) have been gaining a lot of research interest over the last few decades. This paper provides a review of recent different topologies in VFMs. A classification of the VFMs is introduced, considering the fact that the source of varying the magnetic flux in VFMs is either the permanent magnet (PM) or magnetizing coils (MC) or both. In each class, several topologies are explored and investigated in terms of their performance.

articleTitle: Qualitive Predictive Model of the Insulation Condition of HV Electrical Machines through a Combination of Diagnostic Techniques and NNs
abstract: Electrical Machines (EMs) hold significant importance in electricity generation and industrial applications. One of the most significant characteristics that an EM must have, is the reliability and as much as possible long lifetime. Insulation Resistance (IR), Polarization Index (PI) and Partial Discharges (PDs) Measurements are three of the most important diagnostic factors for the insulation system of EMs. This paper studies the aforementioned factors and their respective techniques combined with another two operational characteristics of an EM (years of operation and times of failures) and suggests a qualitive predictive model for the condition of their stator insulation with the use of Neural Networks (NNs). By leveraging NNs and evaluation metrics, it offers insights into the EM's insulation system state of health (Excellent, Good, Acceptable, Bad) and suggests appropriate actions for maintenance and further inspection. The model could be used for any electrical machine regardless of its power and voltage and it is capable to predict the insulation condition of the EMs with Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0812.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review of Restarting Strategies for Free Running Induction Motor Drives
abstract: Inverter-fed induction motor (1M) drive systems find extensive applications in various industries. However, in certain scenarios, these systems may encounter short-term power interruptions, necessitating a swift and seamless restarting of free running motors. This paper highlights the importance of fast and smooth restart strategies for free running motors in inverter-fed 1M drives. The need for efficient free running techniques becomes evident as such interruptions can lead to operational disruptions and production losses. The review explores the existing methods, their advantages, limitations, and potential areas for improvement, aiming to enhance the reliability and performance of inverter-fed 1M drive systems. The findings of this research contribute valuable insights to researchers, engineers, and practitioners seeking to optimize motor drive systems in the face of momentary power interruptions. The further research directions in the field of free-running restoration are also recommended.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization of Squirrel-Cage Induction Machine
abstract: In electrical engineering, a design of electrical machine using numerical methods, such as Finite element method, is a common practice. Electrical machines are complex multi-physical systems where for finding the optimal sets of designs solutions, called Pareto fronts, a very effective approach is to use multi-objective optimization. The most popular method for multi-objective optimization of machine design is the use of numerical optimization algorithms such as NSGA-II. However, due to the time-consuming nature of induction machines simulations, this approach is not very effective. This paper addresses this issue by proposing machine learning as a solution, specifically utilizing Multi-objective Bayesian optimization. This optimization method has been used in many industries as an efficient global optimization of the modeled system. By using the right acquisition function, the search space can be efficiently navigated to find the optimal candidates. Moreover, the optimization requires only a limited number of samples. The main aim of this paper is to present this method, which is demonstrated on the optimization of a 1.5 kW induction machine with time-consuming calculations. The machine optimization approach is not the main focus here, as this method can be effectively applied to any machine design or even any optimization approach. Furthermore, two possible approaches of machine optimization using this method are presented here.

articleTitle: Comparison of Field Winding Inter-Turn Short Circuit Fault Idendification Methods in a Salient Pole Hydro Generator
abstract: This paper presents the results of an investigation into the failure of a salient pole hydrogenator. The rotor poles are observed to have undergone significant overheating and several poles are likely to have suffered from resultant interturn short circuit. In order to identify the source of the fault, conventional voltage drop methods and recurrent surge oscillograph results are compared with a new approach proposed in this paper - injecting higher frequency currents (3rd harmonic and 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic). Analysis of fault identification methods demonstrates the difficulty of identifying the location of field winding faults, even when they are clearly present. The results demonstrate that the method proposed in this paper, injection of a 180Hz current in the field winding, offers superior ability to identify which poles may have faulted in a generator with a high number of salient poles.

articleTitle: Design of High Power Density IPM Machines with Fractional or Integral Slot for Off-Highway Vehicles
abstract: This paper deals with the design of high-power Interior Permanent Magnet (IPM) motors. Typical applications of this motor size and topology are: e-mobility, off highway vehicle, wind turbine and yachts. These motors are characterized by a wide constant power-to-speed ratio and high power density, high efficiency, making them a more interesting machine compared to more traditional induction motor. When it comes to IPM motors, different solutions are generally adopted in terms of slot-pole combination, i.e. fractional slot winding (concentrated or distributed) or integral slot (only distributed winding). The paper focuses on three different IPM motor configurations, an integral slot with 8 and two fractional slot with 10 poles and 14 poles, both analytical and experimental results are provided.

articleTitle: Comparison of Carbonised Foam to Other Testing Media for Insulation Verification of Hairpin Windings
abstract: Insulation testing is a vital part of electric motor manufacturing, because insulation failure can cause short circuits, overheating and premature motor failure. Traditional motors use thin round enamelled wire with multiple strands to form the coils, however a newer type of motor, the hairpin motor uses rectangular cross section conductors coated in enamel. This has the advantage of greater conductor area within a slot, partly due to the rectangular packaging offering greater packing density, and partly due to lower enamel area within the slot. However, the disadvantage of the hairpin motor design is that the wire must be formed to fit into the slot. Insulation can be deformed or broken as a result of this forming. Testing for insulation failures is usually performed by immersing the hairpin in conductive metal shot which can erode enamel, is hard to automate and has a limited contact area. This paper presents a comparison of alternative grounding media for hairpin insulation testing, including graphite powder, copper tape, carbonised foam and mild steel. Carbonised foam as a grounding medium is shown to facilitate a low cost, non abrasive, residue free, high speed method of testing insulation parameters.

articleTitle: Characterization of a Thermal FEA Model for Electrical Machines
abstract: This work proposes a methodology to characterize a thermal finite element analysis model. The aim is to obtain an efficient calculation model with a high spatial resolution at the same time. The method is based on the superposition principle, which is valid for linear thermal networks. The procedure is applied on a permanent magnet synchronous machine for an automotive use case. Validation with different test cases is presented for an error estimation between the characterized and the finite element analysis model. Finally, the model is used to derive the thermal behavior respectively the continuous performance of the machine.

articleTitle: A Dual SOGI-PLL Based Position Sensorless Control for Doubly Salient Electromagnetic Generator System with Active Rectifier
abstract: Compared with the traditional doubly salient electromagnetic generator system with the diode rectifier, the active rectifier can significantly improve the output power of DSEG, but the position sensor is necessary to obtain rotor position. This paper presents a new position sensorless control method for the doubly salient electromagnetic generator system with active rectifier. First, a flux observer based on the equivalent integrator and equivalent self-inductance is used to estimate the line-to-line excitation flux. Due to the asymmetric magnetic circuit structure, the flux is highly non sinusoidal. Then, two second-order generalized integrators are used to extract the fundamental component of the observed flux. Meanwhile, the phase-locked loop is used to estimate the rotor real-time position and speed. The proposed method enhances the harmonic suppression capability and improves the accuracy of the position estimation. Finally, the performance of the method is demonstrated by means of simulations and experiments implemented on an 18/12 pole DSEG prototype.

articleTitle: Investigation of Discrepancies Between Induction Motor Test Results and Design Simulation
abstract: This work investigates discrepancies in parameters and performance between an induction machine design simulation and the produced unit. The squirrel cage motor is explored analytically and in finite element space based on the complete design blueprints and material properties. The built motor is subjected to the DC, no-load, locked-rotor, and load tests. The simulated model is created parametric, according to the manufacturing process and tolerances. Solution space search results indicate that performance and parameters can deviate with minor structural changes. Reliable simulation prior to production can greatly reduce production time and cost, while improving performance and allowing for optimization. The resulting approach will be used as a basis for a manufacturing digital twin in further collaboration.

articleTitle: Modeling Voltage Distribution Along the Hairpin Windings of an Electrical Machine Using Impedance Fitting
abstract: A conductor-based model has been developed to address the high-frequency modeling of electrical machines with hairpin windings. The primary challenge in this modeling lies in accounting for the frequency-dependent mutual impedance between conductors within the same slot. Model parameters are determined by fitting the impedance spectra across a wide frequency range of up several Mega-Hertz. The high-frequency model is validated in the frequency domain, demonstrating effective common mode impedance modeling with an averaged relative error of 0.7 % along the stator winding. Additionally, time domain validation is performed based on measurements from the test bench, revealing a relative error of less than 1.9 % in the conductor-to-housing voltage signals along stator windings. In terms of differential mode voltages, the most representative one between two adjacent welding points in the end wind areas closely matches the measured signals in their voltage peak values.

articleTitle: Impact of Electric and Magnetic Loading on the Electromagnetic Stress of PM Machines
abstract: The air-gap flux density distribution generates electromagnetic stress which acts on the machine bore. The variation in magnetic or electric loading alters the electromagnetic stress pattern in the air-gap. The air-gap magnetic field varies with the level of magnetic flux contribution from armature excitation and permanent magnets. The proportion of contribution from either sources of magnetic flux depends on machine configuration. In this paper, the impact of design configurations, magnetic and electric loading on the distortion of air-gap flux density distribution are analysed. The change in electromagnetic stress, acting on the stator bore, due to the air-gap flux density distribution is investigated. The level of distortion in the magnetic flux density distribution, due to permanent magnet and armature excitation and its subsequent effect on the electromagnetic stress distribution are analysed using finite element methods. The effect of change in machine configuration on the flux from armature excitation is investigated. The spatial components of stress, its temporal frequency of oscillation and effect on structural vibration are studied using modal and harmonic analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of AC Winding Resistance considering different Conductor Materials in Transverse Flux Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
abstract: In various applications of the drive technology is a demand for a high gravimetric torque density. An aluminum containing conductor with a lower density compared to copper improves this specific property. For Transverse Flux Machines, the influence on other parameters are barely investigated. Within this work, a comparison of conductor material with focus on AC resistance is performed. A machine is presented and the impact on performance values with relation to DC resistance is described. The modeling of the AC conductive loss is presented using a hybrid multi-static and a transient FEA approach. Further, the AC resistance in dependence on the operating point defined by electrical frequency and current density is investigated. The AC resistance of copper material increases by 17.00 % in an exemplary operating point with maximum speed, whereas the aluminum conductor's by 6.34 %. Thus, the advantage of lower resistance of copper diminishes with increasing electrical frequency. Therefore, an aluminum containing conductor results in a significant advantage in the gravimetric torque density of the machine, accepting a slight reduction in efficiency. In future work, a specially designed machine optimally utilizing this conductor material may lead to a superior performance.

articleTitle: Revised Correction Factors in the Specht's Model for Calculation of the Transformer Inrush Current
abstract: In this study, correction factors are introduced for Specht's analytical model, which is used to estimate the inrush current peaks of transformers and their decay rates. The factors are derived for a set of five transformers using a least squares approach to minimize the discrepancies between the inrush current values from the Specht's model and the transient 2D finite element (FE) simulations. The 2D FE model uses an equivalent permeability of air and copper to mimic the flux linkage vs. current characteristics of the 3D FE model and effectively accounts for the effects of air core inductance at extreme saturation. The study considers the winding connections YNyn and YNd under the assumption that the connection to the grid is made on both the high voltage and the low voltage side.

articleTitle: Discretization Study for 2D Axisymmetric Modeling of an Ultrafast Thomson Coil Actuator
abstract: DC circuit breakers (DC CBs ) play a crucial role in ensuring the safe and reliable operation of envisioned medium voltage and high voltage DC power grids. Existing AC circuit breaker technologies are not suitable for application in DC grids due to the lack of current zero-crossings. Additionally, the fault current interruption time is required to be at least an order of magnitude shorter compared to conventional AC circuit breakers. For DC grid applications, hybrid DCCBs are being developed, combining power electronic devices and an ultrafast mechanical switch actuated by a Thomson coil (TC) actuator. The design and optimization of these TC actuators requires accurate and efficient simulation models. In this study, a 2D axisymmetric multiphysics simulation model of a state-of-the-art TC actuator is presented. A numerical discretization study is performed regarding the meshing and time stepping of the simulation. The results indicate a computationally efficient discretization that maintains the required accuracy under the given boundary conditions.
